papers.abstract: Randomized quantum algorithms for the estimation of expectation values of molecular observables offer a promising route to early fault-tolerant quantum advantage by trading circuit depth for an increased number of samples. However, this begs the question whether the resulting measurement overhead remains feasible for industrially relevant molecular systems. In this work, we benchmark the randomized sampling algorithm of Wang et al. [1] through numerical simulations on a hydrogen molecule and resource estimates for various active spaces of the cytochrome P450, an industry-relevant system in the pharmaceutical industry. Our numerical simulations reveal that the analytical error bounds significantly overestimate the actual sampling error, whereas the analytical bound on the required imaginary evolution time is comparatively tight, exceeding a direct DMRG estimate by roughly 44% for the active space where the comparison is feasible. The measurement overhead nevertheless remains prohibitively high: even for the smallest active spaces, the expectation-value estimation alone requires around 1010 samples, scaling to beyond 1015 for the largest active spaces considered. These results suggest that substantial improvements in measurement strategies or algorithmic scaling are necessary before randomized early-fault-tolerant algorithms become competitive for industrial quantum chemistry applications.

papers.title: Fingering instability of thin films with an inclined contact line
papers.abstract: The fingering instability of thin-film flow is a significant obstacle to producing uniform and stable films in industrial processes. In the framework of lubrication theory, we investigate the linear stability of a gravity-driven thin film with an inclined contact line using numerical and asymptotic methods. The contact-line singularity is regularized by imposing the Greenspan slip model. As demonstrated by the results, although the contact-line inclination slightly enhances long-wavelength instability, it significantly suppresses the growth of spanwise finite-wavelength perturbations. Moreover, the most unstable wavenumber shifts toward the long-wave region as the inclination angle increases. The inclination of the contact line introduces complex eigenvalues, leading to traveling-wave modes, in contrast to the standing-wave modes observed for horizontal contact lines. We also performed asymptotic analysis in the limit of small wavenumbers, confirming the enhanced long-wave instability. The physical mechanisms underlying these stability characteristics are elucidated, revealing that the effects of contact-line inclination come from the eigenmode distortion and additional streamwise flux.

papers.title: Large deviation principles for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations on unbounded channel-like domains
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the large deviation principle for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations driven by multiplicative noise and defined on an unbounded channel-like domain. We first prove the existence and uniqueness of probabilistically strong solutions for the stochastic equation under small noise perturbations by means of the local monotonicity method. Subsequently, we show the well-posedness of solutions to the corresponding control equation and the convergence in distribution of the solutions for the stochastic equation as the noise intensity tends to zero. Finally, we establish the Freidlin-Wentzell type large deviation principle for the solutions of the stochastic equation by using the weak convergence method. To overcome the lack of compactness of Sobolev embedding on unbounded domains, we employ a scalar stream function together with a truncation technique to derive uniform tail estimates for the solutions of the control equation.

papers.title: Behavior-Conditioned Animal Vocalization Generation: Event-Aware Modeling and Multidimensional Evaluation
papers.abstract: Behavior-conditioned animal vocalization generation aims to synthesize vocalizations from natural-language descriptions of animal behaviors, social interactions, and contexts. This task remains largely unexplored, with limited behavioral text supervision and substantial variation in vocalization duration. We construct the Behavior-Vocalization Dataset (BeVo) by integrating public bioacoustic data from six species with natural-language behavioral conditions derived from species-specific ethological and bioacoustic literature, totaling 31,191 events. We then adapt a rectified-flow-based generator with Event-Aware variable-length modeling, which encodes vocalizations at their actual durations and uses masks to prevent attention to padded latent positions and exclude these positions from the training loss. We evaluate vocalization discriminability, acoustic distribution fidelity, and language-aligned representation fidelity. Experiments show that task-specific adaptation improves all evaluated metrics compared with its zero-shot baseline, while Event-Aware modeling further increases vocalization-anchor macro accuracy from 59.86% to 61.99% and reduces Frechet Audio Distance from 1.40 to 1.22. Conditioning analyses further show that behavioral conditions improve target-anchor discriminability, while swapping behavior shifts generations toward the corresponding vocalization anchors. Demos are available on our project page.

papers.title: Throwing4: Phase-Aware Pose Modeling for Throw-Distance Prediction in Elite Athletics
papers.abstract: Elite athletics throwing provides a structured biomechanical action sequence together with an objective continuous outcome, namely throw distance, making it a suitable setting for performance-oriented sports analytics. In this work, we investigate whether explicit phase alignment of pose dynamics improves throw-distance prediction under realistic broadcast conditions. To support this study, we curate Throwing4, a dataset of 500 elite throwing clips spanning javelin, discus, hammer, and shot put, with corresponding two-dimensional pose sequences, frame-level phase annotations, and official distance labels. We formulate throw-distance prediction from broadcast-derived pose as a regression problem and compare full-sequence modeling against a phase-conditioned approach that partitions each attempt into four technique stages and fuses phase-specific motion representations. Experiments across multiple graph-based pose encoders show a consistent reduction in prediction error when phase structure is incorporated, indicating that phase-aligned modeling provides a more stable representation than treating the entire motion as an unstructured sequence. These findings suggest that explicit biomechanical phase information is a useful inductive prior for pose-based performance modeling in elite athletics throwing. Beyond score prediction, the dataset and protocol provide a basis for future work on fine-grained technique analysis, interpretable sports analytics, and robust modeling from broadcast video.

papers.title: Risk-aware Road-network Trajectory Synthesis under Local Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: Road-network trajectory synthesis under local differential privacy (LDP) enables mobility data analysis without uploading raw trajectories to an untrusted server. Existing locally private trajectory synthesis methods mainly model whole trajectories, point sequences, or grid-level mobility patterns. However, they cannot handle non-uniform privacy risks caused by local road-network and trajectory contexts, such as endpoints, long-stay-associated regions, and low-out-degree branches. They also do not directly protect conditional next-hop choices on road networks, where a user's selected successor may reveal sensitive local movement intentions. To address these challenges, we propose TrajRACE, a locally private synthesis framework for road-network trajectories. TrajRACE uses start, segment-count, and transition reports to represent trajectories. For each transition, it keeps the current road segment as a public aggregation context and perturbs the true successor among legal successors on the client side. It then assigns risk-aware protection strengths to transitions according to local road-network and trajectory contexts. Finally, the server recovers population-level start, segment-count, and conditional transition statistics from heterogeneous privatized reports, and generates synthetic trajectories that follow the public road-network topology. Experiments on three road-network trajectory datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of TrajRACE in improving synthetic-data utility across distributional, query-based, and pattern-level metrics, while providing stronger protection for high-risk local transitions.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium framework for first-order phase transitions
papers.abstract: The first-order phase transition is central to electroweak baryogenesis and gravitational wave generation, yet thermal equilibrium effective potential analyses cannot describe the real-time non-equilibrium dynamics of the phase transition process. We use the Schwinger-Keldysh closed-time-path formalism of real-time finite-temperature field theory to study these effects. For the $φ^6$ model, we derive the effective action and the corresponding Langevin equation. We further extend the formalism to the two scalar fields case, obtaining the coupled Langevin equations. These results provide a theoretical framework for the bubble nucleation simulation of the non-equilibrium phase transition process, laying the foundation for reliable predictions of baryogenesis and gravitational wave signals.

papers.title: Persistence diagrams of finite topological spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply persistent homology to study finite topological spaces by associating persistence diagrams with their elements through the furtherness function. This approach enables us to classify elements according to their topological evolution within the space. We further establish a bottleneck stability theorem showing that the bottleneck distance between the persistence diagrams associated with two elements is bounded above by their mutual furtherness.

papers.title: SP-Allreduce: Symmetric Tree Schedules for Tori and Beyond
papers.abstract: Allreduce is a fundamental communication primitive in large-scale distributed training, and torus interconnects remain widely deployed in high-performance systems. We introduce SP-allreduce, a new allreduce algorithm for $d$-dimensional tori that exploits the symmetry of the topology and routes only along shortest paths. We call an allreduce algorithm \emph{fully bandwidth-optimal} if it incurs no bandwidth overhead, no multihop-induced traffic inflation, and achieves perfect per-round load balance. SP-allreduce is based on a family of carefully symmetrized shortest-path trees that guarantees full bandwidth optimality in the $α$--$β$ model. We prove that it uses the minimum possible number of rounds among all fully bandwidth-optimal allreduce algorithms on $d$-dimensional tori, and therefore the minimum running time in this class. In this sense, SP-allreduce refines Bucket allreduce: it preserves Bucket's key strengths while reducing the number of rounds by a factor of two. We further extend our approach to broader symmetric topologies and to communication trees of prescribed depths. Experimentally, the resulting algorithms improve over the best compared state-of-the-art algorithms for tori by up to $1.19\times$ on square tori and $1.65\times$ on rectangular tori across the tested configurations. On HyperX and spine-leaf networks, we demonstrate gains of up to $14.82\times$ and $1.72\times$, respectively, over the best evaluated baselines.

papers.title: $\mathcal{D}$-Pullback Measure Attractors of McKean-Vlasov Stochastic Lattice Wave Equations
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the pullback measure attractor for a non-autonomous distribution-dependent stochastic lattice wave equation with nonlinear noise on $\mathbb{Z}$. We establish well-posedness in the energy space $\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2}$ and show that the solution generates a continuous non-autonomous dynamical system on $\mathcal{P}_{4}(\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2})$, which possesses a unique pullback measure attractor $\mathcal{A}$. Furthermore, we prove the convergence of the attractor $\mathcal{A}^{\varepsilon}$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^{+}$ to the attractor of the corresponding distribution-independent limit system.

papers.title: Entanglement and parametric resonance in coupled oscillator systems
papers.abstract: We study a system of two quadratically-coupled harmonic oscillators, prepared respectively in the ground state and in a coherent state. This toy model can describe for instance the dynamics of one mode of a quantum field evolving in a harmonically-oscillating classical background. In such situations, it is well-known that, depending on the background oscillation amplitude and coupling strength, the system may exhibit parametric resonance. Using the Feynman-Vernon influence functional, we analyze the interplay between parametric resonance and quantum entanglement by perturbatively computing the purity of the mixed state resulting from tracing over one of the oscillators. We find a runaway behavior of the quantum entanglement between the two oscillators, as well as a rapid breakdown of the validity of perturbation theory, in regions of parametric instability. This provides a quantitative confirmation of various statements in the literature and is highly relevant to questions pertaining to the validity of the semiclassical approximation in coupled quantum-classical systems.

papers.title: QBFF: Deep Quantum Bottleneck for Automatic Speaker Verification Anti-Spoofing
papers.abstract: A central goal of quantum machine learning is to identify applications in which small quantum circuits can improve task performance while remaining executable on real hardware. We investigate deepfake (synthetic) speech detection, a largely unexplored application in this area, where reliable confidence scores are as important as discrimination performance because deployment decisions are made at fixed thresholds and overconfident errors can be costly. We introduce QBFF, which routes a compressed speech representation through a small 8-qubit variational circuit (VQC) used as a drop-in bottleneck, with a matched classical bottleneck as the control. The quantum circuit yields better-calibrated confidence in most matched comparisons, including out-of-distribution evaluation, though the downstream deployment-cost benefit is model-dependent. We then run the same circuit on a real IBM quantum processor. To our knowledge, this is the first anti-spoofing pipeline to run on a QPU; hardware execution demonstrates feasibility, with lower subset EER and $C_{llr}$ but higher mean actDCF than the matched classical reference. Together, these results show that hardware-executable quantum bottlenecks can improve score reliability, with gains that vary by evaluation setting.

papers.title: RetroPlanner: Multi-Route Expansion and Multi-Objective Reasoning for LLM-Based Retrosynthesis Planning
papers.abstract: Multi-step retrosynthesis planning is often considered solved once a route to purchasable starting materials is found, but such a route should also be practical in real-world chemistry. Recent LLM-based planners formulate this process as sequential decision-making over an AND-OR graph, yet typically expand a single molecule per turn and are optimized for solvability alone, leaving alternative routes uncompared across the multiple objectives that determine practicality before the search budget is committed. We introduce RetroPlanner, an LLM-based planner that jointly compares multiple routes to steer the search toward higher synthesizability, as measured by reaction plausibility, round-trip consistency, and starting-material price. RetroPlanner is trained to reason over chemical evidence: structural progress from the target molecule, bond changes and reaction classes, where candidate routes diverge from one another, and how they rank across multiple objectives. Experiments on multi-step retrosynthesis benchmarks demonstrate that RetroPlanner recovers more alternative routes than prior LLM-based planners while improving synthetic route quality and maintaining a high success rate.

papers.title: Ramsey Meets Simultaneous Planarity: Vertex Integrity and Pathwidth
papers.abstract: We study the following simultaneous embedding problem: Given k graphs on the same vertex set with the same pairwise intersection, do they admit planar drawings that coincide on their shared graph? We establish fixed-parameter tractability with respect to the vertex integrity of the union graph (that is, the union of the input graphs) plus k, resolving an open question and generalizing the known algorithm parameterized by vertex cover number plus k. Our main technical contribution on the way towards this result is the extension of the recently introduced Ramsey pruning technique beyond ordering problems. Finally, we complement our tractability result with a lower bound that establishes NP-hardness when both k and the pathwidth of the union graph are bounded by constants, ruling out a generalization of our main result to path- or treewidth.

papers.title: Almost invariant subspaces in the topologically non-trivial setting: a pedestrian approach
papers.abstract: We present a self-contained, algorithmic construction of almost invariant subspaces [Panati et al. (2003), De Nittis and Panati (2010), Freund and Teufel (2016)] for Hofstadter-like Hamiltonians $H_b $ acting on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^2,\mathbb{C}^n)$. More precisely, for rational values of $b_0/(2π)$ we describe an iterative procedure that takes a ``locally gapped" projection $P_{0}$ (possibly topologically non-trivial) which commutes with $H_{b_0}$, into a projection $P_{\varepsilon}$ that commutes with $H_{b_0+\varepsilon}$ up to an error of order $\varepsilon^\infty$. Our construction insures that the Chern number of $P_{\varepsilon}$ equals the Chern number of $P_0$ as long as $P_\varepsilon$ exists. Moreover, its integrated density of states varies linearly with $\varepsilon$ (the ``Středa formula"). We also show that any spatially localized Parseval frame of $P_{0}$ can be mapped into to a localized Parseval frame of $P_{\varepsilon}$. We choose to work with a discrete model in order to keep the technicalities to a minimum level, with no need for advanced pseudo-differential calculus. Nevertheless, we are confident that most of our results can be extended to (unbounded) magnetic (pseudo)differential operators, but the technical burden would be much heavier. This is left for future work.

papers.title: Dynamical generalizations of the two-point Chowla conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the values of the Liouville function become asymptotically uncorrelated at consecutive natural numbers. Recently, the two-point case is resolved by OpenAI. In 2026, Charamaras and Richter conjectured a generalization of the Chowla conjecture to the asymptotic independence of the consecutive prime Omega functions. In this article, we prove the two-point case of their conjecture. As a consequence, we obtain a dynamical generalization of the two-point Chowla conjecture.

papers.title: Space AI Infrastructure: Where the Edge Meets the Orbital Cloud
papers.abstract: The fusion of artificial intelligence (AI) and space technologies is extending spaceborne intelligence beyond onboard payloads toward a global infrastructure, here termed Space AI infrastructure (SpaceAI-Infra). Its promise rests on two distinctive advantages of space systems: abundant solar energy in orbit and the global reach of satellite constellations. Realizing this promise hinges on a fundamental systems question: How should satellite constellations be designed and orchestrated to deliver data-center-scale AI services competitive with their terrestrial counterparts? This article develops a roadmap-oriented answer. We first chart the evolution of SpaceAI-Infra through three progressive stages: onboard AI, Space Edge AI, and Space Cloud AI. By revisiting the space-constrained fundamentals for end-to-end token services, we derive enabling design principles and translate them into an integrated space edge--cloud architecture. The communication-centric space edge comprises free-flying LEO constellations that provide user-proximate computing and form the access and backhaul fabric for cloud AI services. Complementing the edge, the computing-centric space cloud comprises formation-flying satellite constellations organized as space data centers in dawn--dusk sun-synchronous orbits. A case study demonstrates that the proposed architecture can support data-center-scale foundation-model inference for millions of concurrent users worldwide.

papers.title: Sampling from Neural Operator Priors to Solve Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Guided sampling with sparse observations and PDE residuals has recently been combined with neural operator priors to solve partial differential equations in function space, their natural setting. We pair such a prior with pseudo-bootstrap sequential Monte Carlo (pBS SMC), a guided sampling framework that accommodates proposals without tractable densities, and introduce a new proposal by adapting the DPM++ algorithm to the guidance setting. Across five benchmark PDE systems this proposal attains the best error--time trade-off at every step count tested, and wrapping it in pBS gives the lowest error on most inverse-problem settings, with the largest gains when few sampling steps are used.

papers.title: Recursive Environment Scaling for General Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: We study environment scaling as a way to increase agent-benchmark difficulty while holding core task objectives fixed. Our framework, Recursive Environment Scaling (RES), transforms existing benchmark environments while preserving their objectives and completion requirements. A proposer changes information access, resource relations, and execution dependencies; execution-grounded checks validate the resulting candidate, and accepted changes are inherited across rounds. This produces related environments for paired evaluation and training-trajectory collection. Experiments on 294 initial tasks from three benchmarks show lower task success for all six evaluation models, with decreases of 57.14--77.14 percentage points on Claw-Eval-Live. With equal trajectory counts and identical optimization settings, fine-tuning on RES trajectories outperforms original-trajectory SFT in all nine model--benchmark comparisons by 7.00--14.61 percentage points. Ablations identify recursive inheritance and dependency composition as important contributors to increased difficulty. Together, these results support environment scaling for both agent evaluation and training.

papers.title: LABIT: Long-Horizon Robotic Assembly Benchmark for Industrial Tasks
papers.abstract: Robot learning has undergone significant advancements in the domain of compliant control and robotic assembly. The development of novel methodologies has transcended the capacity to address discrete tasks, such as grasping or inserting, and has evolved to encompass the comprehensive construction of entire assemblies. Conventional benchmarks, which are predominantly focused on single tasks, are no longer adequate to address the complexity and interconnected nature of modern manufacturing processes. Consequently, the necessity for benchmarks to encompass a broader spectrum of assembly and subassembly steps is becoming apparent. In light of these developments, we propose LABIT, an industrial robotic assembly benchmark for long-horizon manipulation. This benchmark encompasses DIN-norm assembly tasks, including screwing, placing, inserting, and snapping, under both high and low tolerance conditions. The successive nature of these assembly steps implies that prior errors can influence subsequent manipulation. Consequently, this benchmark is particularly relevant for assessing the robustness of intelligent robotic systems. The proposed benchmarking protocols and novel performance metric, based on a taxonomy of assembly complexity in conjunction with the comprehensive list of parts and their corresponding CAD models, serve as essential tools for research and development in the field. To provide a baseline, we evaluate the benchmark using traditional force-position control and report reliability and score metrics per primitive, subtask, assembly category, and subassembly. Accompanying data is available at https://irp-hka.github.io/robotic-assembly-benchmark/.

papers.title: Boundedness and exponential stabilization in a degenerate migration-consumption system with logistic damping
papers.abstract: We study the no-flux problem for a taxis-type migration-consumption system with logistic damping in a bounded planar domain, where the motility function \(φ\) vanishes at zero and degenerates algebraically of order \(α\ge1\). We prove uniform boundedness in \(L^\infty(Ω)\times W^{1,\infty}(Ω)\) for every fixed damping coefficient \(b>0\), without any smallness assumption on the initial data, thus improving the previous \(L^2\)-boundedness results. For \(α>1\), we further prove that the solution converges exponentially to the spatially homogeneous state \((a/b,0)\), with an explicit admissible rate. The proof combines a weighted Gagliardo--Nirenberg type inequality adapted to the degeneracy with the dissipative structure of the signal equation. Therefore logistic damping drives the system toward homogeneity, despite the loss of uniform elliptic regularization.

papers.title: Towards modelling abreast to in-file transitions in small pedestrian groups
papers.abstract: Pedestrians in a crowd largely walk in small groups, dyads above all, and modelling how these groups arrange themselves is a step towards realistic models of the crowd as a whole. A dyad walks side by side in a dilute crowd and one behind the other in a dense one, an abreast to in-file transition recently measured in real life across the full range of naturally occurring crowd conditions (van der Laan and Corbetta, PLOS ONE 2026). The cost-function models of dyad formation by Zanlungo and coworkers (Phys. Rev. E 2014; EPL 2015) hold the pair abreast and have no in-file minimum at any finite density. Building on them, we propose and analyse a qualitative model in which the transition appears as an effective density parameter grows: the two formations become minima that coexist over a window of densities and exchange stability within it. We quantify this transition by computing the Orientation Log-Odds $Π_\text{OLO}$ as predicted by the model. This paper is a first step towards quantitative models of dyads and of their formation transitions.

papers.title: Magic-Free Certification of Logical Error Rates in Universal Fault-Tolerant Circuits
papers.abstract: As quantum hardware enters the fault-tolerant regime, algorithms are beginning to be executed on encoded qubits, yet scalable certification of how well they run remains an open problem. Here we introduce magic-free certification, a certification protocol for universal fault-tolerant circuits that consumes no magic, the resource that generally places them beyond efficient classical simulation and is by far the most expensive element of a fault-tolerant computation. The protocol is code- and decoder-agnostic, runs interleaved with the target circuit on the same device, and has a sample complexity that grows linearly with the number of logical qubits and non-Clifford gates while remaining decoupled from the logical error rate itself. Given a predefined error tolerance $p_L^*$, the protocol determines at a chosen confidence level whether the device executes the target circuit at a logical error rate below $p_L^*$. The method relies on trap circuits, copies of the target with every magic state replaced by a stabilizer state, whose outcomes are deterministic and which, being indistinguishable from the target to stochastic Pauli noise, fail at the same rate. We illustrate the protocol in Steane-code simulations of a magic state injection gadget and a quantum Fourier transform.

papers.title: EvoWeb: A Benchmark for Coding Agents on Evolving Web Applications
papers.abstract: Web application development often proceeds through successive requests that extend an existing implementation. Yet web-generation benchmarks primarily evaluate development toward fixed specifications. We introduce EvoWeb, a novel benchmark comprising 320 cumulative requests over 32 web applications, grounded in real-world product features and structured by functional dependency graphs. Agents iteratively modify a persistent codebase, while a multimodal web agent tests each intermediate application in a live browser, assessing newly requested functionality, cross-request integration, and previously requested functionality. To characterize reliability throughout development, we integrate trajectory performance across user-tolerance thresholds rather than impose a fixed stopping criterion. Experiments across open- and closed-source frontier models show that EvoWeb reveals clear performance differences between models, with cross-request integration emerging as a key challenge. Further analysis shows that later requests with deeper or more numerous dependencies are solved less accurately, while runtime errors become more frequent over successive requests. EvoWeb provides a testbed for evaluating and improving coding agents in long-horizon, multi-request development.

papers.title: Ideal quotients of $n$-exact categories
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend the notion of a removable subcategory to $n$-exact categories, and prove that an ideal quotient by a subcategory of projective-injectives inherits an $n$-exact structure from the original category if and only if the subcategory is removable. In the Frobenius case, the quotient remains Frobenius, and the stable $(n+2)$-angulated categories are equivalent. We give a sufficient condition for a subcategory of projective-injectives to be removable. We also show that the ideal quotient construction is compatible with cluster tilting. Finally, we apply the construction to $2$-cluster tilting subcategories of the category of ACM bundles on a Geigle--Lenzing projective plane, obtaining quotients for both natural and relative $2$-exact structures.

papers.title: IMPULSE: Push First, Then Predict in V-JEPA 2 Feature Space
papers.abstract: Latent world models such as V-JEPA 2 forecast in the feature space of a video encoder, but one look at an object does not reveal how hard it is to rotate, how much it bounces or how much it slides. People find out by trying: a few pokes reveal how an object responds. IMPULSE, named after the impulse response it infers, gives a predictor in frozen V-JEPA 2 feature space the same ability. A Bayesian contact memory summarizes three short calibration pushes, a predicted object pose carries it into the predictor, and a lightweight random-Fourier pose head lets the predictor use the pose. On 512 fresh objects, in a pre-specified held-out confirmation with models sealed before the data existed, the memory lowers the 1-second feature-forecast error by 11.6-12.8% relative to the same predictor without experience, for all 8 training seeds, with a 95% seed-and-object interval excluding zero. The gain also holds for 128 objects with out-of-range physics (11.7-14.0%), and the full extension beats a plain predictor by 15.5-16.6%. An information-ladder argument, exact for ideal predictors, shows that physics reaches the features only through motion, so we measure how much the pathway lets pose help. On fresh objects, the Fourier head roughly triples the gain of a perfect memory over plain pose tokens (2.8-3.2x). Raw push measurements fed through the same pathway give a similar gain, so the Bayesian summary is not required; it condenses the trials into eight interpretable numbers. The gain is absent at contact onset and grows afterwards.

papers.title: Effective shadowing of transition maps for a Hamiltonian saddle-center-center equilibrium
papers.abstract: We introduce a general methodology to construct globally unstable trajectories near the normally hyperbolic invariant manifold (NHIM) of a saddle-center-center Hamiltonian equilibrium. The proposed approach builds upon the classical geometric mechanism of searching for trajectories near heteroclinic connections between invariant tori of the NHIM. The main ingredient is the Birkhoff normal form near the NHIM, which allows us to control the dynamics of the hyperbolic and center components. We construct transition maps on the NHIM that encode the dynamics along heteroclinic connections. By combining the transition maps with the inner dynamics, given by the restriction of the Hamiltonian flow to the NHIM, we show that these connections can be efficiently (in terms of the travel time) shadowed by true trajectories of the full Hamiltonian system. Finally, the efficiency of this methodology is illustrated in the case of the NHIM associated to the libration point $L_1$ of the Spatial Restricted 3-Body Problem (SR3BP) for the Sun-Earth system.

papers.title: Reverse Hölder Class and Two-Parameter Good-$λ$ Inequality over Hausdorff Content
papers.abstract: Classical harmonic analysis is built upon Lebesgue (or more general) measure. Such a framework is remarkably successful for sets of full ambient dimension, but becomes intrinsically insensitive to lower-dimensional geometry: curves, surfaces, and more generally fractal subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\) with zero \(n\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure. In contrast, Hausdorff content provides a dimension-sensitive notion of size for lower-dimensional sets or fractal sets, but harmonic analysis in this setting is still largely limited to maximal operators. In this paper, we establish a weighted two-parameter good-\(λ\) inequality under Hausdorff content setting, providing a route toward other general operators from maximal operators over Hausdorff content. To do this, we firstly identify an appropriate reverse Hölder class $\mathcal R\mathcal H_{q,δ}$ associated with Hausdorff content, and then prove the self-improving property of $\mathcal R\mathcal H_{q,δ}$ by establishing the fundamental equivalence between reverse Hölder weights and capacitary Muckenhoupt weights. As direct applications, we obtain weighted Fefferman--Stein inequality and some boundedness on general operators over Hausdorff content. The methodology developed in this paper, even when reduced to the Lebesgue measure case, also provide novel insights, which shows that the good-\(λ\) principle is not intrinsically tied to an underlying measure, but can extended to a non-additive framework.

papers.title: Equilibria and consensus in discrete-time opinion dynamics with mixed weighted-averaging and weighted-median mechanisms
papers.abstract: Opinion dynamics models relate interpersonal influence to consensus or persistent disagreement. We study a discrete-time model combining weighted-average and weighted-median updates on a fixed directed network. Individuals update synchronously with possibly different adjustment coefficients. We characterize equilibria through local balance conditions and opinion level sets, and establish convergence to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium using nonexpansiveness and Krasnosel'skii--Mann theory. We define type-dependent cohesive sets: each weighted-average member assigns all its weight to the set, whereas each weighted-median member assigns at least one half. Consensus is reached from every initial condition if and only if no two such sets are disjoint. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent disagreement. Replacing weighted-median individuals by weighted-average individuals preserves consensus whenever it is already guaranteed for all initial conditions. Four numerical studies examine the number and locations of weighted-average individuals. The frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with their fraction in the sampled ensembles, but individual realizations need not follow this trend.

papers.title: Stable reduction and large Nielsen orbits on generalized Markoff surfaces
papers.abstract: We establish lower bounds on the orbit cardinalities of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ on the $\mathbb{F}_p$-points of the generalized Markoff surfaces given by $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz = τ+2$. We show that outside of the reductions of a certain exceptional finite set of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-points found by Dubrovin and Mazzocco, every orbit has cardinality $\ge p$. Together with a recent result of Nathaniel Kingsbury-Neuschotz, this establishes, for all but finitely many primes $p$, the classification conjectures of McCullough-Wanderley (2013), and gives a complete classification of the connected components of the Hurwitz stack of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of elliptic curves, only branched above the origin. This extends earlier work of Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak and the author in the Markoff case $τ= -2$. Our method studies certain noncongruence modular curves attached to a $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$-orbit. These modular curves parametrize elliptic curves with a $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-cover. We use this moduli interpretation to show that the noncongruence modular curves involved have bad reduction, as a cover of the $j$-line, at some place above $p$. This implies that the degree of the cover is $\ge p$, which translates into the desired bound on orbits. Key inputs include a result of Bouw-Wewers on bad reduction of three-point $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of the projective line, and the general stable reduction theory of Henrio, Obus, Raynaud, and Wewers.

papers.title: Classification of Projective Models of $K3$-surfaces
papers.abstract: Extending the methods previously established for plane sextics and quartic surfaces, we develop a unified and systematic framework for the equisingular deformation classification of projective models of $K3$-surfaces of arbitrary polarization. We treat all polarizations of degree $2n$ with $n\le 4$, including the higher-degree cases of sextic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^{4}$ and octic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^{5}$. The computational machinery developed here is degree-independent and provides a complete tool for enumerating and distinguishing the deformation classes arising from singular projective models of $K3$-surfaces. This framework lays the foundation for future investigations in higher degrees, particularly the geometry of equisingular strata, extremal configurations, real structures.

papers.title: Recovering from Pose-Selection Failures in Repeated Visual Localization
papers.abstract: Repetitive structures can give an incorrect pose candidate more inlier support than an accurate one, causing visual localization to select it. History-Guided Pose Reselection (HPR) uses coarse position forecasts from up to five past localization outputs to distinguish well-separated current-query candidates. The best-fitting forecast proposes an alternative; HPR accepts it only if every well-fitting forecast is much closer to it than to the localizer's pose. HPR needs no odometry and returns the selected candidate unchanged, using prediction for selection rather than pose refinement. With one development-set threshold, HPR improves recall within 5 meters and 10 degrees in all 12 main configurations of Hierarchical Localization (HLoc), MASt3R-based pose generation, and JIST-based retrieval, losing successes on fewer than 0.4 percent of queries. On NAVER Gangnam B1, HPR corrects 97 HLoc failures and loses six successes; gains persist within 0.25 meters and 2 degrees on all three HLoc test sets. Median HPR runtime on HLoc candidates is below one millisecond, excluding pose generation. Recovery weakens under less frequent localization.

papers.title: What UI Design Can Do For "Good" Oversight Work: A Three-Month Action Research Study
papers.abstract: With AI automating consequential tasks, human oversight is required for ethical, legal, and practical reasons. Yet these oversight tasks can be demanding and often make for poor work. Empirical evidence on overseers' lived work experiences remains underexplored, yet critical for designing ``good'' oversight. We provide longitudinal, in-the-wild insights through action research accompanying (N=8) tutors who oversaw an AI-supported learning assistant over three months. Our thematic analysis combines insights from twelve weekly meetings and two workshop iterations and was enriched by four repeated questionnaires. We identified stimulation, mastery, and relatedness as key challenges, stemming from the task's repetitiveness, unclear impact of interventions, and limited connections with students and peers. Informed by our initial findings, we deployed targeted UI modifications with mixed success. This paper documents the long-term evolution of the work characteristics of a real-world oversight task and discusses which oversight work characteristics can and cannot be supported by interface design.

papers.title: Estimating the Causal Impact of Social Navigation Signals in Corridor Scenarios
papers.abstract: Deploying robots in human-shared environments requires deciding not only how to navigate, but also when dedicated social signals are worth emitting. Classic observation-based inference can be misleading in such settings: confounding factors may bias the estimated relationship between a signal and the task outcome, leading to incorrect decisions. Causal inference provides a framework for disentangling these relationships by modelling the mechanisms linking observations, actions, and outcomes, and by estimating interventional effects after accounting for confounding paths. We study a human-robot interaction scenario in a corridor and use a causal model to estimate whether a social navigation signal causally improves transit success. We represent the interaction as a causal DAG involving robot action, pedestrian occupancy, available space, task outcome, and a controlled confounder (static obstacles). We compare the interventional estimate with the observational estimate obtained by conditioning only on the robot action, which does not explicitly model interventions. Our results show that accounting for confounding variables can reverse the conclusions drawn from naive observational analysis: the observational estimate wrongly suggests that the social signal is detrimental, whereas the causal estimate shows that it is beneficial. This discrepancy highlights how failing to account for confounding can lead to incorrect conclusions and demonstrates the importance of causal models for context-aware signalling decisions in social robot navigation.

papers.title: SLS-Bench: A Benchmark for Incident Log Summarization with Synthetic Observability Data
papers.abstract: As IT systems grow in complexity, automated agent-driven incident response becomes increasingly critical. A key capability for these agents is summarizing large log streams into human-readable reports. Further progress requires meaningfully evaluating this function, yet existing benchmarks leave end-to-end summarization from large log streams underexplored due to the prohibitive cost and complexity of collecting real-world data. We introduce SLS-Bench, a benchmark for incident log summarization featuring 90 tasks grounded in real-world incident reports, each with a synthetic log stream and a reference summary. To construct SLS-Bench, we developed a data generation pipeline that converts incident reports into structured incident models, which guide the generation of synthetic logs and reference summaries. This pipeline combines narrative grounding, explicit incident modeling, generator-verifier loops, and statistical comparisons with real-world log streams to produce realistic and controllable observability data. Our evaluation of 14 LLMs on SLS-Bench shows that while frontier models can produce useful summaries, they do so at substantial cost and latency, and open-weight models lag significantly. SLS-Bench provides a framework for systematic evaluation of log analysis agents and a scalable blueprint for future synthetic observability benchmarks.

papers.title: Probing first-generation doublet vector-like leptons via single production at the 3 TeV CLIC
papers.abstract: The single production of first-generation $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ doublet vector-like leptons (VLLs) at the Compact Linear Collider (CLIC) with $\sqrt{s}=3~\mathrm{TeV}$ is studied. The neutral and charged VLL states are investigated through $e^+e^-\rightarrowν_e\bar N+\barν_eN$ and $e^+e^-\rightarrow e^\pm E^\mp$, respectively. The neutral VLL is searched for in the $N\rightarrow W^\mp e^\pm$ channel with $W^\pm\rightarrow jj$, leading to the $e^\pm+2j+\slashed{E}_T$ final state. The charged VLL is explored through $E^\pm\rightarrow e^\pm h$ ($h\rightarrow b\bar b$) and $E^\pm\rightarrow e^\pm Z$ ($Z\rightarrow q\bar q$), yielding the $e^+e^-+2b$ and $e^+e^-+2j$ signatures. Signal and background simulations include initial-state radiation, beamstrahlung, and detector effects. Cut-based analyses are performed for integrated luminosities of $1$, $3$, and $5~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$ to obtain the exclusion and discovery sensitivities in the VLL mass--mixing parameter space. The neutral-VLL channel gives the best sensitivity. At $1~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, the $2σ$ exclusion reaches $\varepsilon\simeq0.013$ at $M_N=1.3~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $\varepsilon\simeq0.065$ at $M_N=2.9~\mathrm{TeV}$, while the $5σ$ discovery reach corresponds to $\varepsilon\simeq0.02$--$0.10$. At $5~\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, the charged-VLL channels probe masses up to about $2.9~\mathrm{TeV}$ and $2.8~\mathrm{TeV}$ in the $e^\pm h$ and $e^\pm Z$ modes, respectively. These results demonstrate that a 3 TeV CLIC can provide sensitive probes of first-generation doublet VLLs over a wide mass range, including scenarios with small VLL--electron mixing.

papers.title: Purpose IR: Compiling User Purpose for Privacy-Preserving Agent Workflow State
papers.abstract: LLM-agent workflows routinely transform rich observations into plans, summaries, memories, handoffs, and other reusable state. This creates a privacy boundary that task relevance alone does not capture: an observation may be needed as evidence for a task without its full semantics being authorized to persist. We call this mismatch the purpose-to-state semantic gap. The key distinction is that evidence authority is not release authority. We introduce Purpose IR, a bounded typed intermediate representation that compiles natural-language user purpose into an executable semantic boundary for reusable agent state. A Purpose program is an acyclic semantic dataflow graph in which evidence leaves specify task-required semantics, typed dependencies constrain authorized derivations, and declared sinks determine which values or actions may cross the reusable-state boundary. A deterministic compiler constructs and validates the authoritative program, while a typed runtime reconstructs reusable state only from validated sink outputs. Under explicit execution contracts, this design yields release confinement and purpose noninterference, characterizing what factual semantics may be released and which observation differences must become irrelevant to reusable state. Across 1,200 cases spanning LangGraph, CrewAI, and MobileRun, Purpose IR achieves 99.6% Privacy, 83.3% Task, and 83.3% Privacy-Compliant Success (PCS), outperforming the strongest high-privacy baseline by 27.5 PCS points. On 493 PrivacyLens trajectories, it achieves the highest Safe Action Rate at 77.3%, 10.4 points above the next-best method, extending the same boundary from reusable state to downstream actions. These results show that privacy-preserving agent state requires more than filtering sensitive or task-irrelevant content: it requires an explicit, executable representation of what the user's purpose authorizes to survive.

papers.title: Chain Dimension Scaling: Communication-Efficient Loop-Style Scaling for Industrial Short-Video Ranking
papers.abstract: Industrial recommendation rankers keep scaling in width and depth to billions of parameters, but this increasingly incurs costs in parameter growth, distributed communication overhead, and training inefficiency. We introduce \underline{C}hain \underline{D}imension \underline{S}caling (CDS), a scaling strategy orthogonal to width and depth. CDS repeatedly applies a single feature-interaction block with parameters shared across iterations, so the number of iterations (the chain length) becomes a new scaling dimension that adds no parameters. A lightweight intra-chain residual connection stabilizes optimization and improves quality. CDS enables two regimes. In the \emph{compression regime}, shallow blocks with a longer chain match deeper baselines with fewer parameters and faster training; in the \emph{quality-scaling regime}, increasing chain length under a fixed parameter budget yields consistent offline and online gains, suggesting the chain dimension adds modeling capacity beyond parameter reuse. We evaluate CDS in a large-scale multi-task short-video ranking system in production. In the compression regime, CDS stays within $0.03\%$ of baseline offline quality while reducing trainable parameters by 26.6\% and improving training throughput by 6.4\%, with neutral-to-positive online participation. In the quality-scaling regime, quality improves monotonically with chain length. Wall-clock analysis shows the efficiency gain comes mainly not from reduced FLOPs but from lower cross-device synchronization overhead and reduced optimizer update cost. These results position parameter-shared iterative computation as a practical, communication-efficient scaling axis for industrial ranking systems.

papers.title: MPASCNet: Magnitude-Phase-Aware Adaptive Spectral Compression for Compressed Music Restoration
papers.abstract: Compressed music restoration aims to recover high-fidelity audio from lossy codecs such as MP3 by restoring missing spectral content and reducing coding artifacts. Recently, generative adversarial networks and band-split models have made progress in compressed music restoration. However, existing methods either operate without explicitly modeling phase or rely on predefined frequency partitions, which may limit restoration performance and the use of input-dependent frequency information. To address these issues, we propose MPASCNet, a Magnitude-Phase-Aware Adaptive Spectral Compression network. Instead of using fixed bands, MPASCNet combines magnitude and phase features to guide cross-attention, adaptively compressing full-resolution spectral features into compact tokens. These tokens are then processed by a spectro-temporal backbone to model spectral-temporal dependencies. Finally, separate decoder branches reconstruct the full-resolution magnitude and wrapped phase spectra. Experiments on MP3 restoration show that MPASCNet outperforms the Apollo and AEROMamba baselines across multiple restoration metrics while using only 6.49 M parameters. The code is available at https://github.com/xinghour/MPASCNet.

papers.title: Not All Challenges Are Equal: Evaluating Interactive Liveness Detection Against Real-Time Face Swaps
papers.abstract: Remote identity verification assumes that a camera stream shows a live person, yet public real-time face-swap tools can replace that person before the stream reaches the verifier. Passive deepfake detectors generalize poorly to new generators, while interactive challenges are often selected without evidence of which gestures expose current attacks. We evaluate randomized gesture challenges in 108 live sessions with six subjects, 24 impersonated identities, and two face-swap tools, DeepFaceLive and FaceFusion, injected through a virtual camera. The static calibration segment reaches a session-level AUC of 0.878 with a frozen UCF spatial detector, while the mean across the active-gesture windows reaches 0.988. Pose and combined gestures have the highest point estimates, whereas expressions show no clear improvement. Hand occlusion against FaceFusion, configured with an occlusion mask, scores below the static baseline. The end-to-end time required to satisfy the validator also distinguishes attacks from genuine sessions, achieving a session-level AUC of 0.732, although this signal includes synthesis and transport delays. These results show that challenge sets should be tested against current attack configurations and that response time can provide an additional, deployment-specific signal.

papers.title: Kinematic saturation of the electromagnetically-induced-transparency peak in thermal atomic vapors
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that, in thermal atomic vapors, the electromagnetically-induced-transparency (EIT) transmission peak exhibits saturation. Investigating the amplitude of the velocity-selected double-resonance transmission peak-a purely kinematic effect arising from finite wavevector mismatch-we identify a threshold atomic column density Ns. For column densities N below Ns, the amplitude of the transmission peak maximum increases with column density. Once it exceeds Ns, the peak amplitude maximum remains constant, while the corresponding detuning shifts away from resonance and scales as the square root of ln(N over Ns). Furthermore, We find that the operating point for optimum photon-shot-noise-limited sensitivity deviates from that of the transmission peak maximum. Our study provides guidance for optimizing EIT readout in vapor cell and for precision measurements built upon this scheme.

papers.title: Learning $ω$-Powered Conditional Distributions with Importance-Weighted Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) with guidance scale $γ$ is commonly motivated by the $ω$-powered conditional distribution obtained by setting $ω=γ$, but CFG does not, in general, sample from this distribution exactly. We study whether the powered target can instead be learned explicitly. We introduce Importance-Weighted Conditional Flow Matching (IW-CFM), which reweights conditional flow-matching examples using density ratios obtained from frozen conditional and unconditional flow models. With exact normalized weights, the resulting objective has the same gradient as flow matching on the powered target; in practice, we use self-normalized estimation and a regularized empirical approximation for high-dimensional data. On synthetic distributions, IW-CFM recovers analytical powered targets for which numerically matched CFG, $γ=ω$, exhibits a visible mismatch. On ImageNet, an amortized lightweight corrector achieves better alignment than fixed- and matched-guidance CFG with the corresponding weighted and filtered reference distributions. We additionally present an exploratory CLIP analysis of powered-density rankings on real ImageNet data. Aggregate shifts across selected prompt-specific contrasts coexist with heterogeneous classwise responses, including nonmonotonic trajectories. These results provide a practical route for studying and approximating model-defined powered conditional distributions.

papers.title: The Inviscid Limit of Viscous Burgers through Shock Formation and Development
papers.abstract: We study the inviscid limit of the one-dimensional viscous Burgers equation from smooth initial data through nondegenerate shock formation and subsequent shock development. Chaturvedi and Graham \cite{CG} obtained sharp estimates of order $ν^{1/4}$ up to the shock-formation time. We extend their analysis beyond this time, comparing the viscous solution with the inviscid entropy solution evolving from the same initial data. With the shock-formation time normalized to $t=0$, we prove a pointwise error bound on a fixed interval $0\leq t \leq \bar{\varepsilon}$, where $\bar{\varepsilon}>0$ is independent of the viscosity $ν$. The bound consists of a term of order $ν^{1/4}$ and an exponentially localized contribution originating from the viscous shock layer. The proof is based on matching an outer expansion, an inner expansion near the formation point, and a viscous shock-profile expansion. Combined with the results of Chaturvedi and Graham, this yields a quantitative description of the inviscid limit from the initial time through the development of the young shock.

papers.title: Angle-Resolved Photoemission as a Sensitive Probe of Surface Quality: Sputtered versus Annealed Cu(001)
papers.abstract: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) requires a well-ordered surface, whose quality is routinely judged from low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). We compare LEED, XPS, and ARPES of a Cu(001) single crystal measured in situ at four stages of surface preparation: as-prepared, after aging for 24 h at 6 K, after Ar$^+$ sputtering, and after annealing. The sputtered and annealed surfaces show nearly identical $(1\times1)$ LEED patterns and Cu 2$p$ core levels, but the sputtered surface yields a momentum-independent ARPES spectrum, and the band dispersion recovers after annealing. We attribute this contrast to how each probe responds to sputtering-induced defects: LEED reflects the average lattice, which remains periodic, whereas ARPES reflects the electronic states, whose crystal momentum is no longer well defined. Our results indicate that a sharp LEED pattern and clean core-level spectra do not guarantee a surface suitable for ARPES.

papers.title: Multivariate phase-space interpretation of ensemble forecasts: A comparison of physical and AI models
papers.abstract: Ensemble forecasts from the ECMWF's Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) and the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS-ENS) are compared using a multi-dimensional evaluation framework. Within this framework, the uncertainty is interpreted as the linear subspace spanned by the ensemble members in phase space, from which various geometric properties are extracted. As revealed by the analysis, the error does not entirely lie in this subspace, but is reasonably well calibrated in all directions. Moreover, the framework allows to quantify that this subspace critically depends on the number of ensemble members, suggesting that the current setups only partially represent the uncertainty subspace. This phase-space interpretation furthermore allows a direct comparison of the error-representation patterns of AIFS-ENS and IFS by computing the principal angles between the subspaces: IFS and AIFS ensemble subspaces do not entirely overlap in phase space, even though they were shown to have similar abilities to represent the amplitude and the structure of the error.

papers.title: Low-Cost Deep Learning for Automated Keyframe Interpolation in Sprite Animation
papers.abstract: Sprite-based animation remains prevalent in video game development, but manual in-betweening---generating intermediate frames between keyframes---is labor-intensive. Existing video frame interpolation methods, optimized for photorealistic content, introduce smoothing artifacts when applied to the sharp edges, limited color palettes, and stylized motion characteristic of hand-drawn sprites. We present a deep learning approach for sprite in-betweening that adapts a U-Net encoder-decoder architecture with domain-specific modifications, including RGBA-aware processing, multi-scale flow refinement, and alpha-gated blending to preserve pixel-perfect sprite aesthetics. Following data-centric AI principles, we demonstrate that a few carefully curated sprite animation triplets---selected for diversity, quality, and representative edge cases---enable effective training without requiring massive generic datasets. Experimental evaluation using the FLIP perceptual metric shows that our method achieves a mean error of 0.258 on 42 test triplets, outperforming state-of-the-art video interpolation RIFE (0.313, 17.5\% worse), traditional optical flow Lucas-Kanade (0.449, 42.6\% worse), and general frame synthesis CyclicGen (0.603, 57.2\% worse). This study shows that quality-over-quantity data curation and domain-specific architectural adaptations yield better interpolation quality than general-purpose methods trained on orders of magnitude more data, validating the data-centric AI paradigm for specialized visual domains. This is particularly important for small-to-medium-sized game development studios, where budget and time constraints are critical.

papers.title: Thermal softening of the yield stress in glasses with different stability
papers.abstract: The yielding of amorphous solids has been extensively studied in the athermal limit, but the influence of thermal fluctuations is much less understood, in particular for glasses of different stability. Using molecular dynamics simulations of a model glass where the swap Monte Carlo algorithm can be employed, we study the yield stress at finite temperature and shear rate, both in steady flow and at shear start-up, over a broad range of glass stability. Thermal fluctuations soften both the dynamic yield stress in steady state and the start-up yield stress. In all cases, the temperature dependence is compatible with the $T^{2/3}$ law expected for thermally activated yielding near a saddle-node instability, with no systematic dependence of the exponent on stability or shear rate. Extrapolations to zero temperature recover the athermal yield stresses. The amplitude of the softening at start-up, by contrast, depends strongly on stability: highly stable glasses are much less sensitive to temperature than poorly annealed ones. A description of yielding at finite temperature must therefore account explicitly for the stability of the glass.

papers.title: Federated Coreset Subsampling for Distributed Memory Banks
papers.abstract: In real-world scenarios, industrial processes can span multiple factories and goods are often produced at multiple sites, leading to a shared yet non-identical distribution of data across locations. To address this, we propose two federated approaches for i) combining existing coresets (Double Subsampling) and ii) creating new coresets (Federated Subsampling) in a distributed anomaly detection setting. In particular, we adapt the memory bank based PatchCore algorithm to a federated setting, resulting in increased cold-start performance, resilience to domain- and sensor-shift, and resilience to unreliable actor participation, a common problem in classical, network based federated learning strategies.

papers.title: AuthGateBench: Benchmarking LLMs as Authorization Gate
papers.abstract: Automated approval systems let coding agents execute high-risk actions with minimal human oversight by delegating the authorization decision to a classifier, typically a large language model (LLM). Such systems, adopted in tools like Claude Code and Codex, remain vulnerable to failure modes such as scope escalation, where the agent takes actions exceeding what the user authorized. Existing benchmarks focus mainly on malicious requests, evaluating refusal under an implicit policy. We introduce AuthGateBench, the first policy-guided benchmark for authorization gating under benign requests. We implement a novel pipeline where an LLM generates contrast pairs with identical action and trajectory but differing request, flipping the label between block and allow. This allows us to assess whether models reason over context rather than the action alone. We further examine whether auxiliary environment signals can help models make better decisions. The resulting benchmark comprises 1,400 instances spanning five failure modes drawn from real-world Claude Code incidents. Evaluations show accuracy degrades unevenly across failure modes as models over-rely on internal safety alignment, and models still block most actions even when explicitly authorized, revealing unstable rather than deterministic decisions; retrospectively retrieved environment signals, however, substantially improve authorization accuracy.

papers.title: Resample the Answer: Where to Spend Test-Time Compute in Recursive Reasoning
papers.abstract: Recursive reasoning models such as the Tiny Recursive Model (TRM) iteratively refine two latent states: an answer state y, decoded into the output, and a reasoning state z, which is never decoded. Many of their failures have been attributed to bad basins, regions of latent space that trap the recursion on wrong answers. Recent test-time approaches perturb y, z or both to recover these failures, but the impact of this choice on performance, test-time compute efficiency and scaling properties remains unclear. Through controlled experiments on TRM, we find that a failed trajectory carries its failure in its answer state. At equal compute, whether retries continue a failed trajectory (depth scaling) or draw multiple trajectories from the initial states (width scaling), resampling y recovers more failures than any perturbation of z we tested, and the performance gap widens as the test-time compute budget grows. Our approach, Gated Answer Resampling (GAR), pairs this resampling of the answer state with the model's own halting head and restarts only the puzzles that the head rejects. With at most 64 restarts per puzzle and no training or hyperparameter search, GAR takes TRM from 85.9% to 99.4% on Sudoku-Extreme and from 68.8% to 85.6% on Pencil Puzzle Bench validation. On the same checkpoints, GAR also outperforms Probabilistic TRM (PTRM), which perturbs z at each step, even when PTRM uses 42 to 197 times as much compute. Our code is available at https://github.com/MaximeILL/GAR.

papers.title: From the QBO to Rieger-type periods: Explaining extreme solar events by tidally triggered magneto-Rossby waves
papers.abstract: It has recently been demonstrated that the occurrence of extreme solar events is governed by a phase-stable period close to 1.723 years (629.29 days). According to our previously developed tidally-synchronized solar dynamo model, this is one of the periods resulting from two-planet spring tides exerted by the tidally dominant planets Venus, Earth and Jupiter, which trigger magneto-Rossby waves in the solar tachocline. Overall, the squared sum of these three waves incorporates nine periods ranging from 59 to 629 days. Using a standard Rayleigh test, we demonstrate that all nine of these periods can be identified in the data on extreme solar events. For the latter, we use a combination of 72 ground-level enhancement (GLE) events with various X-flare data, the number of which increases when the threshold is successively lowered from X10 to X1. To identify the spectral peaks, it is necessary to analyze the sidebands that emerge due to the modulation with the longer-term periods such as the 11-year Schwabe cycle and the third harmonics of the Hale cycle. In this framework, the seminal Rieger period of 154 days is re-interpreted as the lower sideband of 146 days which is the quarter of the synodic period of Venus and Earth.

papers.title: Taming Nonconvexity with Epigraph Lifting
papers.abstract: We consider inverse problems regularized by a trained neural network with \emph{convex activations} and \emph{unrestricted weights}. The resulting optimization problem is generally nonconvex, and gradient-based methods may converge to poor local minima. We introduce a \emph{penalized epigraph lifting} of the network and show that the lifted problem admits a \emph{difference-of-convex (DC) decomposition}. For Lipschitz continuous activations, we establish \emph{finite exactness}: the original objective is recovered exactly at a finite and explicitly computable penalty threshold $\barρ$. Building on this structure, we propose \emph{H-DC} (Homotopic DC), a homotopic scheme that solves a sequence of DC subproblems with increasing $ρ$, warm-starting each level from the previous solution. Numerical experiments on synthetic problems, a manifold denoiser regularizer, and image inpainting with a learned Mumford--Shah regularizer show that H-DC consistently escapes poor local minima and reaches solutions with lower objective values than gradient-based methods from the same initialization.

papers.title: Spiking Neural Beamforming for Multichannel Speech Enhancement on the Edge
papers.abstract: Speech enhancement with wearable and edge devices requires architectures that balance enhancement quality against power and memory resources. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a promising path towards this goal through sparse, event-driven computation, but existing SNN-based speech enhancement methods are largely restricted to single-channel processing and therefore cannot exploit the spatial diversity available from microphone arrays. In this work, we propose a fully SNN framework for multichannel speech enhancement based on a fully connected architecture (FC-SNN) with sequential spike encoding, derived from a compact artificial neural network (ANN) baseline via leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. We characterize how enhancement performance scales with model size and spike-train length relative to ANN and classical beamforming baselines, and report the resulting parameter counts and computational complexity. We further compare direct and rate spike encoding, revealing a clear trade-off between event-driven computation and enhancement performance, and use these results to identify favorable configurations for edge devices.

papers.title: Lens spaces that cannot be obtained by two integral surgeries
papers.abstract: In this article, we demonstrate that there exists an infinite family of lens spaces L(p,q) that cannot be obtained from the 3-sphere by two integral surgeries. The first such lens space in our family is L(177,29).

papers.title: Cotangent cohomology and higher-order obstructions of matroids
papers.abstract: Matroid Stanley-Reisner rings admit essential deformation obstructions of arbitrarily high order over every field, already at corank three. For each $m\ge3$, we construct a connected cosimple matroid and $m$ fine-homogeneous first-order classes whose proper subcollections integrate jointly and whose pairwise primary cup products vanish. A specified joint $(m-1)$-jet nevertheless has no lift to order $m$, even without preserving the grading. The construction rests on formulas for every multigraded component of the second cotangent cohomology $T^2$ and of its primary cup image, expressed through flats and parallel classes of the dual matroid. These formulas show that $T^2$ vanishes exactly when every connected component has corank at most two, or equivalently when there is no $U_{1,4}$-minor. This proves a conjecture of Constantinescu, Klein, Nguyen, Singh, and Venturello (2025) and characterizes formal smoothness of the affine deformation functor. For the duals of rank-three truncations of $U_{2,m}\oplus U_{2,n}$, $m,n\ge3$, each nonzero homogeneous class modulo the primary cup image is realized as a higher-order obstruction, and the quotient has an explicit presentation with $m+n-2$ minimal homogeneous generators.

papers.title: Fading Memory and Nonlinear Dynamics in a Microring Resonator Network and their Use in Computation
papers.abstract: Silicon microring resonators are promising components for photonic reservoir computing because their nonlinear optical response can transform signals and retain information about recent inputs. Under constant optical excitation, their coupled free-carrier and thermal dynamics can generate self-pulsing: a periodic output response. However, constant-input behavior does not reveal how these dynamics respond to randomly modulated signals or whether their memory is useful for temporal processing. Here, we characterize a single silicon microring resonator and a passive network of microring resonators under random input modulation. The temporal component associated with self-pulsing remains observable under random modulation, but the largest fading memory occurs near the self-pulsing boundary, where no resolved self-pulsing-like oscillation is present. reservoir computing metrics, such as memory capacity, map this accessible memory, and its decay provides effective timescales associated mainly with free-carrier and thermal relaxation. Finally, we use NARMA reconstruction to test whether the measured memory profile supports nonlinear temporal processing. Responses with a resolved self-pulsing-like component perform worse on this task, and the intrinsic memory profile is not matched to the required input history. These results show that reservoir computing metrics can characterize nonlinear microring resonator dynamics even when the physical system is not an effective standalone reservoir for the selected task.

papers.title: ECHO: Correcting Time Series Foundation Model Forecasts with Historical Analogues and Errors
papers.abstract: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) provide general-purpose forecasting capabilities, yet their forecasts can remain misaligned with the temporal characteristics of a target domain. This motivates lightweight forecast correction even when only black-box access to the TSFM is available. Our key observation is that two forms of historical information provide complementary correction signals: historical analogues reveal how similar contexts evolved, while past forecast errors reveal a TSFM's characteristic deviations in the target domain. Based on this observation, we propose ECHO, a black-box forecast correction framework that learns from both sources. ECHO uses AnalogE to assess retrieved historical analogues together with the current context and base forecast, learning transferable corrections through cross-domain pretraining. In parallel, RecentE learns target-specific residual corrections from past forecast errors and refines them as causally available feedback accumulates. ECHO dynamically combines the two corrections according to their observed forecasting performance. Across 5 representative TSFMs and 9 real-world datasets, ECHO reduces MSE in all 45 backbone--dataset settings, yielding an average relative reduction of 9.26\% in macro-average MSE. Its gains also extend to long-horizon forecasting.

papers.title: Biconservative hypersurfaces in Euclidean Spaces
papers.abstract: An isometric immersion $X: Σ^n \longrightarrow \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is biharmonic (BHH) if $Δ^2 X = 0$, i.e., if $ΔH =0$, where $Δ$ and $H$ are the metric Laplacian and the mean curvature vector field of $Σ^n$ respectively. More generally, biconservative hypersurfaces (BCHs) are isometric immersions for which only the tangential part of the biharmonic equation vanishes. BCHs are first described and then constructed.

papers.title: CultureBot: A Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Exploration of Cultural Heritage Data
papers.abstract: Digital cultural heritage collections encode rich relations among objects, places, periods, providers, images, and source institutions, yet users typically access them through keyword search and faceted browsing. We present CULTUREBOT, an interactive framework for natural-language exploration of cultural heritage collections that combines knowledge-graph-guided retrieval, lexical-semantic retrieval, and source-linked generation. CULTUREBOT maps user queries to structured catalogue relations, enriches retrieved records with textual evidence, and generates answers that link back to the underlying repository records. We instantiate the framework on 81,852 SearchCulture records and release an online demonstration. In an expert evaluation involving six cultural-heritage specialists, 55 persona-grounded queries, and 250 evaluations, the graph-guided system was rated significantly higher than two general-purpose assistants and a non-graph ablation, with the largest gains in evidence grounding, diversity, reasoning, and completeness. These results support graph-guided retrieval as a practical way to expose the relational structure of cultural collections through conversational access while preserving links to catalogue evidence.

papers.title: Radial pressureless Euler flow: structure and stability of absorption at the origin
papers.abstract: We study absorption at the origin in radial pressureless Euler flow in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq2$. For rotation-invariant nonnegative locally finite initial mass and bounded radial initial velocity vanishing at the origin, we prove global existence and uniqueness in a full-space radial entropy class with a one-sided Lipschitz bound and an initial kinetic-energy trace. Absorption is permanent, including retention of any initial origin atom. For finite positive mass with finite second moment, a Lagrangian projection representation characterizes the absorbed mass and its left limits at positive times through extreme minimizers of a free-position primitive. We derive a radial scalar momentum balance with a nonnegative Stieltjes boundary impulse measure. The minimum value of the same primitive yields a weighted Stieltjes identity equating accumulated time-weighted impulse with the integral of initial radii over absorbed labels, valid also for jumps and singular continuous absorption; the boundary impulse measure and the absorption measure are mutually absolutely continuous on $(0,\infty)$. For such finite-mass data with common total mass, strong $L^2$ convergence of initial quantiles and Lagrangian velocities, together with convergence of initial origin masses, yields convergence of absorbed mass at continuity times of the limiting absorption and local weak convergence of absorption measures on $(0,\infty)$. Finally, even with a fixed smooth initial radial probability density, every probability measure compactly supported in $(0,\infty)$ can be realized as the absorption measure by choosing a bounded radial initial velocity; in particular, purely singular continuous absorption occurs.

papers.title: Tempered fractional Laplacian: Boundary regularity
papers.abstract: We study the boundary regularity of solutions for the tempered fractional Laplacian \[ (-Δ)^s_λu=f \quad \text{in }Ω, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ, \] where \(0<s<1\), \(λ>0\), and \(Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a bounded Lipschitz domain satisfying the exterior ball condition. The tempered operator is defined by \[ (-Δ)^s_λu(x) = c_{n,s}\operatorname{P.V.} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{u(x)-u(y)}{|x-y|^{n+2s}} e^{-λ|x-y|}\,dy, \] which was originally proposed in [Koponen, Phys. Rev. E (1995), 1197-1199]. % Exponential tempering preserves the leading singularity of % the kernel but destroys its homogeneity, preventing a direct % application of classical boundary regularity estimates. % Extending these estimates [Ros-Oton and Serra, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2014), 275--302] to the tempered setting therefore % requires overcoming the difficulties caused by the loss % of scale invariance. By decomposing the operator into the classical fractional Laplacian and the correction operator \(\mathcal Q_λ^s\), and combining approximation, localization, and iterative arguments with interpolation inequalities, we establish the global estimate \[ \|u\|_{C^s(\mathbb{R}^n)} \le C\|f\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}. \] For more regular data, we derive interior and boundary-weighted Schauder estimates. In particular, under suitable regularity assumptions on \(f\), these estimates yield \[ |D^νu(x)| \le C\,δ(x)^{s-|ν|}, \quad |ν| > 0, \] where \(ν\) is a multi-index and \(δ(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,\partialΩ)\).
