These bounds quantify the possible growth of higher-order derivatives near the boundary and provide a regularity foundation for numerical error analysis of the tempered problem.

papers.title: Decoupling Trap States in Amorphous Oxide Semiconductor Transistor Using a Conductive-Semiconducting-Conductive MOS Structure
papers.abstract: We propose a novel amorphous oxide semiconductor (AOS)-based conductive-semiconducting-conductive (CSC) MOS test structure to effectively sense, discriminate, and analyze distinct trap-induced conductance losses in AOS transistors. In conventional test structures, non-ideal metal-AOS contacts convolute the conductance loss generated by various trap states. The CSC architecture mitigates these contact-related artifacts, enabling the decoupling of interface states and shallow states. Furthermore, the contributions from leakage, series resistance, and device-geometry effects are identified and calibrated. Our results yield bias-resolved trap profiles and reveal three distinct regimes: (1) In the depletion region, interface states dominate the conductance loss. These states exhibit sub-microsecond time constants and their density increases slightly with deeper depletion, which is associated with donor-like states. (2) From weak to moderate accumulation, shallow states become the primary contributor, displaying a Gaussian-like volumetric density-of-states distribution with response times spanning from microseconds to nanoseconds. (3) In the strong accumulation regime, interface states regain dominance with an increased state quantity, while their time constants remain invariant. These bias-resolved profiles clarify how different trap populations impact AOS transistors under distinct operating conditions, providing intuitive metrics for understanding reliability degradation. Consequently, the CSC structure offers a simple, scalable, and robust platform for trap characterization in AOS transistors.

papers.title: Thermally Enhanced Pseudo-Goldstone Spin Gap in the Isotropic Helimagnet ZnCr$_2$Se$_4$
papers.abstract: In magnetically ordered systems, the spin gap in the magnon spectrum is normally expected to decrease on warming and close at the transition out of the long-range order. The presence of a pseudo-Goldstone gap is commonly associated with nonlinear terms in spin-wave theory. However, its precise origin and detailed properties can vary and remain under debate. Here we show by means of inelastic neutron scattering that the pseudo-Goldstone gap in the Heisenberg helimagnet ZnCr$_2$Se$_4$ exhibits an atypical, nonmonotonic temperature dependence: the gap increases over much of the ordered phase before closing near $T_\mathrm{N}$. These results align with recent spin-dynamic simulations based on an effective quartic potential in an isotropic system~[Phys. Rev. B \textbf{113}, L220411 (2026)]. As the pseudo-Goldstone spin gap in ZnCr$_2$Se$_4$ is dominated by quantum effects at subkelvin temperatures, its characteristic growth on warming is caused by thermal fluctuations.

papers.title: ARMED: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Medication Recommendation
papers.abstract: Medication recommendation requires jointly considering diagnoses, comorbidities, longitudinal patient history, and treatment interactions. Although recent retrieval-augmented generation approaches using language models have shown promise for clinical recommendation, most existing systems rely on fixed retrieval pipelines that cannot adapt to diverse clinical retrieval scenarios and may introduce noisy or irrelevant evidence. We propose ARMED, an adaptive clinical RAG framework that dynamically expands retrieval according to retrieval sufficiency and current-admission relevance. ARMED first observes the initial retrieval outcome and selectively performs supplementary or fallback multi-query retrieval when additional evidence is needed. The framework also incorporates a relevance gate that activates only clinically relevant same-patient history and organizes retrieved evidence into structured query-level clinical evidence. Experiments on MIMIC-IV demonstrate that ARMED consistently outperforms previous static retrieval baselines and improves overall medication recommendation quality. By combining locally runnable small language models with adaptive retrieval, ARMED supports medication recommendation without relying on external language model APIs or task-specific fine-tuning.

papers.title: VisExMEM: Visual Evidence-Based Explainable Multimodal Evaluation Metric
papers.abstract: Current image-text evaluation often relies on a global score, which gives limited insight into which semantic details are supported by the image. Explainable metrics provide rationales, but the visual evidence supporting those rationales can still be difficult to verify. We introduce VisExMEM, a reference-free evaluator that decomposes captions into atomic claims, localizes visual evidence, verifies each claim, and averages claim-level support into a global score. Explanations use the same evidence and decisions. We train Qwen3.5-based 4B and 9B models on 100K samples with multi-task SFT, counterfactual refinement, and evidence-aware GDPO. Across eight benchmarks, VisExMEM-9B achieves the highest descriptive composite among open-source evaluators in our comparison, exceeding VQAScore by 11.7 points while remaining competitive with GPT-5.6 Sol. We also introduce AGITA-Bench, containing 600 human-annotated image-text pairs and 8.7K atomic claims for global and claim-level evaluation. For untuned Qwen3.5 and GPT-5.6 Sol controls, decomposed prompting raises the same composite by 3.6-5.1 points relative to holistic prompting. Human evaluation shows that VisExMEM explanations outperform prior explainable metrics and approach GPT-5.6 Sol.

papers.title: Revisiting Fast Tendermint: An Agreement Violation and Two Repairs
papers.abstract: Fast Tendermint reduces Tendermint's good-case latency to two communication steps for n>=5f+1. We show that its published round-change rule violates Agreement: one Byzantine process suffices for every f>=1, and for f>=2 two Byzantine processes suffice without double signing. The failure occurs when a process advances past a round without recording the value that may have been decided there. The Quint specification that accompanies the protocol does not allow this kind of round skipping and is not affected; the violation lies in the published pseudocode. We present two repairs. Walk requires a process to leave each round on a quorum of that round's precommits and to precommit before leaving. It keeps the recorded valid state and removes the wait after a precommit quorum. Justify carries the evidence needed to accept a proposal in the proposal itself, removing both the recorded valid state and the proposer's synchronization wait. Both satisfy Agreement and Validity under asynchrony and Termination under the partially synchronous gossip model of Tendermint and Fast Tendermint. Both retain proposal timeouts. The main text presents the executions that violate Agreement and explains the two repairs. The appendices provide proofs, a brief comparison with other round-change designs, and an extension to chains.

papers.title: RAP-WAM: Learning World-Action Models through Predictive Rehearsal and Action Perturbations
papers.abstract: Recent world action models draw on video generation priors to jointly predict future observations and robot actions. Adapting these priors to control requires determining how future predictions should guide policy learning. RAP-WAM combines predictive Rehearsal and Action Perturbations (RAP) with future-supervised queries and Coupled Action Projection for policy learning. Predictive rehearsal trains on model-generated inputs while retaining recorded targets, and accumulates recurring errors into a spatial prior. We perturb actions and measure changes in video predictions. Action-response-based spatiotemporal credit assignment combines these responses, prediction error, and the rehearsal prior to allocate visual supervision; spatially aggregating the responses determines supervision intensity across future action steps. No separate scoring network or deployment-time probe is required. The base learns from a video-pretrained backbone without intermediate pretraining on external embodied data. We evaluate the fixed base and its agent-refined, task-conditioned system. On 42 RoboDojo tasks, their average success rates are 12.85% and 15.62%, with Scores of 17.86 and 20.59. Across 15 real-robot tasks, the complete system achieves 89.00% task-macro-average success, exceeding the strongest of five baselines by 37.67 percentage points. Across 315 fixed-output simulation windows, 45.21% of response-top20 positions fall outside error-top20, revealing information beyond prediction error. Videos and further details are available on the project website: https://rapwam.github.io/.

papers.title: Pixels or Code? Benchmarking Instruction-Guided Visual Artifact Operation
papers.abstract: Visual artifacts such as charts, technical diagrams, webpages, and document pages underpin scientific, commercial, and engineering workflows. Editing these artifacts requires direct modification, dependency-aware updates, preservation of unaffected content, and compliance with domain constraints. We define this capability as Visual Artifact Operation (VAO). Prior benchmarks test parts of this problem, including cascading updates in charts. We study direct edits, dependent updates, and preservation across visual domains and pixel, code, and agent paradigms under one image-only protocol. We introduce Visual Artifact Operation Bench (VAO-Bench), comprising 1,573 manually screened tasks across nine artifact categories and three difficulty levels. VAO-Bench uses executable artifacts and deterministic rendering to trace reference transformations and annotate direct edits, dependent updates, and preservation constraints. All systems receive the same source image and instruction; we evaluate pixel-space editors, code-generating multimodal systems, and tool-using agents on direct-edit accuracy, dependency-aware update, content preservation, domain validity, and visual quality. Experiments show that executable-code systems better support dependent updates, while pixel-space editors offer faster execution and strong visual quality. Explicitly stating dependencies improves both paradigms, identifying implicit-update inference as a central bottleneck. VAO-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for dependable visual artifact editing across generation paradigms.

papers.title: Depth-zero local Langlands via shtukas in mixed characteristic
papers.abstract: Assuming a smoothness property for mixed-characteristic shtuka spaces and hyperbolic localization for twisted sheaves, we determine the inertial restriction of the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter for irreducible depth-zero representations. Let $E$ be a non-archimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$, let $G$ be an unramified connected reductive group over $E$, and let $π$ be an irreducible smooth depth-zero representation of $G(E)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{\ell}$ where $\ell$ is a prime number which does not divide $p|π_0Z(G)|$. Let $\varphi_π^{\operatorname{FS}}$ be the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter associated to $π$. We describe the restriction of $\varphi_π^{\operatorname{FS}}$ to the inertia subgroup in terms of Deligne-Lusztig theory. We prove this by computing the inertia action on the cohomology of shtuka spaces with depth-zero level structure. As an application, we prove that the Fargues--Scholze $L$-parameters agree with DeBacker--Reeder $L$-parameters over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ell}$.

papers.title: The rich-neighbor chromatic index is linear in the maximum degree
papers.abstract: An edge of a multigraph is rich with respect to a proper edge-coloring if all the edges adjacent to it receive mutually distinct colors, and a proper edge-coloring is a rich-neighbor coloring if every non-isolated edge has a rich edge adjacent to it. The least number of colors in such a coloring is the rich-neighbor chromatic index chi'_rn(G). So far it was studied for subcubic graphs only, and multigraphs of larger maximum degree are considered here for the first time. The only upper bound valid in general was the quadratic one inherited from the strong chromatic index, while a single rich edge already requires 2D-1 colors in a D-regular graph, where D denotes the maximum degree. We give an upper linear bound chi'_rn(G) <= 6D-8 which holds for every loopless multigraph G with D >= 3, and we show that a coloring realizing this bound can be found in polynomial time. Consequently chi'_rn(G) = Theta(D). For D-regular graphs with D >= 3 the lower bound is 2D-1, and the upper bound is 5D-8. The bound 5D-8 holds more generally for every multigraph with D >= 3 which has a dominating P_{>=3}-system, and we characterize these multigraphs: such a system exists if and only if k_2(G-T) <= 2|T| holds for every set T of vertices, where k_2 counts the components on two vertices. In particular the bound holds for every graph with 3 <= D <= 4d-4, where d denotes the minimum degree. The paper is concluded with a conjecture on the tight upper bound on chi'_rn(G).

papers.title: Explaining Heterogeneous Treatment Effects with Causal Forests and the Hoeffding Functional Decomposition
papers.abstract: The estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects is a central objective of causal inference. However, state-of-the-art algorithms to solve this task are based on machine learning principles, and thus behave as black boxes. Consequently, the identification of covariates driving heterogeneity remains a challenging and open problem. To address this limitation, we introduce CausalTreeHFD, an interpretable extension of causal forests, based on the Hoeffding functional decomposition adapted to tree ensembles. Our approach decomposes predictions of conditional average treatment effects (CATE) into contributions from individual covariates and pairwise interactions, providing a direct characterization of the factors driving treatment effect heterogeneity. We establish the consistency of CausalTreeHFD, which converges towards the Hoeffding decomposition of the underlying CATE function, under standard assumptions for the analysis of causal forests. Experiments on simulated and real datasets show that CausalTreeHFD accurately identifies relevant covariates and interactions, and precisely recovers their contributions to heterogeneous treatment effects.

papers.title: Tikhonov-Stabilized Bezier Representation Forecasting for Training-free Diffusion Acceleration
papers.abstract: Diffusion models, particularly Diffusion Transformers, achieve strong image and video generation quality but remain expensive at inference time due to repeated denoiser evaluations. Feature caching offers a deployment-friendly acceleration strategy by reusing or predicting intermediate representations without retraining the generator or modifying the sampler. However, existing cache-then-forecast methods often rely on Taylor-style finite-difference extrapolation, which can become unstable over longer cache intervals, and typically predict local module outputs whose errors may accumulate through subsequent denoiser blocks. We propose \textbf{BeziCast}, a training-free diffusion acceleration framework that forecasts output-proximal denoising representations using low-order B'ezier trajectories. BeziCast estimates B'ezier control points via Tikhonov-stabilized fitting, providing a smooth, capacity-controlled temporal parameterization that avoids explicit high-order derivative estimation and decouples trajectory capacity from cache-query density. To moderate aggressive extrapolation, we further derive equivalent forecasting weights and introduce a convex-hull-inspired guardrail that detects high-risk predictions and softly pulls them toward a conservative simplex-projected estimate. Extensive evaluations across advanced image and video diffusion models demonstrate the effectiveness of BeziCast. In particular, BeziCast accelerates FLUX.1 by up to (4.79\times) and HunyuanVideo by up to (4.11\times), while preserving substantially better generation quality than competing acceleration baselines.

papers.title: CryptoFlowBench: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Reasoning on Blockchains for Cryptocurrency Fund Tracing
papers.abstract: Pseudonymous accounts and complex smart-contract ecosystems substantially hinder the tracing of illicit cryptocurrency fund flows. Existing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved promising performance in blockchain fraud detection, yet their static node- or edge-level predictions do not naturally generalize to multi-hop fund tracing. Meanwhile, existing tracing methods mainly rely on predefined heuristics to capture multi-hop relationships, limiting their adaptive reasoning capabilities. To bridge this gap, we introduce CryptoFlowBench, a benchmark constructed from authoritative reports on cryptocurrency-related illicit incidents, with four tasks spanning local to multi-hop fund tracing. These tasks pose substantial challenges to existing learning- and heuristic-based methods, particularly in complex multi-hop scenarios. We therefore propose ChainSleuth, a graph-tool-augmented agent that iteratively reasons, invokes graph tools, and updates its tracing trajectory, enabling adaptive information acquisition and recovery from erroneous paths. Experiments show that no baseline consistently dominates all four tasks, revealing substantial gaps between local fraud detection and multi-hop fund tracing. ChainSleuth achieves notable improvements on multi-hop tasks, demonstrating the potential of agentic graph reasoning for cryptocurrency fund investigation.

papers.title: CivWorldBench: Evaluating Language World Models in Structured Multi-Agent Sandbox Worlds
papers.abstract: The growing use of language models for forecasting motivates a broader evaluation of their world-model capabilities. Such evaluation must go beyond predictive accuracy to assess hidden-state inference and intervention prediction. Real-world forecasting benchmarks offer limited access to hidden-state ground truth and controlled experiments. We introduce CivWorldBench, a benchmark built on a multi-agent strategy game engine with recorded internal states, controlled observations, and paired intervention rollouts. Its 1,900 decision points from 475 worlds support three task levels: association forecasting, belief inference, and intervention prediction. Reference predictors support attributable evaluation of capability gaps, with an expert harness and empirical ceiling estimates contextualizing scores. Stored trajectories make intermediate predictions verifiable, while agent-play experiments test whether world-model capabilities support decision-making. The main panel comprises eleven frontier language models. Composite benchmark scores correlate with real-world forecasting leaderboards on matched model panels, more closely than with a general-capability index, supporting its use as a proxy for real-world forecasting capability. Strong association forecasts do not consistently extend to belief inference or intervention prediction, and effect magnitudes remain poorly calibrated despite informative direction predictions. Process verification reveals errors missed by final-answer evaluation, and structured reasoning improves intervention prediction for the strongest model in the process study. Agent-play experiments identify useful assisted plans and motivate evaluating decision-relevant capabilities beyond association forecasting. These findings identify hidden-state inference, intermediate-state prediction, and effect calibration as priorities for world-model training.

papers.title: StructZO: Structured Zeroth-Order Optimization for Memory-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models at scale is increasingly limited by the memory cost of backpropagation. Zeroth-Order (ZO) optimizers reduce this burden by relying only on forward function evaluations, but they still exhibit a substantial performance gap to first-order (FO) optimizers such as Adam. We argue that this gap does not arise solely from the absence of explicit gradients: FO fine-tuning also benefits from informative low-rank optimization geometry, large-scale signal aggregation, and well-conditioned update directions. Motivated by this, we introduce StructZO, a structured Zeroth-Order optimization framework for memory-efficient LLM fine-tuning. StructZO performs large-query ZO estimation within an activation-induced informative subspace and applies spectral control to the resulting reduced-space update before mapping it back to the original parameters. This lets ZO aggregate useful directional signals in a compact, geometry-aware space while avoiding the activation and optimizer-state memory costs of backpropagation. We show theoretically that, when the induced subspace captures concentrated optimization-relevant directions, StructZO reduces the effective ZO estimation dimension from $mn$ to $mr$, with the remaining projection error governed by the spectral tail of the activation Gram matrix. Empirically, across OPT-series and Llama3.1-8B on diverse downstreamtasks, StructZO improves over the strongest existing ZO baselines by up to $8.7%$ relative on average and up to $26.9%$ relative on individual tasks, while remaining within $1.5%$ of FO-Adam on average. These results suggest that structured and spectrally controlled ZO updates can substantially narrow the gap between ZO and FO optimization.

papers.title: Not Every Cue Is Evidence: Cue Supportability for Forensic Distillation in Face Forgery Detection
papers.abstract: Explainable face forgery detection requires not only correct judgments but also forensic evidence supported by the input image. However, training cues are typically derived from the forgery generation pipeline. Since images available to the model are of limited quality and resolution, it is difficult to observe the fine-grained traces these cues refer to. Training methods that further supply such cues as privileged supervision exacerbate the problem, as the student is taught to articulate evidence it cannot perceive. The student consequently resorts to templated or over-generalized expressions, giving rise to the correct-answer, wrong-evidence (CAWE) failure. We propose a dual supportability audit that filters privileged cues before distillation. Each candidate cue must be predictable from the remaining privileged context and causally tied to high-attribution visual regions in the current image. Only cues satisfying both conditions receive substantial distillation weight, preventing unsupported details from leaking into the student. Experiments across eight benchmarks show that our method maintains or improves detection accuracy while significantly raising explanation faithfulness compared to existing paradigms.

papers.title: SiO Maser Line-width Diagnostics of AGB Stars and Red Supergiants: The RSG-adjacent Region in the FWZI--Luminosity Plane
papers.abstract: We investigate whether SiO maser line profiles can distinguish asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars from red supergiants (RSGs) and identify unusual AGB-classified sources near the RSG regime. We compiled 2,956 detected SiO maser spectra for 1,551 objects and constructed reference samples of 1,068 O-rich AGB stars and 36 RSGs. The full width at zero intensity (FWZI) was reliably measured for 1,020 AGB stars and 32 RSGs. AGB stars are concentrated at narrow line widths: 81.5% have FWZI <10 km s^-1, whereas 81.2% of RSGs have FWZI >15 km s^-1 and none has FWZI <10 km s^-1. Infrared two-color diagrams provide only partial separation. Combining FWZI with luminosities based primarily on quality-filtered Gaia/Bailer-Jones distances, with independent literature distances for several RSGs, reveals a weak tendency for wider SiO maser lines at higher luminosities but no clean boundary. We therefore define an empirical RSG-adjacent region in the FWZI-luminosity plane, 15 <= FWZI <= 26.6 km s^-1 and 3.9 <= log(L/L_sun) <= 4.9, to characterize the high-luminosity, broad-line tail of the AGB-classified sample. Ten sources fall within this region. Using infrared SEDs, DUSTY fits, OH/H2O maser information, and variability, we find that six are most naturally interpreted as luminous AGB-like objects, two warrant follow-up to assess possible high-initial-mass AGB, RSG-like, or SAGB-related interpretations, and two are less securely constrained because of poor DUSTY fits. The RSG-adjacent region is therefore a physically mixed screening space, not a definitive classification box, for selecting high-priority follow-up targets.

papers.title: Axioms and internal rigidity of spectral duality structures
papers.abstract: Spectral duality structures (SDS) explain why a distinguished family of initial distributions makes the absorption probabilities of resetting processes insensitive to the resetting mechanism. Here we study their axioms. We prove that the six defining conditions are mutually independent and determine what each one contributes. The key tool is a structure theorem valid for an arbitrary permutation and an arbitrary positive weight: every insensitive distribution is supported on a union of cycles balanced at a common level, and the level of a cycle is fixed by the geometric mean of the weight on it. From it, positivity selects the admissible root, the constant orbit product is equivalent to the existence of an insensitive distribution of full support, and the involution is equivalent to the response rank being equal to the number of free weight parameters. Without the duality relation, insensitivity of a single distribution is cheap and generically isolated; duality turns it into structural neutrality of the separatrix. The full-rank condition splits into two layers: a weaker condition is equivalent to maximal response rank, while full rank also excludes insensitivity at any other level. We then show that a single SDS is internally rigid: compatible semigroup structures force a constant weight, compatible abelian group structures obey a precise arithmetic condition, congruences form a simple lattice, and the automorphism group is computed explicitly. Finally, the axioms do not determine the orientation of the response; in the two-site case we give the exact condition under which the geometric and analytic sign criteria agree.

papers.title: GHOST: Geometry-Constrained Hybrid Diffusion for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graph Generation
papers.abstract: 3D scene graph generation requires understanding both object semantics and metric spatial relations. However, existing open-vocabulary methods often struggle with spatial predicates because language similarity reflects semantic co-occurrence rather than explicit geometry. We propose GHOST, a Geometry-constrained Hybrid diffusion framework for Open-vocabulary 3D Scene graph generaTion. GHOST jointly models continuous node geometry and discrete edge predicates, following a geometry-to-constraint-to-predicate denoising process to ensure geometrically consistent relation prediction. It introduces language-grounded constraint induction, which maps predicate embeddings to differentiable geometric constraints that guide both layout refinement and predicate reweighting. A Geometry-Topology Collaborative Denoiser further couples node and edge reasoning through noise-adaptive interaction and orientation-aware modeling. Experiments on 3DSSG demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both closed-set and open-vocabulary settings, including over 17-point gains over RelationField on spatial predicates.

papers.title: A temporal graph dissimilarity measure capturing epidemic spreading behavior
papers.abstract: Comparing temporal networks is a challenging problem in network analysis. Commonly adopted methods compare structural properties of temporal graphs and can be highly sensitive to the pre-selected features. However, temporal networks are the support of dynamical processes, and a process may take place in statistically indistinguishable ways on structurally different temporal graphs. In particular, a dissimilarity measure that compares temporal graphs based on how spreading processes unfold on them is highly desirable. In this work, we first define the Time-Shift DTW, a dissimilarity between epidemic curves that accounts for both differences in their shape and temporal shifts. We then introduce Epidemic-Aware Temporal Graph Dissimilarity (EATGD), a deterministic and differentiable dissimilarity between temporal graphs that combines an embedding-based temporal graph distance with a set of topological and temporal features. Its parameters are calibrated using stochastic SIR simulations to maximize the correlation with the Time-Shift DTW, after which graph comparisons require no further epidemic simulations. Using empirical human proximity networks from the SocioPatterns collaboration and synthetic temporal graphs, we show that EATGD captures epidemic-based graph dissimilarity and generalizes across heterogeneous network settings. Its differentiability and computational efficiency make EATGD suitable for integration into machine-learning pipelines and provide a potential loss function for training generative models to reproduce epidemic dynamics without requiring an exact reconstruction of fine-grained network structure.

papers.title: SHOES: Sim-to-real Hardware-adaptation via On-policy Expansion of Skills for Legged Robots
papers.abstract: Humans expand their locomotion capability by wearing appropriate footwear, such as hiking boots for mountains or skates for ice. Footwear changes the ground-contact interface and enables traversal of otherwise difficult terrain. In contrast, locomotion controllers are typically trained for a fixed morphology, and their performance can degrade when shoes alter foot geometry, mass, and friction. We propose SHOES, a sample-efficient framework for adapting locomotion policies to footwear-induced morphology changes. SHOES freezes a simulation-trained nominal policy and fine-tunes only lightweight, identity-initialized modulation modules on the robot, preserving the initial behavior while enabling efficient hardware adaptation. We also introduce SafeBox, a workspace-aware waypoint sampler that constrains online adaptation within a user-defined workspace. The simulation results with a shoe-equipped Unitree Go2 show that SHOES substantially recovers locomotion performance after footwear-induced morphology changes using limited additional adaptation. Under the same adaptation budget, SHOES outperforms FiLM-only, Linear Adapter-only, and residual-RL baselines. Real-world experiments on a Unitree Go2 fitted with human shoes further evaluate the effectiveness of SHOES for hardware deployment.

papers.title: Differential Privacy Protected Preference Alignment on Survey Derived Data
papers.abstract: Preference alignment enables language models to better reflect human values, but the preference data contains sensitive information, especially when derived from surveys about political beliefs, social norms, religion, gender attitudes, and cultural values. This paper studies privacy-preserving alignment on questionnaire-derived data from the World Values Survey, where supervision takes the form of ordinal labels rather than standard pairwise rankings. Existing efforts mainly focus on general privacy protections upon model training, while data-specific methods for survey data remain unexplored. We first show the vulnerability of aligned models, then formulate the task as rating prediction and introduce label differential privacy. Building on this formulation, we construct a differential private pipeline utilizing three privacy mechanisms: randomized response, exponential mechanism, and DP-SGD. Experiments show that simple label-level mechanisms outperform gradient-level methods, and proper aggregation function for preprocessing also make large contribution. The new fine-grained private comparison motivates explorations toward language model alignment with formal privacy guarantees.

papers.title: Edge and spectral conditions for rainbow bipancyclicity in bipartite graph collections
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{2n}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct balanced bipartite graphs of order $2n$ with a common bipartition $V=(X,Y)$. A cycle $C$ with $V(C)\subseteq V$ and $|E(C)|\leq 2n$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $φ\colon E(C)\to [2n]$ such that $e\in E(G_{φ(e)})$ for each $e\in E(C)$. The graph collection $\mathbf{G}$ is said to be \emph{rainbow bipancyclic} if it contains a rainbow cycle of every even length from 4 to $2n$. In this paper, we show that if $e(G_i)\ge n^2-n+1$ for each $i\in[2n]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ is rainbow bipancyclic unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{2n}\cong B_{n}^1$, where $B_{n}^1$ is the graph obtained from $K_{n,n}$ by deleting all edges in its one subgraph $K_{n-1,1}$. As a corollary, we obtain that if $ρ(G_i)\ge ρ(B_{n}^1)>\sqrt{n(n-1)}$ for each $i\in[2n]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ is rainbow bipancyclic unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{2n}\cong B_{n}^1$, which strengthens Theorem $5$ of [Electron. J. Combin., \textbf{33}(3)(2026), \#P3.29] and Theorem $1.6$ of [Linear Algebra Appl., \textbf{743}(2026), 250--270] from rainbow Hamiltonicity to rainbow bipancyclicity. We also characterize all bipartite graph collections that are not rainbow bipancyclic under the condition $ρ(G_i)\ge \sqrt{n(n-1)}$ for each $i\in[2n]$

papers.title: The interpreter as developer: An autoethnographic design study of building a computer-assisted interpreting tool through human-LLM co-creation
papers.abstract: Real-time AI captioning now serves audiences at multilingual events, yet computer-assisted interpreting (CAI) tools are still built for interpreters, rarely by them. This article reports an autoethnographic design study in which a professional interpreter with no programming training built a local-first CAI system through expert-led 'vibe coding', co-creating with an LLM architect and a coding agent. Analysis of the complete development dialogues shows how tacit professional knowledge, from segmentation to booth infrastructure, was externalized into design after generic defaults failed in use. In a demanding public scientific event, three mechanisms of in-booth appropriation emerge under a firmly human-led division of labor; telemetry from a first fully instrumented assignment shows a fully local chain sustaining a median translation latency of 0.94 s across 971 utterances. The case is read as lead-user innovation newly enabled by generative AI, with implications for the technological literacy of interpreters and the future of interpreter training.

papers.title: On the Weyl tube formula for nonlocal perimeters
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the nonlocal perimeter of tubular neighbourhoods. For a closed $C^{1,1}$ submanifold of Euclidean space, we show that a suitable rescaling of the nonlocal perimeter of its tube converges to an explicit constant times the Hausdorff measure of the submanifold. The constant is the fractional perimeter of the unit ball in the codimension of the submanifold. For finite point sets, we obtain an exact tube formula in terms of a generalised hypergeometric function. In contrast with the classical Weyl formula, this expansion has infinitely many terms, contains both noninteger and integer powers of the tubular radius, and has coefficients that depend on the relative positions of the points rather than only on their intrinsic geometry. We also establish a point-set expansion for general analytic kernels.

papers.title: Photon echo from Maki-Thompson interference in a fluctuating s-wave superconductor
papers.abstract: We study theoretically the nonlinear optical response of a fluctuating s-wave superconductor driven by two successive terahertz pulses. We show that the response exhibits a photon echo signal that arises from the quantum interference between the time-reversed electron and hole trajectories in the Maki-Thompson process. By contrast, the transport of the fluctuating Cooper pairs responsible for the Aslamazov-Larkin conductivity does not generate an echo. The photon echo signal can be readily measured using terahertz two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy, highlighting its potential to distinguish different fluctuation conductivity mechanisms.

papers.title: DeTac: Dual-branch Decoupling of Texture and Force Signals in Vision-Based Tactile Sensors
papers.abstract: Vision-based tactile sensors enable fine-grained perception for dexterous robotic manipulation, but current marker-based designs tightly couple surface texture and contact force signals within a single observation. Existing data-driven decoupling methods rely on serial mask-based inpainting, which suffers from mask-sizing dilemmas caused by physical indentation effects, error retention, and lack of real paired data for supervision. To address these challenges, we propose DeTac, a novel dual-branch generative framework that concurrently extracts clean shading and marker images from a single mixed tactile image. DeTac leverages full-image synthesis to naturally bypass mask dependency and introduces a cross-branch synergistic optimization that enables mutual supervision, effectively preventing error retention. Furthermore, we construct a strictly aligned, real-world paired tactile dataset using custom hardware to provide high-quality supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DeTac achieves state-of-the-art decoupling accuracy, significantly facilitating downstream surface reconstruction and force estimation tasks while exhibiting cross-sensor generalization.

papers.title: Online Individualized Treatment Selection under Partial Feedback: False Discovery Control and Minimax Optimality
papers.abstract: We study online individualized treatment selection when only the outcome under the assigned treatment is observed. Our objective is to preferentially treat individuals whose potential outcomes under treatment exceed a covariate-specific control reference, while limiting false discoveries among treated individuals. We propose Partial-Feedback Adaptive Individualized Treatment Selection (PAITS), which initializes learning from historical data and combines sequential estimation of local null risks, randomized exploration, and feedback-driven updates of the treatment selection threshold. Under regularity conditions, we establish asymptotic false discovery rate control and sublinear gap-weighted assignment regret relative to a population oracle. We further establish a minimax lower bound on assignment regret under prescribed uniform nuisance-estimation requirements and give conditions under which PAITS attains the corresponding constrained minimax rate up to logarithmic factors. These results quantify the tradeoff between accurate treatment assignment and nuisance learning under partial feedback. Simulation studies and a real-data analysis using the Jester recommendation dataset illustrate the finite-sample performance of PAITS.

papers.title: Teaching Vision-Language Models to Decline: Support Completion Against Mirage
papers.abstract: Vision-language models answer questions about images they were never shown, a failure called mirage. Such an answer can be correct without being justified by the evidence, and the difference matters wherever a model's output is checked by someone who did not see its input. We locate the failure in the training objective: cross-entropy separates a model that reads the image from one that ignores it by only the conditional mutual information between answer and image, and no training example rewards declining. We formalise support completion, TIDE, which also shows each training question with a blank image, a same-domain wrong image and an out-of-domain image, with targets that decline, and prove that under TIDE every image-blind predictor is suboptimal by at least 1.04 nats per example, that the optimum declines exactly on the counterfactual kinds while keeping its behaviour on valid images, and that for any finite model the error of its answer-or-decline decision, declining on valid input plus answering on invalid input, is bounded below by how well its representation separates valid from invalid evidence. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B under a frozen held-out protocol with two judges, the three-condition predecessor of TIDE reduced the invalid-evidence mirage rate from 0.759 to 0.097 and the blank-image rate from 0.700 to 0.003 at a false-abstention cost of 0.126; label-free grounding raised the rate to 0.859, a likelihood-advantage contrast moved it only to 0.718 because its empty-image term carries no gradient, and grounding applied after support completion re-opened the mirage. The four-condition protocol on three base models, with seeds and component ablations, is in progress and not reported here.

papers.title: PATMT2: Two-stage domain adaptation for multilingual patent translation
papers.abstract: We present PatMT2 (Patent Machine Translation, v2), a two-stage LoRA pipeline that adapts the Hy-MT2-7B dedicated translation model to four-language (Chinese/English/Japanese/Korean) patent translation. On six translation directions, the Stage-2 checkpoint reaches a macro-average BLEU of 43.39 (BF16) to 43.57 (AWQ INT4), improving over the Hy-MT2-7B base by up to +8.8 BLEU and also exceeding Qwen3-32B and several external systems on the same average. We then measure the cost of adaptation: probing 38 languages absent from the fine-tuning data, the model still produces correct, fluent output on 34, while four low-resource languages collapse into distinct, reproducible failure modes. We treat these as diagnostic cases rather than retention rates, and report their mechanisms without attributing them to a single cause. Paired bootstrap tests confirm the translation gains over all baselines (p < 0.001).

papers.title: Modelling the dynamics of the martensitic transformation in Ni$_2$MnGa with machine-learning force-fields
papers.abstract: The martensitic transformations in stoichiometric Ni$_2$MnGa and related Heusler alloys are governed by a delicate interplay between electronic structure, magnetism, and lattice dynamics. While density functional theory (DFT) has successfully mapped the energy landscape of modulated martensites, it remains computationally prohibitive for capturing finite-temperature dynamics across relevant length and time scales. Here, we bridge this gap by constructing DFT-trained machine-learning force-fields (ML-FF) interpolated from ab initio molecular dynamics. We demonstrate that ML-FF trained on DFT data can reproduce key features of Ni$_2$MnGa, including the soft TA$_2$ phonon and a preference for nanotwinned martensites. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we explore the impact of adaptive nanotwinning on the austenite-martensite transition, which facilitates the dynamics of both, forward and backward transformation. We demonstrate, that the negative twin boundary energy along the entire transformations path predicted by DFT for $T=0$, supports the formation of ordered modulated martensites at finite temperatures. Our results pave the way for large-scale simulations of magnetic shape memory alloys with near-DFT accuracy.

papers.title: Deterministic positioning accuracy of B centers in hBN by electron irradiation
papers.abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is a promising material platform for quantum technologies, enabling both the realization of nanophotonic devices and the hosting of point defects that act as high-quality single-photon emitters (SPEs). Among these defects, B centers, which reproducibly emit at 436 nm, can be generated individually at predefined positions using electron beam irradiation, a crucial capability for top-down quantum photonics. Yet, the spatial accuracy of emitter creation strongly conditions the potential applications. Here, we generate arrays of individual B centers in a scanning electron microscope (SEM) with in-situ cathodoluminescence (CL) monitoring. We characterize the sources of random deviations from the target positions to identify the limitations to their deterministic positioning. In particular, we measure the distance between the electron beam and the emitter at the moment the emitter is created based on CL mapping. This approach provides a direct estimation of the spatial extent of the beam-emitter interaction. We find this contribution to be the main constraint to the emitter fabrication accuracy, yielding a standard deviation of 27 nm. Additional contributions, primarily from the finite density of UV-emitting carbon dimer precursors, increase the overall positional standard deviation to 40 nm. Our results highlight the possible improvements to the B center creation technique to reach sub-10 nm accuracy.

papers.title: Foresee: Making Procedural Futures Tangible through Generative Previews
papers.abstract: Procedural guidance can show users how to act without explaining what an action enables later. We present Foresee, an interface combining next-step guidance with consequence previews, method comparisons, and cross-step access. A hybrid pipeline combines structured rendering, image editing, and video generation. A literature-informed framework and six-participant formative study shaped its design. A 24-participant study compared AR guidance, AR with generated video, and Foresee across digital painting, gameplay, and cocktail making. Exploratory painting comparisons showed higher correct completion without a recorded error than AR and higher post-task quiz accuracy than generated-video guidance under task-wise correction. Interviews revealed that users could overlook valued explanations, match visible outcomes without understanding later possibilities, or wait for concrete demonstrations when symbolic cues were unclear. These findings inform generative previews that explain what actions enable or constrain while supporting ongoing execution.

papers.title: CircuitBreak: Pruning a Sparse Safety Circuit of Neurons
papers.abstract: White-box neuron pruning has shown that refusal in large language models (LLMs) can depend on a small, removable set of feed-forward (FFN) channels. Existing attacks either need carefully paired ``twin'' prompts or score each neuron in isolation. Pruning also has an unavoidable capability cost, so over-removal compounds the loss. TwinBreak removes $1\%$--$5\%$ of parameters and NeuroStrike removes $0.3\%$--$0.7\%$ of neurons in targeted layers. We model safety as a small \emph{circuit} whose neurons contribute jointly rather than independently. We propose \textsc{CircuitBreak}, a neuron-pruning attack that greedily searches for a sparse set of FFN neurons whose joint ablation flips a refusal readout. \textsc{CircuitBreak} re-scores every candidate after the neurons already removed and needs no twin prompts. On ten instruction-tuned models, the greedy search converges after removing $29$--$150$ neurons ($0.0066\%$--$0.0388\%$ of the MLP). The pruned models raise the attack success rate from $2.24\%$/$7.35\%$ to $87.54\%$/$87.54\%$ on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and from $8.95\%$/$5.43\%$ to $88.50\%$/$88.18\%$ on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, as judged by Llama Guard 3 8B on StrongREJECT.

papers.title: Auditing Observation-Quality Shortcuts in the Evaluation of Person-Centered Motion for Video Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Video anomaly detection (VAD) identifies deviations from normal patterns, but such deviations do not necessarily correspond to safety-critical events. We focus on human-centered emergencies and violence and investigate whether motion-based anomaly discrimination reflects task-relevant motion information or observation-quality differences arising from person detection, pose estimation, and tracking. We introduce an observation-quality-aware evaluation framework that combines quality diagnostics, quality balancing, motion orthogonalization, and robustness analyses. On human-centered categories of UCF-Crime, quality-only features match or exceed the discrimination of multi-cue motion in the original cohort, revealing a strong observation-quality shortcut. After cardinality matching brings all 11 measured quality variables below a prespecified marginal balance threshold, multi-cue motion consistently outperforms quality-only features across Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and RBF-SVM, yielding ROC-AUC gains of 0.046-0.141. Because nonlinear quality-only prediction remains above chance after matching, we interpret this result as additional discrimination beyond measured marginal quality rather than as evidence of quality-free or causal motion understanding. These findings show that high VAD performance should not be interpreted as evidence of abnormal-motion modeling without auditing the reliability of the person-observation pipeline. Our study provides a systematic protocol for evaluating observation-quality shortcuts and for assessing whether motion-based discrimination survives explicit control of detection, pose-estimation, and tracking reliability.

papers.title: Representation dependence of the neutron-proton kinetic energy in adiabatic deuteron stripping
papers.abstract: Deuteron stripping reactions such as (d,p) are a main tool for studying the single-particle structure of nuclei, and they are usually analyzed with the adiabatic distorted-wave approximation (ADWA). With nonlocal nucleon optical potentials, ADWA cross sections change by tens of percent, up to a factor of two, depending on which realistic neutron-proton interaction describes the deuteron. Continuum-discretized calculations change much less, and exact Faddeev calculations reduce the spread by about a factor of ten. Should this sensitivity be read as a probe of neutron-proton physics at short distances? One identified route for it in ADWA is a single number, the neutron-proton kinetic energy averaged over the region where the two nucleons interact. I change the AV18 interaction only at short distances, keeping neutron-proton scattering, the deuteron binding energy, and the long-range tail of the deuteron unchanged. This number then rises from 218 to 314 MeV, more than half of its spread among five realistic interactions, while the coefficient that sets the low-momentum shape of the form factor moves by only one percent of its realistic range. The number therefore reflects how the interaction is written, not anything measured. It enters ADWA through two features that the other calculations treat differently: ADWA weights the deuteron where the two nucleons are close, and it assigns the deuteron energy to the pair however fast the two nucleons move. For this short-range change, an average that keeps the full Gaussian shape of the nonlocal potential, instead of expanding it to lowest order, rises by only 6 MeV against 96 MeV.

papers.title: Some complete $ω$-powers of a one-counter language in the difference hierarchy
papers.abstract: Fix a finite alphabet $Σ$ having at least two letters, and natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$. We denote by $D_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$ the class of differences of $n$ subsets of the Cantor space $Σ^ω$ in $\mathbfΠ0_k$, and by $D_n-(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$ the class of complements of sets in $D_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$. We prove, for any natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$, the existence of a finite alphabet $Σ$ having at least two letters and a finitary language $U_{n,k}$ over $Σ$ accepted by a one-counter automaton such that the $ω$-power $$U_{n,k}^\infty:={ w_0w_1\cdots\inΣ^ω\mid\forall i\inω~~w_i\in U_{n,k}}$$ is $D_{2n-1}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$-complete. We also prove a conditional result for the dual classes $D^-_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$: under the assumption that there exists a finitary language $V_{n,3}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $ω$-power $V_{n,3}^\infty$ is $D^-_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_3)$-complete, there would also exist, for any integer $k>3$, a finitary language $V_{n,k}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $ω$-power $V_{n,k}^\infty$ is $D^-_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$-complete. Finally we add another conditionnal result about Wadge degrees of rational $\mathbfΔ^0_2$ omega powers, which completes the recent results of [FGL26].

papers.title: Ontology-Based Post-Coordinated Expression Assembly: from Clinical Narrative to Queryable Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract: Clinical oncology documentation records decisive information in free text, where it remains readable but not retrievable at scale, leaving cohort identification dependent on incomplete diagnostic codes or manual review. The current standard, coding individual terms, captures what a document mentions, not what it asserts: meaning lies in how those terms relate to one another. We present a method for deriving queryable knowledge graphs from clinical narratives, conforming to the Extended Grammar of SNOMED CT across multiple ontologies. The method specifies how entities should be annotated and related. It defines five relation classes, each bound to a construction rule that assembles the entities and relations into post-coordinated expressions. A deterministic implementation, UNIGRAPHE, applies those rules to construct knowledge graphs from annotated text. Applied to expert-annotated real-world oncology documentation, UNIGRAPHE reconstructed 5,299 annotations into 2,196 post-coordinated expressions and shows that relation structure is the missing piece to make clinical narrative formally queryable.

papers.title: Remarks on ultrafilters exponentiation
papers.abstract: Recently, two exponentiations of ultrafilters have been introduced in [7]. We rephrase them in nonstandard terms, and use the nonstandard formulations to characterize some of their properties. We also study their relations with divisibility by introducing factor-picking functions and highly exponential ultrafilters.

papers.title: Schatten--Lorentz properties of commutators with matrix weights
papers.abstract: We study the membership of commutators $[b,T]$ of Calderón--Zygmund operators in the Schatten--Lorentz classes in the matrix-weighted setting. Working on a space of homogeneous type $(X,ρ,μ)$ with a matrix $A_2$ weight $W$, we characterise, for $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $q\in[1,\infty)$, the Schatten--Lorentz norm $\|[b,T]\|_{S^{p,q}(L^2(W))}$ in terms of an oscillation (Besov-type) norm $\|b\|_{\mathrm{Osc}^{p,q}}$ of the symbol: for all $p\in(1,\infty)$, finiteness of $\|b\|_{\mathrm{Osc}^{p,q}}$ is necessary; and for $p>p(η)$, where $p(η)$ depends on the regularity of the kernel of $T$ and a dimensional parameter of the space, the two-sided estimate $\|[b,T]\|_{S^{p,q}(L^2(W))}\approx\|b\|_{\mathrm{Osc}^{p,q}}$ holds. Extending a recent unified framework for unweighted and scalar-weighted versions of such results by one of us to the matrix-weighted setting, our approach combines the dyadic representation of singular integral operators with the nearly weakly orthogonal (NWO) sequences of Rochberg and Semmes.

papers.title: CALIPER: Calibrating HPC/AI Network Simulators
papers.abstract: Network simulation plays an important role in HPC/AI system research by enabling exploration of network architectures, communication strategies, and system configurations at scales that may be impractical to study experimentally. Existing approaches to network simulator calibration and validation lack a principled methodology that combines parameter alignment, constrained inference, and independent validation for collective-centric HPC/AI networks. We present CALIPER, a methodology for systematic calibration and validation of HPC/AI network simulators. CALIPER distinguishes directly observable system parameters from auxiliary parameters which are configured via calibration and constrains the latter to feasible domains consistent with the target system. We evaluate CALIPER's hierarchical, scale-aware calibration and its effects on parameter identifiability and generalization using collective communication benchmarks on a reference system with up to 64-nodes at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre. Validation results show that the calibrated parameter configurations identified by CALIPER predict system performance with less than 5% mean errors across scale-up and scale-out network domains. CALIPER demonstrates that hierarchical, constrained calibration can produce simulator configurations whose predictive accuracy persists beyond the observations used for fitting.

papers.title: XAI-Guided Fourier Domain Generalisation for Pure-Simulation Sim-to-Real Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning has shown strong potential for vision-based autonomous driving, but policies trained in simulation often suffer severe performance degradation when deployed in the real world. Existing sim-to-real methods commonly address this gap through image-transfer-based domain adaptation or policy-agnostic domain randomisation. However, the former requires laborious acquisition of target-domain data and is often limited to the deployment domain, whereas the latter introduces unguided perturbations that may not reflect the underlying sim-to-real discrepancy, leading to suboptimal transfer performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose XFD, an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-guided Fourier domain generalisation framework for pure-simulation sim-to-real reinforcement learning. The proposed framework extracts explainability attribution maps from simulated observations, and converts these attributions into policy-conditioned Fourier-domain interventions. By perturbing appearance-sensitive spectral components while preserving task-defining spatial structures, XFD constructs robustness-enhancing visual domains entirely within simulation. Subsequently, the proposed robust policy optimisation guides the policy towards attending to task-critical features while suppressing sensitivity to irrelevant visual information. Extensive experiments in simulation and zero-shot real-world deployment demonstrate that XFD consistently improves traveled distance and reward over standard policy and randomly domain-randomised baseline, especially on unseen maps with cluttered backgrounds. Attribution-based analysis further proves that the proposed policy preserves more consistent task-relevant visual evidence across simulation and real-world observations.

papers.title: Asynchronous Terahertz-field sampling with soliton microcombs
papers.abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy records the electric field of terahertz transients and underpins applications from materials science to non-destructive testing. Asynchronous optical sampling enables systems without moving parts, but its acquisition rate remains fundamentally limited by the repetition-rate of the driving femtosecond lasers. Here, we demonstrate asynchronous terahertz-field sampling with two chip-based soliton microcombs. Their ultrahigh 25 GHz pulse repetition-rate drastically reduces dead-time during acquisition, and stabilization via sideband injection-locking enables coherent averaging without active feedback loops. At 10 kHz acquisition rate, we achieve a dynamic range of 74 dB in a single 100 $μ$s scan, and 100 dB after 50 ms of coherent averaging with a 1.6 THz bandwidth. Acquisition rates of up to 100 kHz are demonstrated, limited only by detection electronics. Together with a proof-of-concept silicon wafer thickness measurement, these results establish soliton microcombs as compact sources for rapid terahertz-field sampling.

papers.title: PXRD-Bench: How Close Are We to Determining Crystal Structures from Powder Diffraction?
papers.abstract: Determining crystal structures from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) would enable routine characterization of newly synthesized materials, including those absent from reference databases. Generative models offer a promising approach, but existing evaluations remain fragmented and largely assume single-phase samples with known composition. To fill this gap, we introduce PXRD-Bench, a unified benchmark that extends evaluation to unknown per-element atom counts and recovery of both structures in two-phase mixtures. It provides approximately 4.1 million training structures with simulated PXRD, tests generalization to unseen compositions and structural prototypes, and evaluates recovery from experimental PXRD after excluding structurally matching training entries. To provide a strong reference baseline, we also introduce Bragglite, a PXRD-to-structure model developed through a systematic study of PXRD modeling choices. It achieves a 44.2\% Top-1 match rate on experimental RRUFF patterns with known composition, 24.6\% above the strongest prior baseline. Further analysis yields several key findings: some models fail to benefit from experimental PXRD, while generalization to unseen structural prototypes and recovery from two-phase mixtures remain challenging. Together, our benchmark, systematic studies, and Bragglite clarify the capabilities and limitations of current PXRD-to-structure models.

papers.title: Quantum state texture of maximal-resource Fourier states under Hawking radiation
papers.abstract: Quantum state texture (QST) is a recently proposed quantum resource that characterizes the nonuniformity of a density matrix in a given computational basis. In the resource theory of QST, the Fourier states f_k are maximally resourceful states, attaining the maximum QST measure. We study the QST behavior of three maximally resourceful states in a two-mode Dirac field under Hawking radiation from a Schwarzschild black hole, using a fidelity-based measure. We consider three cases: only mode B undergoes radiation, only mode A undergoes radiation, and both modes undergo radiation simultaneously. Our results show that for single-mode radiation, if the mode unaffected by radiation is orthogonal to the single-mode textureless state, the QST of the overall output state remains maximal and is independent of the Hawking temperature; we call this phenomenon orthogonality protection. When both modes undergo radiation simultaneously, orthogonality protection vanishes, and the QST of all three Fourier states decreases with increasing Hawking temperature. Notably, the QST measure of f_3 under two-mode radiation is higher than that under only mode B radiation, indicating that QST can be redistributed among modes: QST gained by one mode under radiation can partially compensate for QST lost by the other. We further provide a general resource-theoretic explanation of orthogonality protection, showing that this phenomenon is independent of the specific form of the QST measure. These results reveal how QST degrades under Hawking radiation and provide a new perspective on the redistribution of quantum resources in black hole backgrounds.

papers.title: MiMaAlign: Hierarchical Micro-Macro Alignment for Physically Plausible Video Generation
papers.abstract: Text-to-video (T2V) diffusion models have made remarkable progress in generating high-fidelity visuals, yet their outputs still often exhibit physically implausible phenomena, including discontinuous dynamics and implausible event interactions. Existing representation alignment methods mainly transfer generic video features or short-range motion cues, treating physical plausibility as a single-level representation problem. To address this issue, we propose MiMaAlign, a hierarchical micro-macro alignment framework that transfers complementary dynamics-oriented and event-oriented knowledge into different abstraction depths of a pretrained video diffusion model. Specifically, micro-level continuous dynamics alignment imposes constraints by aligning diffusion features with a continuous-time motion representation learned by a Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (Neural ODE), while macro-level event-commonsense alignment provides representations of object interactions and event semantics through an instruction-prompted vision-language model (VLM). With training-only auxiliary objectives, we align the complementary supervision from the two teachers with shallower and deeper generator features, respectively, enabling the generator to internalize the corresponding physical priors. Empirical evaluations show that, on CogVideoX-2B, MiMaAlign achieves a relative improvement of up to 21.0% in the Physical Commonsense (PC) score on the VideoPhy benchmark over the baseline, and also delivers substantial gains on the highly challenging VideoPhy2 benchmark, while maintaining general video quality on VBench and being supported by blind user comparisons.

papers.title: Molecule-intercalated van der Waals Josephson junctions uncover complex multiband superconductivity
papers.abstract: Intercalation of molecular species provides a route to tailor the electronic structure in van der Waals superconductors, yet intercalated compounds have rarely been integrated into phase-sensitive quantum devices. Here, we realize hybrid molecular Josephson junctions based on TaS2/NbSe2 heterostructures. Selective intercalation of the TaS2 electrode induces monolayer-like Ising superconductivity, while the junctions exhibit asymmetric Fraunhofer interference, field-induced and spontaneous Josephson diode effects. The zero-field diode disappears upon reversing the electrode stacking and re-emerges after intercalating the lower NbSe2 electrode. These findings indicate that the hybrid superconducting electrode hosts unconventional superconductivity underlying the nonreciprocal transport, while molecular intercalation acts as a tuning knob for its internal phase structure. This behavior is consistent with a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking multiband superconducting state characterized by a nontrivial relative phase between superconducting condensates. Our results establish hybrid molecular Josephson junctions as a quantum-device platform for phase-sensitive investigation and integration of molecularly engineered superconductors, opening opportunities to uncover and engineer unconventional superconducting phases.

papers.title: SLEM: Spectrum-Aware Latent Expert Merging
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models scale model capacity efficiently by activating only a small subset of experts for each input, while still requiring all parameters to be stored in memory, resulting in substantial memory overhead. Expert merging techniques have recently emerged as a promising compression paradigm that reduces this overhead by consolidating multiple experts into a smaller set. However, existing approaches have two key limitations: (i) direct convex interpolation in parameter space is not generally guaranteed to yield meaningful interpolation of expert functions; and (ii) estimating expert similarity or merging coefficients often relies on calibration data, introducing dependence on the calibration distribution. To address these limitations, we propose Spectrum-Aware Latent Expert Merging (SLEM), a calibration-free expert merging framework that occurs in a structured latent representation of expert weights using a VAE. SLEM groups experts within and across layers based on latent similarities and derives merging coefficients from expert weight spectra. It then performs geometry-aware latent interpolation and decodes the resulting representations into merged expert weights. Compared with existing expert merging methods, SLEM achieves comparable or better performance on general knowledge benchmarks and higher average performance on generation benchmarks involving mathematical reasoning and code generation.

papers.title: A geometric lower bound for the clamped plate eigenvalue problem in low dimensions and extensions
papers.abstract: We show that the spectrum of the Dirichlet-biLaplacian can be quantitatively bounded from below in terms of the inradius only, for a general open set in dimensions $2$ and $3$. For the same dimensions, we also extend this result to fractional powers $s$ of the Laplacian, with $N/2<s<2$. The resulting estimate comes with a constant having the correct asymptotic behavior as $s$ approaches the two endpoints $N/2$ and $2$. The proofs exploit capacitary techniques in the vein of Maz'ya.

papers.title: Poincaré inequalities, logarithmic growth and doubling
papers.abstract: We investigate when a Poincaré inequality forces the underlying measure to be doubling, with particular attention to the space \(X\) controlling the oscillation. We identify \(L\log L\) as the sharp threshold: under a natural local growth condition on the measure, doubling is forced precisely when \(L\log L(0,1)\not\hookrightarrow X\). We also obtain a doubling criterion under a weaker geometric assumption when the oscillation norm is sufficiently stronger than \(L\log L\). We show that this threshold is sharp in every fixed Euclidean dimension, using a dimension-free local \(L\log L\)-Poincaré inequality for log-concave measures and non-doubling Gaussian examples. We then turn to infinite-dimensional spaces, where doubling is impossible for the measures under consideration. Nevertheless, the \(L\log L\)-Poincaré inequality continues to hold, and we establish sharp characterizations for infinite product models, Gaussian measures on Hilbert spaces under power-type small-ball estimates, and Wiener measure with the uniform norm.

papers.title: The triangular metric on projective surfaces
papers.abstract: In \cite{ThurstonStretch} Thurston introduced stretch paths and stretch maps between hyperbolic surfaces. In this paper we extend similar constructions to the space of convex real projective structures on surfaces. Using Fock-Goncharov-like parameters, we introduce stretch paths and construct explicit stretch maps between the projective surface. We show that stretch maps are $e^t$--Lipschitz with respect to a triangular metric we introduce on the projective surface. This allows us to gain control on several length functions on an open set of the space of convex real projective structures (those where there is no ``local back--tracking"). As an application we obtain pointwise upper bounds for the Hilbert entropy of some convex real projective structures in terms of Fock-Goncharov-like parameters.

papers.title: Emergence of Nonlocal Hydrodynamics in Many-Body Radiative Heat Transport
papers.abstract: We develop a nonlocal hydrodynamic theory of radiative heat transport in many-body systems by coarse graining their microscopic electrodynamic interactions. Long-range radiative exchange naturally generates a spatially nonlocal constitutive relation in which the heat current at a given position depends on temperature gradients over an extended region, while energy conservation retains its local conservative form. Fourier transport emerges as a controlled long-wavelength limit when the interaction kernel has a finite second spatial moment. When this moment fails to converge, spatial nonlocality survives coarse graining and gives rise to non-Fourier transport. The resulting framework establishes a systematic bridge between discrete many-body fluctuational electrodynamics and a continuous description of radiative heat transport.

papers.title: A Multipatch Model for Evaluating Interdivisional Connectivity and Vaccination Dynamics in the 2026 Bangladesh Measles Outbreak
papers.abstract: The 2026 measles resurgence in Bangladesh motivates a spatial modelling framework that accounts for heterogeneous local transmission, vaccination activity, and interdivisional connectivity. We formulate a multipatch susceptible-vaccinated-infectious-recovered model for the eight administrative divisions of Bangladesh. Division-specific parameters are estimated from reported measles cases \cite{DGHS} and smoothed vaccination data using bounded nonlinear least squares, with uncertainty quantified through 1000 parametric bootstrap replicates. The fitted divisional systems are then connected through compartment-specific movement and cross-patch infection coefficients adjusted for connectivity and the source division's relative reproduction number. The fitted model captures the main division-specific epidemic patterns. Estimated local reproduction numbers range from \(1.1386\) in Khulna (95\% CI:\(0.5703\)--\(1.3834\)) to \(4.3491\) in Dhaka (95\% CI: \(1.4449\)--\(5.6307\)), while Chattogram also exhibits high transmission potential (\(\mathcal{R}_0^i=4.2275\); 95\% CI: \(4.0019\)--\(4.3185\)). Baseline spatial coupling increases the network-wide epidemic peak from \(190.96\) to \(313.20\) infectious individuals and more than doubles cumulative infections from \(1086.42\) to \(2345.35\). Relative to baseline coupling, 50\% and 80\% restrictions reduce the epidemic peak by \(26.69\%\) and \(34.37\%\), and cumulative infections by \(25.07\%\) and \(41.48\%\), respectively. Conversely, a 50\% increase in spatial coupling raises the peak by \(30.14\%\) and cumulative infections by \(23.54\%\). Although local transmission remains dominant in every division, cross-patch infection accounts for \(28.83\%\) of new infections in Rajshahi at the baseline epidemic peak. Source-sink analysis identifies Dhaka as the dominant cross-patch source and Chattogram as a smaller secondary source.

papers.title: Growing and Transferring Pathways for LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can substantially improve the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but an effective training run requires considerable resources. Reusing the computation acquired through RL across models would extend the value of that training. We propose GrowRL, an RL method that organizes learned updates into compact computational pathways through structural growth. GrowRL freezes the pretrained backbone and adds an independent causal attention branch and a feed-forward network branch at each Transformer layer. Zero-initialized output projections preserve the pretrained policy at initialization, and RL updates only the added pathways. The learned pathways remain explicit after training, allowing transfer to structurally compatible target models and subsequent adaptation with the target backbone frozen. The architecture also supports sequential transfer of additional pathways. By keeping the learned attention and feed-forward computation separate from the pretrained weights, GrowRL provides an explicit structure for preserving and reusing the outcome of an RL run. Experiments across five backbones show competitive mathematical reasoning and out-of-distribution performance with a small number of trainable parameters. Learned pathways provide immediate gains across all three transfer directions, with performance after only 10 target-side updates already close to that after 100 updates in every case. These results support computational pathways as parameter-efficient and reusable units of reinforcement learning adaptation.

papers.title: Communication, Vocalisation, and Language
papers.abstract: The contention is that the current batch of Large Language Models don't *understand* language, but they *do* it. Rather than LLMs forming some kind of ``distributed representation'' of symbols, the claim is that LLMs are capturing ``Cultural Intelligence'' and grounding symbols in what the sociologists call practices.

papers.title: Drafting Agents, Not Just Tokens: Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Systems
papers.abstract: Improving an agent through successive revisions requires balancing exploration and evaluation under a limited budget. A narrow search can miss useful sequences of edits, while fully evaluating every intermediate version often exhausts the budget before those sequences yield a verified improvement. Inspired by the draft--verify principle of speculative decoding, we propose Speculative Recursive Self-Improvement (SpecRSI), a two-level framework coupling inner-loop agent search with outer-loop improver learning. SpecRSI drafts successors before their predecessors are fully evaluated, while adopting only fully evaluated, admissible versions. In the inner loop, Verification-Aware Tree Search (VATS) allocates the budget between further edits and outstanding checks using the predicted verified return of a continuation. In the outer loop, Group Verification Optimization (GVO) updates the improver from completed searches while keeping the real evaluator fixed. We evaluate SpecRSI on scientific optimization (including active queue management (AQM) for network infrastructure), coding, and general agent-system benchmarks. Under matched evaluation-call budgets, SpecRSI improves scientific terminal gain over Janus by 60.0%--96.3% and area under the budget curve by 32.1%--91.6%, while achieving higher means across all 50 scientific backbone--task pairs and outperforming MetaRSI-v1 by 1.30--2.70 percentage points (pp) in system score across twenty backbones. On instance-level comparisons, it further improves PyBaMM terminal gain by 142.6% and SWE-Pro success by 6.0 pp at 7.0% and 9.2% lower token cost, respectively. These results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach.

papers.title: On the cyclic limiting behavior of the restarted Arnoldi algorithm for real symmetric matrices with restart length $s=2$
papers.abstract: We prove that the restarted Arnoldi algorithm for real symmetric matrices with restart length $s=2$ has a cyclic limiting behavior. In the terminology established in (arXiv:2209.14579), this is a proof of the ACI($s$) conjecture for $A=A^T\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and $s=2$. As explained in (arXiv:2209.14579), this also proves the Forsythe conjecture (Numerische Mathematik, 11 (1968), pp. 57-76) about the limiting behavior of the conjugate gradient method and positive definite $A=A^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ for $s=2$. The proof we give is an extensively rewritten and simplified version of a proof found using Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol. At the end of this paper, we discuss its origin and evolution, as well as related recent developments around the Forsythe conjecture. Our motivation is to present a proof that is instructive and transparent, so that it can enhance the knowledge of interested human readers.

papers.title: Bell's go theorem: regaining local causality with a new notion of realism
papers.abstract: Bell's theorem is popularly stated as the inconsistency of quantum theory with local realism. Realism is here formalized by the ontological models framework, where elements of reality are points of a measurable space and probabilities obey the Kolmogorov axioms. In the Bell scenario, locally causal ontological models posit a common cause supporting a global valuation, a joint assignment of outcomes to all measurements at once, across incompatible contexts. Within this notion of realism, Bell's theorem makes any realist explanation of the quantum predictions conspiratorial: any mechanism, whether superluminal, superdeterministic, or retrocausal, must be finely tuned so as never to manifest operationally. We redefine realism through a new ontological framework that generalizes the standard one. The elements of reality, which we call records, are no longer points but relational parts of a point-free generalization of a topological space (sublocales of a locale). A record shared by two incompatible contexts establishes the sameness of a measurement across them, without such pairwise identities composing into a global valuation, and the common cause is then a web of such records. Within this framework, Bell's no-go theorem becomes a go theorem: local causality, restated for records, is no longer at odds with the quantum statistics.
