We examined when they help and how this evidence can guide training using Brazilian Portuguese questions from medical and multiprofessional residency examinations. First, we measured how a teacher rationale changed the student's probability of selecting the correct answer and compared this effect with rationales drawn from other questions. The complete rationale increased this probability by 21~p.p. when the teacher was correct and decreased it by 14~p.p. when the teacher was wrong. By intervening on the reasoning content, we showed that shuffled rationales did not produce the same pattern. Guided by this result, we trained only with rationales attached to correct teacher answers and compared answer-only training, step-by-step distillation, and our proposed Distill-SFT method. Distill-SFT showed a modest advantage over step-by-step distillation on previously missed questions under reasoning, while using fewer training instances by combining the answer and rationale into a single target. We also investigated catastrophic forgetting using the out-of-domain ENEM dataset. Answer-only training reduced reasoning accuracy by 12~p.p. relative to baseline, compared with approximately 4~p.p. for either rationale-based training method. Together, these findings support a workflow that audits rationale content before distillation, verifies teacher answers before supervision, and trains compact models efficiently for health professions question answering.

papers.title: Forecasting carbon-risk hotspots ahead of the extreme 2026 El Niño
papers.abstract: A potentially super El Niño is forecasted in 2026, raising the need to anticipate land carbon-cycle risks before its impacts unfold. We develop a prospective early-warning framework that uses dynamic global vegetation models driven by an ensemble of ECMWF seasonal climate forecasts and machine-learning burned area predictions. Forecasts indicate a $0.23 \pm 0.21$ PgC reduction in global net biome productivity in the second half of 2026, with hotspots of sink weakening in eastern South America and elevated fire risk in Southeast Asia.

papers.title: The Online Steinitz Problem
papers.abstract: Inspired by Steinitz's celebrated result (1913) and recent online vector-balancing results of Kulkarni et al. (2024) and Aden-Ali (2026), we introduce the online Steinitz problem: $T$ vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, each of $\ell_2$-norm at most $1$ and with total sum zero, arrive one at a time and must be assigned immediately and irrevocably to unused positions of an array. The goal is to keep every prefix sum of the resulting order small. We first obtain deterministic prefix-discrepancy bounds of $O(\log T)$ for $d=1$ and $O(\sqrt T)$ for $d\ge2$. Our main contribution is a general reduction that converts deterministic and randomized online vector-balancing algorithms, which assign signs to arriving vectors, into online ordering algorithms. Combined with recent vector-balancing results, this yields a randomized algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log T+\sqrt{d\log T})$ and running time $O(dT\log T)$. The guarantee holds with high probability against an oblivious adversary. The reduction also gives bounds for sparse vectors and extends to inputs in arbitrary compact convex bodies. Finally, we prove matching lower bounds in both the deterministic and randomized cases.

papers.title: Versatile two-layer model for thermohydraulic prediction of microchannel heat sinks
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional conjugate heat-transfer simulations provide detailed predictions for microchannel heat sinks but can be computationally demanding when many geometries and operating conditions are evaluated. This study develops a versatile two-layer model (VTLM) that reduces the three-dimensional problem to two coupled two-dimensional fields while retaining the in-plane geometry of the flow passages and fins. Effects associated with the unresolved channel-height direction are incorporated through hydraulic and thermal closures that account for wall friction and the fluid- and fin-side contributions to interlayer heat transfer. The closures are evaluated from the representative channel geometry, flow-development condition, and fin configuration. The VTLM was assessed against three-dimensional reference models across broad ranges of channel aspect ratios and operating conditions, including uniform and nonuniform fin arrangements. Compared with the existing two-layer models, the VTLM showed improved overall agreement with the three-dimensional reference results. The results showed that prediction accuracy was governed mainly by the flow-development condition and channel aspect ratio, from which a conservative screening guideline was proposed for the examined straight-channel configurations. The assessment of finned expansion--contraction channels further supported the applicability of the VTLM to the investigated passages with abrupt width changes. Overall, the VTLM provides a reduced-dimensional framework for thermohydraulic analysis across the range of microchannel heat-sink configurations examined in this study without explicitly resolving the channel-height direction.

papers.title: Where Is the "Self" of a Large Language Model? -- From Self-Index to Self-Reference
papers.abstract: Whether a large language model has a self is usually argued without a way to measure it. We measure a functional self with two levels familiar from biology: a self-index, which marks material as the model's own, as animals tag self-generated signals with a corollary discharge, and self-reference, the ability to recognize what is one's own, as in mirror self-recognition. Our main finding is that language models mark their own messages in their internal representations and that recognizing these messages depends on this mark: no model we tested recognizes its own messages without it, and in the three models we edited, changing the mark removes or creates the recognition. We place the same text in an Assistant, a User, or a System message of the model's own chat template. In Qwen3.8-27B, the representation separates the model's own message from both external sources at every one of its 64 layers and in every held-out text. Asked who wrote a message, the model answers "you" with probability 0.77 for its own messages and at most 0.07 for the others. At each layer, we find eight directions along which the model's own message differs most from the same text as a User message. Giving the model's own message the User values along these directions lowers the rate of "you" to at most 0.05. Giving a User message the model's own values makes the model claim it, closing 41-67% of the gap between the two messages. Edits along eight random directions do neither. This holds in Qwen3.8-27B without and with thinking, gpt-oss-20b, and gpt-oss-120b. Across twenty-five open-weight models from fourteen developers, the two levels are nested: no model recognizes its own messages without a self-index, a pattern that would arise by chance with probability 0.004 if the levels were unrelated. These results support the account that self-reference is a readout of a self-index.

papers.title: Safeguarding Intelligent Power Dispatch:A Performance-Equivalent-Model-Based Safety-Critical Control Method for DC Microgrids
papers.abstract: Intelligent power dispatch is enabling fast and self-adaptive decision-making in microgrids, yet its deployment in real-world industry remains limited due to unresolved safety concerns. Existing safety-preserving approaches typically rely on an accurate characterization of the feasible operating region, which is impossible to obtain under uncertain and heterogeneous system dynamics. Moreover, even a dispatch command verified as feasible at a discrete setpoint may become unsafe during its continuous physical execution. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a safety-aware dispatch adjustment framework that uses performance-equivalent modeling of closed-loop systems (PEM-CLS) and embeds high-order control barrier functions and control Lyapunov functions within a quadratic programming formulation (HOCBF-CLF-QP). PEM-CLS captures EMS-required power-regulation dynamics solely from port-level responses, without requiring internal subsystem models, parameters, or controller information. Its modeling error is analytically characterized and explicitly bounded, enabling requirement-oriented dynamic abstraction for safety-critical control. Based on these PEMs, the HOCBF-CLF-QP safety controller coordinates heterogeneous transient power responses and corrects unsafe EMS commands to maintain dynamic safety during command execution. Four deliberately constructed extreme stress-test scenarios are used to expose conflicts between nominal EMS commands and physical safety. Without intervention, the DC-bus voltage violates its safety limit in all four cases, whereas the proposed framework maintains QP feasibility and limits the voltage deviation. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an algorithm-agnostic safety execution layer for intelligent power dispatch without requiring an exact feasible-region model or detailed internal information of lower-level devices.

papers.title: Realistic simulation of universal multiport interferometers with losses within a Gaussian formalism
papers.abstract: Photonic technologies are among the leading platform contenders for demonstrating quantum advantage. Nevertheless, photon losses represent the major hurdle for the realization of a fault-tolerant optical quantum computer, and the need for an accurate characterization of this phenomenon is crucial for classical simulations of quantum algorithms on noisy backends. The noisy regime would require the simulation of the algorithm on a Fock backend or rather assuming the a priori hypothesis on the uniformity of the optical losses, which may lead to wrong predictions about the outcome from the algorithm on a cerain hardware. We propose a Gaussian model that can reproduce a lossy dynamics through the experimental characterization of imperfect interferometers, yielding the corresponding mean vector and the covariance matrix. Such model can be adapted to any continuous-variable architecture (spatial or time-bin encoded) and for both the Gaussian boson sampling or general-dyne based algorithms. Eventually, we quantify the drift of optical losses from being uniform throughout the multiport interferometer by a numerical simulation. This work proposes a blueprint for future characterizations, tailor-suited for specific devices and architectures, as well as for potential error correction and mitigation techniques, and it paves the way for realistic simulations of quantum algorithms on NISQ optical platforms.

papers.title: Learn from Move: the Next Step for GUI Agents
papers.abstract: Existing benchmarks for GUI agents primarily focus on increasing task difficulty by extending task horizons. Besides, enabling agents to explore unfamiliar environments and successfully complete tasks within them is also a critical yet challenging problem. We introduce LatentGUIWorld, a benchmark of six tasks in three matched pairs organized by the evidence needed for control: $I_0$ uses prior knowledge and available observations, $I_1$ requires interaction that directly reveals hidden semantics, and $I_2$ identifies dynamics from action-response relationships. Frontier models struggle especially on $I_2$ tasks. We introduce MOVE, which separates movement from button events and exposes intermediate visual feedback, together with demonstrations of iterative exploration and control. Ablations show that both action granularity and multi-step demonstrations improve performance. After SFT, LatentLearner-9B achieves 50.0% overall success on LatentGUIWorld, comparable to several frontier models. Joint RL further raises egocentric Drag and Ten-Choice success to 92.0% and 75.3%. Behavioral analysis reveals multi-step exploration. In egocentric Drag, RL increases Pearson correlation between error-normalized commands and ideal gain compensation from 0.610 to 0.803. Together, these behaviors show that models learn to explore through interaction and adapt their control to environment dynamics. The same format improves GUI grounding after RL, reaching 67.37% mean accuracy across five benchmarks versus 66.72% for conventional RL.

papers.title: Optical Signatures of a Black Hole in Effective Quantum Gravity
papers.abstract: In this article, we present an investigation of observational signatures of a black hole (BH) in effective quantum gravity (EQG), particularly gravitational weak lensing and shadow analyses with the assumption that the BH is surrounded by uniform and non-uniform plasma. First, we review the spacetime by comparing it with well-known BH spacetimes such as Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström BHs. Subsequently, we explore the effect of the uniform and non-uniform plasma on the BH shadow. The results indicate that shadow radii decrease under the influence of the BH charge and both uniform and non-uniform plasma parameters. In addition, we obtain theoretical constraints on the spacetime parameters using observational data from the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration. Finally, we study gravitational weak lensing around the BH in EQG surrounded by uniform and non-uniform plasma. It was found that increasing the uniform plasma frequency leads to a rise in the deflection angle and vice versa for the non-uniform plasma.

papers.title: Lost in Contrast: Instruction-Preserving Decoding for Reliable Visual Question Answering
papers.abstract: Visual contrastive decoding corrects answers using the prediction difference between the original image and a reference condition, yet the same contrast also turns supported abstentions into incorrect answers. We find that abstentions are lost at two stages: contrastive decoding with candidate filtering can exclude the abstention token before any comparison takes place, and the reference branch's response to the abstention instruction is removed when the reference prediction is subtracted. We therefore propose instruction-preserving decoding, which keeps the effect of the abstention instruction on the original-image prediction intact while leaving the contrast strength freely adjustable. Using a perturbed image and an image-free prediction as references, we obtain IP-VCD and IP-M3ID. On decision utility (DU), which credits both correct answers and supported abstentions, both methods outperform all compared non-IP baselines on every one of nine models on VizWiz, and IP-VCD also leads on eight of nine models on Food-101. Candidate measurements and paired per-question comparisons show that computing the instruction effect and the visual contrast term separately lets contrastive decoding support both correct answers and supported abstentions.

papers.title: Matrix algebras with orthogonal Cauchy-like transforms and Toeplitz approximation: a negative result
papers.abstract: We consider newly designed matrix algebras associated with Cauchy orthogonal transforms. In this work, we are interested in checking the approximation of Toeplitz matrices using algebras of matrices, where each matrix is diagonalized by a fixed Cauchy orthogonal transform, in the spirit of fast algorithm based on preconditioning. We use the Korovkin theory for checking the Toeplitz approximability. Unfortunately and somehow surprisingly, the Korovkin test is negative, in contrast with the successful test for all the Fourier-like and trigonometric algebras, widely used in the relevant literature. More in detail, for the Cauchy algebras, the Frobenius optimal approximation fails to lead to the desired clustering, as also confirmed by ad hoc numerical experiments. It remains open to understand which kind of structured matrices can be approximated by these new algebras.

papers.title: Universal Varieties for Signatures of Membranes
papers.abstract: Membranes are sufficiently smooth vector-valued functions defined on the unit square, widely used in applications such as interpolation of image data. The signature of a membrane is a collection of nonlinear features that capture its essential geometry. We index these features in the graded Hopf algebra of two-parameter shuffle products and study the algebraic varieties for each graded component. At each truncation level, we obtain the dimension of this variety via a novel Witt-type formula. We propose a Chen-Chow theorem for membranes, provably at the second truncation level, and conjecturally for higher levels with extensive computational evidence in the computer algebra system OSCAR.

papers.title: Trace-to-Architecture: Capability Bottleneck Diagnosis for Harness Revision
papers.abstract: Improving an LLM agent requires knowing what to change when it fails. Similar failures can require different fixes, and resolving one problem can expose another. We introduce Trace-to-Architecture (T2A), a framework that uses execution trajectories to determine what to change in an agent's harness and when those changes apply. A development agent diagnoses failures using execution evidence from successful and failed tasks, revises the corresponding harness components, and then checks whether target tasks improve, selected successful tasks remain successful, and the edits are actually triggered. New execution evidence guides subsequent diagnosis and revision. Across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and AppWorld, T2A achieves the highest aggregate score for all three evaluated task agents, exceeding their respective strongest baselines by 6.2--30.3 points. We also integrate T2A's diagnosis and validation procedures into Meta-Harness, improving the resulting harnesses' mean ScienceWorld score by 21.6 points from the same starting harness.

papers.title: Bounding MrP: Subnational public opinion estimation without detailed census data
papers.abstract: Multilevel regression with post-stratification (MrP) is the dominant method for estimating public opinion in subnational units. The method requires the full joint distribution of demographic variables in a subnational unit, which is often unavailable from public census tabulations. Existing approaches fill this gap by imposing assumptions to combine marginal distributions of census variables into a synthetic joint distribution. We propose sharp MrP bounds instead: the smallest interval containing all estimates of subnational public opinion consistent with the marginal distributions alone. The bounds solve a pair of linear programs and are computationally feasible for typical applications in political science. Applied to two prominent examples in the literature, the bounds are tight enough to be informative and often more accurate than MrP restricted to a coarser, observed joint distribution of census variables. The bounds serve as margin-consistent interval estimates and a diagnostic when researchers use a synthetic joint distribution to construct MrP estimates.

papers.title: MMP for smooth co-rank one foliations
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of minimal models for smooth co-rank one foliations of general type.

papers.title: Finite-event modulation transfer through forward-scattering media
papers.abstract: How spatial structure is transferred through a forward-scattering medium depends jointly on pattern scale and propagation distance. Starting from photon exit displacements, we derive modulation transfer while retaining the number, depths, and projected angles of individual deflections, with event occurrences described by a homogeneous Poisson process along the propagation path. The second angular moment yields a leading low-frequency loss proportional to $k^2z^3$, where $k$ is angular spatial frequency and $z$ is thickness. At finite frequency, the model predicts two coupled departures: loss bends below its low-frequency quadratic extrapolation at fixed thickness, and transfer curves separate by thickness at fixed $k^2z^3$. The leading corrections to both effects arise from the same fourth angular moment. For symmetric, nondegenerate projected-angle distributions, the full response further establishes increasing loss with thickness in the same medium at fixed joint variable. Binary-pattern measurements through TiO$_2$ suspensions span five nominal loadings, seven thicknesses, and 20 spatial frequencies, supporting the approximate low-frequency scaling and showing both departures. A Gaussian effective-angle response calibrated only on lower-frequency data predicts the held-out higher-frequency band without refitting, with a logarithmic root-mean-square error of 0.0181 compared with 0.1021 for quadratic extrapolation. The results show that finite-event statistics provide a common physical origin for spectral bending and thickness-dependent departure from low-frequency scaling, linking coarse-pattern transport to finer spatial structure.

papers.title: Quantifying Precision in Measurement of Individualized, Evidence-Based Learning Across Sessions in Applied Behavior Analysis Therapy
papers.abstract: Current performance criteria used in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) are often based on whether a learner meets a predetermined benchmark e.g., 8 out of 10 correct responses across several sessions. Although these criteria help practitioners make instructional decisions, they provide limited information about how likely it is that the learner has truly acquired the skill. In this paper, we introduce a Bayesian approach that combines practitioners' prior expectations with the learner's ongoing performance data to estimate the learner's future performance level. Rather than providing only a pass or fail decision based on the criteria, we add an element of precision around that criteria to make decisions more nuanced to the testing conditions used. We also developed an R Shiny application for Measurement of Individualized, Evidence-Based Learning (MIEBL) that allows practitioners to apply this method in practice, supporting more informed instructional decisions and providing insight into the strengths and limitations of commonly used mastery criteria.

papers.title: Queue-Aware Token Communications: Bridging AI Representation and Wireless Service
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of foundation models and edge intelligence is transforming wireless networks from data-oriented communication systems into artificial intelligence (AI)-native service platforms. Token communications (TokenCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm that directly transmits task-oriented AI representations. However, existing studies typically assume that generated tokens can be transmitted immediately, overlooking the queueing dynamics arising from the mismatch between token workload generation and time-varying wireless service capability. To address this limitation, we introduce Queue-Aware TokenCom, which explicitly incorporates token queues into the AI service pipeline. We present an end-to-end architecture integrating AI representation generation, token workload management, wireless transmission, and downstream task inference. We then discuss two key design directions: budget-aware token representation optimization and queue-aware token service optimization, with the token budget serving as a critical interface between AI performance and communication efficiency. Moreover, we investigate fixed and adaptive token budget strategies to characterize the fundamental tradeoff between AI performance and communication efficiency in dynamic wireless environments. Finally, we outline research directions toward closed-loop, task-aware, and scalable TokenCom systems.

papers.title: On Intersection of Character Varieties Associated to Dehn Fillings of the Whitehead Link and Its Generalization
papers.abstract: The canonical component of the character variety of a hyperbolic 2-bridge link complement M is an algebraic surface, from the work of Thurston. If we fix a boundary component T of M and perform a Dehn-filling on T, we get a 1-cusped manifold whose character variety is commonly a generalized curve that is naturally embedded in the character variety of M. If we perform distinct Dehn-fillings on M, we get various generalized curves on the canonical surface. In this paper, we analyze how these curves intersect with each other in the surface and study the topological implications for these intersection points. We also classify the intersection points that correspond to reducible characters, using the twisted Alexander polynomials associated to the Dehn-fillings. Throughout the paper, we use the Whitehead link as a motivating example to illustrate our core methodology, while some generalizations to other 2-bridge links will also be discussed.

papers.title: GROMM: Generative Risk-neutral Option Market Models
papers.abstract: We present a statically and dynamically arbitrage-free European option market model with smooth interpolation between option prices, based on the SANOS framework, and prove that its dynamics admit a unique strong solution. In spirit, it is a stochastic model for local volatility when the latter is used as a representation of a European option price surface, not as a pricing model. We illustrate the strength of our approach on S&P Index Option data from January 2022 to August 2025. We show that the model's initial state fits within bid/ask for more than 95% of relevant market option prices. We then train the model dynamics under $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ and show that the model is indeed free of arbitrage while fitting the dynamics of the market well. We also propose a range of BHW-tests to test for absence of arbitrage.

papers.title: PathPilot: An Adaptive Question-Conditioned Multi-Magnification Navigation Agent for Whole-Slide Image Analysis
papers.abstract: The diagnostic capability of WSI agents relies on effective slide navigation to identify diagnostically relevant regions and efficiently integrate evidence across the slide. While in clinical practice, pathologists dynamically examine slides across multiple scales, integrating global and cellular evidence in a sequential manner, existing AI navigation approaches mostly operate at a single fixed magnification or rely on predefined magnification traversal. This mismatch prevents existing methods from modeling cross-magnification interactions and adaptive magnification selection inherent to real diagnostic workflows. We propose PathPilot, a clinically consistent multi-magnification WSI navigation agent that explicitly models cross-magnification localization and evidence-adaptive exploration. Specifically, we introduce a CrossMagLoc that learns magnification-specific diagnostic localization from pathologist viewing behavior and integrates information from adjacent magnifications to identify the diagnostically most relevant region within the current ROI, thereby providing a diagnostically informed starting point for subsequent question-conditioned exploration. We further introduce an EviRegionSearch that starts question-conditioned exploration from this region, progressively accumulating question-relevant evidence and adaptively determining the next navigation action according to the remaining evidence requirement. Their iterative interaction enables PathPilot to sequentially explore across ROIs and magnifications until sufficient evidence is acquired. Extensive QA evaluations across five cohorts demonstrate consistent superiority over competing SOTA methods on inter/external cohorts, respectively, validating question-conditioned evidence acquisition across regions and magnifications that mirrors the sequential, knowledge-driven navigation of pathologists.

papers.title: VAttnPO: Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards commonly assigns one sequence advantage to an entire response. This outcome-level signal distinguishes overall response quality but leaves changes in visual-evidence use across generated tokens implicit. We introduce VAttnPO (Visual Attention-Guided Policy Optimization), which uses answer-conditioned visual attention to refine token-level credit while preserving the verifier-derived trajectory-mean advantage. A frozen old policy constructs a visual reference by teacher forcing the known correct answer and produces a visual distribution for each rollout token. VAttnPO measures their agreement in visual-attention space using Jensen--Shannon divergence, rather than reading guidance from teacher output-token distributions or introducing an attention-matching objective. Trajectory centering, relative-position weighting, and credit balancing turn this agreement into a zero-mean, position-aware correction to the GRPO sequence advantage. Token intervention, visual-index permutation, and trajectory analysis provide diagnostic evidence linking this signal to model behavior, visual correspondence, and generation position. On Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, VAttnPO raises six-task image AVE from 70.97 with GRPO to 73.50 and scores higher on every reported structured, video, and MME metric. Gains over GRPO also hold on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and InternVL3-8B-Instruct.

papers.title: Spatio-Temporal Detection of Photovoltaic Systems on Industrial Building Rooftops Using Satellite Imagery and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The global transition toward carbon-neutral energy systems is heavily dependent on the rapid deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) infrastructure, yet the speed of this expansion has outpaced the ability of administrative registries to maintain accurate records. While high-resolution commercial imagery is often used for monitoring, its high cost and infrequent updates can create an information gap for grid operators, energy infrastructure developers and policymakers. This study addresses the lack of scalable monitoring for industrial-scale rooftop PV systems by developing a machine learning framework that utilizes open-access, multispectral Sentinel-2 satellite imagery. By integrating building geometries from OpenStreetMap with Sentinel-2 reflectance data, a Random Forest model was trained to identify the specific spectral signatures of PV modules. Moving beyond theoretical modeling, this work emphasizes practical implementation through the development of an interactive web-based prototype for on-demand site monitoring. The application enables users to retrieve up-to-date satellite observations and assess the presence of PV systems on industrial building rooftops. The tool incorporates quality metrics that inform users whether a prediction is supported by sufficient training data density or requires manual verification. This end-to-end framework demonstrates that open-source medium-resolution data can effectively bridge this monitoring gap.

papers.title: Amortised adaptive importance sampling
papers.abstract: Monte Carlo sampling algorithms aim to produce samples from a target distribution with a given unnormalised probability density function. The high cost of running Monte Carlo algorithms, with many simulation steps or particles needed to obtain a good empirical approximation to the target, can be reduced by introducing learnable components into the sampler -- a form of amortisation. Once these components are trained, amortised samplers can produce high-quality samples with less computation at sampling time than training-free algorithms would require. We propose an amortised sampler built upon the framework of adaptive importance sampling -- a hierarchical importance sampling procedure where the proposal is iteratively adapted. Our amortised adaptive importance sampling algorithm fits a lightweight neural network that adapts the proposal using information obtained over the course of sampling. By training our sampler over many different targets taken from the same family of distributions, we obtain a sampler that can adapt to a specific target at sampling time without a priori access to the target's parameters. We show that our procedure can efficiently sample from targets within the family the sampler was trained on, giving improvements over target-specific amortised samplers and training-free adaptive importance sampling algorithms. We also explore the potential for generalisation, where the trained sampler is used to sample from targets outwith its training family.

papers.title: CopyQuad: Quadrupedal Skill Transfer from a Single Side-View Video Without a Depth Model
papers.abstract: Video-to-robot pipelines for quadrupedal imitation insert a learned lifting stage, either a monocular depth model or a per-clip 3D reconstruction, to recover the one axis a side-view camera cannot see. We present CopyQuad, which omits that stage and pins the missing axis to the robot's own stance width instead. The setting is side-view footage of sagittally dominated motion, where limb motion is almost entirely in the image plane. A frozen 2D keypoint detector and a fixed analytic retargeting then turn a single uncalibrated clip into a robot reference whose foot targets are reachable by construction, so no per-clip trajectory optimization is needed. One phase-indexed reward structure, whose only per-behavior freedom is three scalars from a shared sweep, learns a dog walk, a horse walk, a horse trot and two non-periodic gestures, all deployed zero-shot on hardware. We then measure what omitting the axis costs. In a training-free rigidity test, a video depth model varies the distance between the animal's hips by $40$ to $107\%$ of its own mean and a single-image metric model by $22$ to $58\%$, though that distance cannot move. Motion capture puts the true lateral paw travel of a dog walk at $4.5$ cm peak to peak, a mean deviation near $1.4$ cm against the $3.5$ cm of lateral foot error our policies already leave, so the discarded axis sits below the pipeline's resolution. Depth repaired to feasibility never beats the constant, and the unrepaired estimates put the robot on the ground.

papers.title: Emergent Spinorial Structure in Mesoscopic Irreversible Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: Can transport coefficients determine both the coherent evolution of a mesoscopic system and distances between its thermodynamic states? We establish this connection within a canonical operator framework. Thermodynamic coordinates and conjugate forces obey commutation relations governed by a reduced constant ${\kbar}_B$. Requiring coordinate evolution to reproduce self-adjoint flux observables fixes a compatible generator up to an additive multiplication operator, set to zero in the minimal realization. The resulting equation describes coherent mesoscopic amplitudes, with transport fixing its coefficients and the reduced constant setting the evolution scale. An exact first-order factorization gives a geometry through Connes' spectral-distance prescription, including for coordinate-dependent transport. The metric is twice the inverse of the symmetric transport matrix. Coordinate derivatives of the antisymmetric part can change the dynamics without changing distances. Published thermoelectric data illustrate the geometry. A separate quadratic entropy-production observable has adjacent entropy levels separated by the reduced constant under the stated canonical and finite-mode matching assumptions. This conditional prediction offers a possible experimental signature. The evolution is unitary; irreversible relaxation requires additional mechanisms, such as environmental coupling or coarse-graining.

papers.title: Impact of shear and dilational membrane viscosities on capsule shape and dynamics under shear flow: a theoretical study
papers.abstract: In artificial (micro)capsules or cells such as red blood cells for example, the two-dimensional (2D) rheology of the membrane (or the shell) is viscoelastic and not only elastic. The deformation and inclination of such a capsule are theoretically studied under shear and extensional flows. The membrane mechanics is described by the Kelvin-Voigt model: the 2D dissipation with the Boussinesq-Scriven law associated to specific dilational and shear Boussinesq numbers $Bq_d$ and $Bq_d$ respectively while the elastic constitutive law is either Hookean, strain-softening (neoHookean) or strain-hardening (Skalak). The dynamics depends on the elastic capillary number $Ca$, the Poisson ratio (or $C$ in Skalak law), the viscosity ratio $λ$, the nonlinearities included in the constitutive law and both boussinesq numbers. Three dynamics are identified in the limit of weak deformations: a tank-treading motion in the limit of small elastic capillary number with a characteristic time depending on $λ$, $Bq_s$ and $Bq_d$, an oscillation without any elasticity and a damped oscillation leading to a tank-treading motion in the limit of large Boussinesq numbers. In all cases, both shear and dilational 2D dissipations contribute differently leading to non-trivial results. In the case of a Skalak law with $C=1$, $Bq=Bq_s=Bq_d$ and $Bq>>λ$, the deformations in the limits $Ca<<1$, $Bq=O(1)$ and $Ca=O(1)$, $Bq>>1$ determined in the seminal work of \cite{barthes1985role} are recovered.

papers.title: Revisiting the Bobkov-Chistyakov-Götze theorem on approximately Gaussian marginals
papers.abstract: We study one-dimensional marginals of an isotropic, log-concave probability measure in $\mathbb{R}^n$. We show that the Kolmogorov distance between a typical marginal and the standard Gaussian distribution is at most $C/n$, for a universal constant $C > 0$. This bound is optimal in general, up to the value of the universal constant. It improves the Gaussian approximation bound of Bobkov, Chistyakov and Götze by a logarithmic factor in the log-concave setting.

papers.title: The XMM Cluster Survey: Cross-Calibration of eROSITA and XMM using Dark Energy Survey Y3 Galaxy Clusters
papers.abstract: We present the cross-calibration of the eROSITA and XMM telescopes, using galaxy clusters detected by redMaPPer from the first three years of Dark Energy Survey observations (DESY3RM). We use the X-ray: Generate and Analyse (XGA) Python module to measure eROSITA properties, and validate our methodology using a deep pointed eROSITA CAL-PV observation of A3158, and a sample of 119 clusters from the expanded HIgh FLux Galaxy Cluster Sample (eeHiFLUGCS). Next, we construct a sample of DESY3RM clusters matched to XMM observations analysed by the XMM Cluster Survey (XCS), and to clusters in the first release of the eROSITA All-Sky Survey (eRASS1). This produced a sample of 114 DESY3RM clusters with both XMM and eROSITA detections. Our resulting X-ray temperatures determined from eROSITA were compared to eRASS1 catalogue values, showing consistency between the two analyses. Comparisons between XMM and eROSITA temperatures reveal a systematic offset, with XMM temperatures 28$\pm$7% higher on average. Finally, we fit $L_{\rm X,soft}$-$λ_{\rm RM}$ and $T_{\rm X}$-$λ_{\rm RM}$ scaling relations for both eROSITA and XMM using the same cluster sample, finding minimal differences in the $L_{\rm X,soft}$-$λ_{\rm RM}$ relation but a clear normalisation offset in the $T_{\rm X}$-$λ_{\rm RM}$ relation, particularly for the highest richness systems. This study will enable future work combining eROSITA and XMM observatories for DESY3RM clusters.

papers.title: A census of Dark Energy Survey Year 3 redMaPPer galaxy clusters in a high exposure eROSITA All Sky Survey region
papers.abstract: We present the cross-match of galaxy clusters detected by redMaPPer using the first three years of Dark Energy Survey (DESY3RM) operations, and the first release of the eROSITA-All Sky Survey (eRASS1) taken by eROSITA on board the Spectrum Roentgen Gamma telescope. We define a sky region ($60^{\circ}<{\rm R.A.}<90^{\circ}$ and $-58^{\circ}<{\rm Dec}<-48^{\circ}$) whereby the mean eRASS1 exposure time of clusters falling within this footprint is $\sim$2.5 times longer than the mean exposure time of the full eRASS1--DESY3RM overlap. Limiting to a redshift range $0.2 < z < 0.65$ and redMaPPer estimated richnesses to $>$50, we obtain a sample of 57 clusters. We match these clusters to the cluster catalogue constructed for the eRASS1, finding 45 clusters with a match and 12 with no match in the catalogue. X-ray properties of the 12 unmatched clusters are estimated via a forced photometry analysis. We investigate the form of the luminosity-richness relation, finding the relation using the full 57 cluster sample is statistically consistent with using only the 45 matched clusters, and will require the deeper data of future eRASS releases (or dedicated X-ray follow-up) to explore further potential differences. Using external data from XMM, ACT and SPT, we find detections of 5 of the 12 unmatched clusters, indicating the presence of virialised gas. Finally, we found the 12 unmatched clusters occupy a higher redshift range and lower richness range (compared to the matched clusters), and find no evidence for an underlying physical reason for the lack of X-ray emission.

papers.title: Essential factors for surface homeomorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least one that is isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism, possibly relative to a finite invariant set. We construct an intrinsic monotone factor by collapsing the maximal continua whose iterates have uniformly bounded diameter in the universal cover. The quotient is homeomorphic to the original surface and the factor is isotopic to $f$ and has several strongly chaotic dynamical features. It is infinitely continuum-wise expansive, tight, and topologically mixing, and it has a dense family of rotational horseshoes, dense periodic points, and a single topological homoclinic class. The factor can be taken as an area-preserving homeomorphism. The quotient preserves stable translation length on the fine curve graph and the applicable homological rotation sets. When $f$ is $C^\infty$, a companion paper gives a unique measure of maximal entropy for the factor; it has full support and is Bernoulli.

papers.title: FoveaTree: Information-Density Trees for Query-Guided Visual Token Pruning in Video Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Video large language models (Video LLMs) encode each frame into hundreds of visual tokens, making video inference expensive. Existing methods reduce this cost through similarity-based merging or attention-based selection but face two challenges: Hierarchy-blind Pruning, which overlooks regional compressibility and can discard critical evidence, and Attention Drift, where positional effects and attention sinks shift text-to-vision attention away from task relevance. We propose FoveaTree, a two-stage, training-free visual-token pruning framework. First, Merge-Gain Density Estimation measures the feature distortion caused by regional merging and constructs a quadtree-derived density map to guide token dropping, merging, and retention. Second, Attention Tree Pruning uses the surviving units and inherited tree topology to refine text-to-vision attention in intermediate LLM layers, preserving relevant regional evidence while removing low-relevance content. We evaluate FoveaTree on InternVL3.5-8B and Qwen3-VL-8B across five video question-answering benchmarks and one captioning benchmark at 50%, 30%, and 10% visual-token retention. FoveaTree consistently achieves overall state-of-the-art performance across the evaluated settings, offering a strong accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

papers.title: Before Attention Sinks Form: Hidden-State Geometry Reveals and Modulates Their Formation
papers.abstract: Attention sinks are usually studied after they have formed. We ask whether a measurable hidden-state change appears beforehand and whether changing that geometry alters what happens later. To remove network depth as a shortcut, we compare prompts in the same model and at the same layer. When sink timing varies across prompts, simple spectral summaries of the hidden states add information beyond current attention, with the clearest prompt-specific signal in a short window about two to three layers before sink formation. The predictive strength varies across cohorts, so we treat the spectrum as a readout of a pre-sink state change rather than a universal warning statistic. The signal is broader than one measured extreme activation. We then modify only the singular values of the post-layer hidden states after current attention has already been computed. These interventions change later sink behavior in Qwen2.5, GLM-Z1, and GPT-OSS relative to norm-matched random spectral perturbations. In Qwen2.5, the immediate suppressive effect is accompanied by a reduction in next-layer query--key preference for position~0, and the learned spectral directions remain stable when estimated from substantially less training data. Together, the results show that attention sinks are preceded by a short spectral reorganization of hidden states, and directly perturbing this geometry can causally alter subsequent sink formation.

papers.title: Superdecomposable Complete Path Algebras
papers.abstract: Generalizing the setting of the second author's work on indecomposable modules without nonzero hollow factors, we characterize quivers $Q$ for which the dual algebra $R$ of the path coalgebra of $Q$, equivalently the complete path algebra, has no nonzero uniform right ideals: this happens exactly when every vertex of $Q$ can reach a vertex emitting at least two distinct arrows. Equivalently, the injective hull $E(R)$ of the right regular module is superdecomposable. These conditions are also equivalent to the path coalgebra having no nonzero hollow factor modules as a left module over its dual algebra.

papers.title: Endpoint Schatten class properties of commutators on quantum tori
papers.abstract: We study endpoint Schatten class properties of commutators $[I_θ^ε,M_x]$ on quantum tori of dimension $d\geq2$, where $I_θ^ε$ is the Riesz potential of order $ε$ and $M_x$ denotes the left multiplication operator by an operator $x$ on quantum tori $\mathbb T_θ^d$. For $-\frac{d}{2}<ε<1$, $ε\neq0$, and $x\in L_1(\mathbb T_θ^d)$, we prove that $[I_θ^ε,M_x]\in \mathcal L_{\frac{d}{1-ε},\infty}$ if and only if $x\in\dot W_{\frac{d}{1-ε}}^1(\mathbb T_θ^d)$. We also determine the singular value asymptotics of this commutator for $x\in\dot W_{\frac{d}{1-ε}}^1(\mathbb T_θ^d)$. The necessary Sobolev condition holds throughout $1-d<ε<1$, $ε\neq0$. For $ε\leq-\frac{d}{2}$, we characterise Hilbert--Schmidt membership, with a logarithmically weighted Fourier condition at $ε=-\frac{d}{2}$. In order to get the singular value asymptotics of commutators, we prove singular value asymptotics for pseudodifferential operators of arbitrary negative order on quantum tori using $C^*$-algebraic principal symbols. This asymptotic result confirms Conjecture~7.1 of McDonald and Ponge (\emph{Adv. Math.} 412 (2023), 108815).

papers.title: Sharp Thresholds for Linear Determinacy and Zero Wave Speed in Lotka-Volterra Competition-Diffusion Systems
papers.abstract: We study two sharp competition thresholds in the Lotka-Volterra competition-diffusion system: the zero-speed threshold for bistable traveling fronts and the linear-determinacy threshold for monostable traveling fronts. Building on our previous results on propagation direction and the classification of traveling waves, we derive explicit Gaussian integral representations of both critical parameters, without involving unknown traveling-wave profiles or speeds. These formulas provide exact characterizations of the optimal competition parameters separating the corresponding propagation regimes. The derivation of these representations was assisted by ChatGPT (OpenAI) Pro, while the underlying theoretical foundations were established in our earlier works.

papers.title: The Midas Touch for Metric Depth: Interpretable Metricization for Generalizable Depth Perception
papers.abstract: Recent foundation models have drastically improved the generalization of monocular relative depth estimation, yet recovering accurate metric depth from their estimates for depth perception tasks remains challenging due to scale ambiguity and local metric-scale inconsistency. Existing approaches recover metric depth from sparse observations using either explicit global affine transformation algorithms or implicit data-driven depth completion networks. The former cannot accommodate spatially varying relative-to-metric relationships, while the latter are sensitive to the distribution of sparse observations and may not fully exploit generalizable relative depth priors. To simultaneously address these issues, this study extends our previous work MTD and proposes MTDv2, a hybrid metric depth perception framework that combines explicit depth metricization with data-driven metric depth refinement. The explicit depth metricization process performs segment-wise affine transformations to recover spatially varying metric scales while preserving the geometric structure of relative depth, followed by pixel-wise depth refinement that propagates metric observations along paths with minimal accumulated geometric variation. The data-driven depth refinement process subsequently extends the explicit single-path depth propagation to a learnable multi-path formulation while preserving its interpretability. Extensive experiments conducted on 16 public datasets demonstrate the robust and generalizable depth scale recovery capability of MTDv2 across diverse sources of sparse observations and different depth estimation paradigms, as well as its broad applicability to downstream 3D perception tasks. Code will be publicly available at https://mias.group/MTD upon publication.

papers.title: NFMap: Topographic 2D Manifold Learning with Invertible Normalizing Flows
papers.abstract: We present NFMap, a dimensionality reduction method for 2D visualisation that extends Generative Topographic Mapping (GTM) with a bijective normalizing flow. Like GTM, NFMap places a fixed mixture grid prior over a 2D latent map, giving a parametric embedding, an explicit likelihood, and the ability to project new points onto an existing map; the likelihood is an effective out-of-distribution signal on chemical datasets. Unlike GTM, whose latent-to-data mapping is an RBF network of bounded flexibility, NFMap's mapping is a normalizing flow, and is therefore fully invertible: any location on the map can be carried back to data space. To alleviate map crowding on large datasets, NFMap additionally supports heavy-tailed Student-t mixture components. NFMap maps data to a latent space of the same dimension, split into a 2-dimensional navigable map and an off-manifold residual. Because the flow is bijective and its objective penalises volume contraction, variance squeezed out of the residual must reappear in the navigable map. The residual scale is the main control between local neighbourhood fidelity and global distance fidelity; its effect depends on the dimensionality of the data and is coupled to the extent of the latent grid.

papers.title: On Solvable Automorphism Groups of Function Fields over Finite Fields
papers.abstract: The classical Hurwitz bound gives a linear upper bound in terms of the genus for automorphism groups of algebraic function fields in characteristic zero, whereas algebraic function fields in positive characteristic can have much larger automorphism groups. Usually, one considers the case where the constant field is an algebraically closed field. Here we focus on function fields over a finite constant field. It turns out that the situation is very different. We firstly investigate solvable subgroups and $p$-subgroups of $\rm{Aut}(F/\Bbb{F}_q)$, where $p=\rm{char}(\Bbb{F}_q)$ and $F/\Bbb{F}_q$ is a function field of genus $g_F\ge2$ with full constant field $\Bbb{F}_q$. We prove that there are explicit constants $C_q^{(sol)}$ and $C_q^{(p)}$, depending only on $q$, such that, for every solvable subgroup $G\le\rm{Aut}(F/\Bbb{F}_q)$ and every $p$-subgroup $P\le\rm{Aut}(F/\Bbb{F}_q)$, $$ |G|\le C_q^{(sol)}(g_F-1),\qquad |P|\le C_q^{(p)}(g_F-1).$$ In particular, one may take $C_q^{(sol)}=12q^2(q-1)$ for $q\ge4$ and $C_q^{(p)}=5q$ for every $q$. In the second part of this article, we give asymptotic lower bounds for solvable automorphism groups. For every $q$ there is an explicit constant $L_q>0$ and a sequence of function fields $F_i/\Bbb{F}_q$ with $g_{F_i}\to\infty$, together with solvable subgroups $G_i\le\rm{Aut}(F_i/\Bbb{F}_q)$, such that $$ |G_i|\ge L_q(g_{F_i}-1) $$ for all $i$. For $q\ge5$ one may take $L_q=2q(q-1)/(q-2)$. If $q=r^2$ with $r\ge3$, an unramified tower construction over the Hermitian function field gives the stronger choice $L_q=2r^3(r-1)/(r-2)$. Moreover, as an application of our tower construction above, we improve the asymptotic lower bound of Ma and Xing for subgroups of $\rm{Aut}(F/\Bbb{F}_q)$ whose order is relatively prime to $p$. As another application, we extend our method to obtain explicit linear bounds for $p$-solvable groups in terms of the genus.

papers.title: Transport Determines Spectral Distance in Mesoscopic Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We derive a distance between thermodynamic states from a positive Hermitian transport tensor within a mesoscopic canonical model. An exact first-order factorization of the evolution generator gives a commutator norm and the metric $G=2g$, where $g$ denotes the symmetric transport tensor. Gradients of the antisymmetric tensor can change the evolution, but they leave this distance unchanged. The construction allows coordinate-dependent coefficients. For constant Onsager coefficients, a Clifford representation gives the same metric. In a two-channel thermoelectric system, the ratio of normalized principal distances is $\sqrt{1+ZT}+\sqrt{ZT}$. Transport coupling thus fixes the anisotropy of this metric. The construction requires neither an independent metric nor a physical spin variable.

papers.title: Automorphisms and canonical forms of integer lattices
papers.abstract: We improve the Plesken--Souvignier algorithm for computing automorphism groups and isometries of positive definite integer quadratic lattices by exploiting characteristic sublattices and refining vector enumeration. For lattices with roots, we also use the Weyl group to accelerate the computation of canonical forms. Experiments with concrete implementations demonstrate substantial speedups and show that canonical forms can be computed at a cost comparable to that of computing automorphism groups.

papers.title: Pseudo-Panel Event Studies: Econometric Foundations for Credible Applications
papers.abstract: Event studies with panel data are widely used to estimate treatment effects. With repeated cross-sections, future treatment dates are unobserved for untreated individuals. Pseudo-panel event studies impute pre-treatment outcomes of the treated using matched untreated individuals. This paper establishes identification in such designs and characterizes bias when identification conditions fail. I show that the pseudo-panel regression is equivalent to weighted least squares with group means. This representation simplifies computation and yields analytical inference. In simulations, analytical confidence intervals attain near-nominal coverage, whereas conventional intervals substantially undercover. I also develop a doubly robust estimator using richer covariates, a symmetric matching design with synthetic type fixed effects, and a fully nonparametric estimator that accommodates heterogeneous treatment effects. In a Korean panel survey, the pseudo-panel regression yields an employment child penalty of 42.1%, close to 46.9% in the actual panel. Applications to repeated cross-sections yield employment penalties of about one-third.

papers.title: The Multilingual Artificial Hivemind: Do All LLMs Think Alike in Every Language?
papers.abstract: Text generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) often remains limited in diversity compared to that produced by humans. Recent advances demonstrate the presence of inter- and intra-model collapse in open-ended generation of English text, raising concerns about the long-term homogenization of LLM, and more importantly, human thought. However, our understanding of whether this homogenization extends to languages beyond English is limited. In this work, we investigate the role of language on output diversity. Specifically, we aim to understand whether multilingual LLM-generated text is also homogeneous, and whether this homogeneity matches what we observe in humans. Across 23 open-weight models and 13 languages, we find that the artificial hivemind effect is pervasive but uneven in its extent. The intra-model effect holds in three different embedding spaces and under a lexical metric that uses no embedding model, so it is not an artifact of how diversity is measured. The size of the homogenization gap is associated with a model's competence in a language, measured on a held-out translation benchmark, robustly across embedding spaces. Thus, we demonstrate a performance-diversity tradeoff in multilingual LLMs.

papers.title: The nabla operator, Hall--Littlewood polynomials and LLT polynomials
papers.abstract:
Bergeron, Garsia, Haiman, and Tesler conjectured that $(-1)^{n-\ell(μ)}
abla\widetilde H_μ[X;0,t]$ and $
ablaω\widetilde H_μ[X;0,t^{-1}]$ are Schur positive, and that $
ablaω\widetilde H_μ[X;0,t^{-1}]-
ablaω\widetilde H_ν[X;0,t^{-1}]$ is Schur positive when $μ$ dominates $ν$. The first statement follows from the compositional shuffle conjecture of Haglund, Morse, and Zabrocki, proved by Carlsson and Mellit. We prove the other two statements. All three statements also hold for $
abla^r$ with $r\geq1$. The main new step is an identity: when $μ$ covers $ν$, the difference $ω\widetilde H_μ[X;0,t^{-1}]-ω\widetilde H_ν[X;0,t^{-1}]$ is minus a power of $t$ times one LLT polynomial. Using the Catalanimals and the Cauchy identity of Blasiak, Haiman, Morse, Pun, and Seelinger, we show that $
abla^r$ of this LLT polynomial is, up to sign, a positive sum of LLT polynomials. We also extend the main results to the Schiffmann algebra setting.

papers.title: Is the Platform Part of the Measurement? A Protocol and Simulation Study for Cross-Platform Equivalence of Machine-Labelled Policy Sentiment
papers.abstract: Comparing machine-labelled sentiment across social media platforms is now routine: differences in classifier scores between platforms are read as differences in public opinion. These comparisons rest on an assumption that the classifier measures the same construct, on the same scale, on every platform. Some studies check a classifier's validity platform by platform, but to our knowledge none has modelled the platform as a facet of the classifier's measurement. We adapt the psychometric equivalence toolkit (generalizability theory, measurement invariance and differential item functioning, and score linking) to machine-labelled policy sentiment, treating the platform as a survey mode, and specify a six-step protocol with anchor events fixed in advance, an anchor-density audit, and a two-classifier convergence control. A simulation with known ground truth illustrates what the assumption can cost in one generating configuration fixed in advance: across 500 replications, because the platforms measure through different functions, a pooled index that takes platform scores at face value reports the wrong sign of aggregate sentiment on nearly a quarter of days, whereas an index adjusted with each platform's known measurement function does so on under one day in sixty on average. A case study of the instrument from the first author's MSc dissertation, a fine-tuned BERT classifier over 255,446 UK economic-policy comments from Twitter/X, Reddit, YouTube, and Quora, motivates the design and illustrates the instrument-dependence the protocol addresses. The full four-platform application, under fresh collection with the pre-specified design, is the designated follow-up study. The protocol lets a researcher test whether pooling platforms is defensible in a given corpus, or whether platform scores must be linked before any average is taken.

papers.title: Multivalued Groups and Schur Rings
papers.abstract: We study finite involutive multivalued groups associated with Schur rings. Their reduced valency is shown to equal the least common multiple of the sizes of the basic sets of the corresponding ring. We prove that the double-coset group associated with a complemented subgroup of a finite group is isomorphic to a Schur multivalued group over the complement. In particular, every coset multivalued group is a Schur multivalued group. Using affine Schur rings, we construct families of pairwise nonisomorphic commutative multivalued groups over elementary abelian groups. We obtain asymptotic bounds for the sizes of these families and prove that the proportion of double-coset groups in them tends to zero.

papers.title: Image Tokenizers Should Be Trained Between Images
papers.abstract: Latent diffusion models generate images as codes of an image tokenizer, whose decoder turns them into the pixel image. Recent tokenizers improve how well these codes reconstruct an image and how easily a generator learns them. Yet a generator does not reproduce the codes of training images, and when a generated code lands outside what the decoder expects, the decoded image contains imperfections. Current methods make the decoder more robust to generated codes by adding noise during training. However, generated codes lie between the training codes and resemble their mixture more than one of them plus noise. To improve generated images, decoders should therefore be trained on codes in the space between training samples. We propose InterpTok, which fine-tunes MAETok to decode mixtures of image codes into natural images. Since no target image exists between two training samples, a discriminator judges whether each decoded mixture looks as natural as its two sources. A mixing ratio loss requires the decoded mixture to keep the mixing ratio of the two codes. Together, they prevent collapse to a trivial solution and yield a sharp and natural composition of both images. InterpTok keeps MAETok's reconstruction quality and improves interpolation quality more than threefold, the best of all tokenizers in a recent benchmark. Beyond interpolation, InterpTok improves the generation FID of a matched diffusion transformer from 11.61 to 8.48 without guidance, and even reaches 8.11 at an eighth of the sampling steps, where the generator on MAETok's codes worsens. The generator trained on our tokenizer also reaches the final result of the one trained on MAETok at half the training steps. Our findings show that the space between image codes can and should be explicitly supervised rather than ignored.

papers.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
papers.abstract: We study Galois coinvariants of the geometric étale fundamental group and étale cohomology of varieties over a finitely generated field $k$. We establish finiteness properties of these coinvariants for (possibly infinite) Galois extensions $L/k$ such that $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As applications, we obtain finiteness results for $L$-rational torsion points on abelian varieties and étale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over number fields.

papers.title: Separating Prompt Harmfulness from Interaction Safety via Partial Generation
papers.abstract: LLM-based information systems need safety guardrails. Most guardrails classify the prompt alone. If the prompt looks harmful, the system rejects it before any answer is generated. This is costly. Many rejected prompts would have received a safe response. Users lose help they should have received from the information system. This cost grows as conversational and generative search becomes common. Prompt-level labels treat harm as a property of the query. But harm depends on what the model actually writes. Existing input-output guards do look at responses. But they judge a finished response, so the decision comes after full generation. However, we observe that safety of model interaction with the input prompt can be inferred early with only partial output. So the system can start generating, watch the partial response, and stop only if it turns harmful. We test this idea in three steps. First, we build a dataset of 41,944 prompt-response pairs with seven open weights LLMs from three families: Llama, Gemma, and Qwen. Second, we show that prompt harmfulness and interaction safety differ. Prompt labels and response labels agree on only 50.46\% of items (Cohen's $κ$ = 0.06). Of the prompts that make any model respond harmfully, only 3.5\% do so for all seven LLMs. Third, we show that partial responses carry most of the signal. Fine-tuned classifiers predict response-level harm well (best AUPRC 0.885, F1 0.807). About one third of the response tokens recover almost full-response AUPRC.

papers.title: Towards Complementary Keypoint Detection via Mixture of Detectors
papers.abstract: Keypoint detection plays a central role in geometric vision pipelines. Existing detectors exhibit complementary strengths across different scene structures and keypoint budgets, and reliance on a single detector often results in suboptimal keypoint distributions. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Mixture of Detectors (MoD)} for dense matching pipelines, a unified framework for complementary keypoint detection through the adaptive composition of heterogeneous detectors. MoD first distills heterogeneous detectors into a unified model, allowing diverse detection maps to be predicted efficiently within a single forward pass. Detector selection is subsequently formulated as a patch-wise, budget-conditioned decision process, in which a lightweight router assigns the most suitable detector to each local region. To avoid heuristic supervision, the router is trained with task-driven rewards derived from downstream matching quality, jointly capturing both keypoint quantity and precision. Extensive experiments on MegaDepth, ScanNet, and HPatches demonstrate that MoD consistently outperforms strong baselines across a wide range of keypoint budgets, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving keypoint distribution and downstream geometric performance.

papers.title: Relational Learning as World Modeling
papers.abstract: Relational learning typically predicts from a database state, but decision making asks a different question: how will that state change under an action? In operational systems, the answer depends on system-specific dynamics that may not be visible in the database itself. We view each such system as a relational "world" and ask whether a model can infer how it behaves from observed executions. We introduce TabWM (Tabular World Model) and WorldRel, a generator of executable relational worlds for pretraining. Given executions from an unseen world, TabWM uses them as context to predict the sparse structured edits caused by a new action without parameter updates. Across 512 held-out worlds, complete-edit F1 rises from 0.016 with no observed executions to 0.685 with 64, where a correct edit must match its operation, relational location, and value. Because these predictions are explicit relational edits, they can be applied recursively to imagine candidate futures and compare actions before they are taken. Broader search over these predicted futures improves the realized return of selected action sequences. Together, these results suggest that relational dynamics can be learned in context, broadening relational learning from modeling system state to modeling how that state changes under action.

papers.title: A note on Finiteness and Boundedness in Cartesian Products of Discrete and Well-Ordered Sets, Application to Transition Systems
papers.abstract: In this short note, we prove that any closed interval in a well-ordered and discrete space is finite. The coincidence between finiteness and boundedness can then be established for transition systems where the state space is well-ordered and discrete. Finally, this result is also proven when the state space is a Cartesian product of $d$ discrete and well-ordered sets.

papers.title: Globally Convergent Block Coordinate Descent Algorithms for Semi-Nonnegative Independent Component Analysis
papers.abstract: We propose a subgradient-based block coordinate descent (BCD-SubG) framework for nonconvex optimization over products of probability simplices and a closed feasible set, motivated by semi-nonnegative independent component analysis (Semi-NNICA). Elementary column transformations are used to preserve simplex feasibility, while first-order information guides block and pair selection. We establish the global convergence of BCD-SubG using a constrained Lojasiewicz inequality; additional eventual-interiority conditions yield stationary limits and convergence rates. We then specialize BCD-SubG to the direct-fit and indirect-fit Semi-NNICA models and derive explicit updates that ensure global convergence without further assumptions. For both models, eventual interiority also yields stationary limits and convergence-rate estimates. Experiments on synthetic mixtures and simulated magnetic resonance spectroscopy data show generally lower recovery errors and shorter wall-clock times than the tested Semi-NNICA baselines. Joint diagonalization experiments further demonstrate lower final objective values.

papers.title: Engineering Ferroelectric Phases in BaTiO$_3$ Films via Buffer-Layer Induced Misfit Strain Reversal
papers.abstract: Controlling ferroelectric phase symmetry through strain engineering is crucial for tailoring polarization topology and functional properties in oxide-based devices. Here, we show that a thin conductive buffer layer can override substrate-induced strain in BaTiO$_3$ (BTO) films on MgO. Although the lattice parameter of MgO(001) would be expected to induce tensile misfit strain, in 500~nm BaTiO$_3$ films the thermal-expansion mismatch dominates, resulting in effective compressive stress upon cooling. Inserting a 50-nm La$_{0.67}$Sr$_{0.33}$MnO$_3$ (LSMO) buffer layer reverses the effective strain state from compressive to tensile. Using temperature-dependent polarized Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and piezoresponse force microscopy, we reveal an unconventional phase sequence upon cooling: paraelectric $\rightarrow$ orthorhombic ($\textit{aa}$-phase, $\sim$407 K) $\rightarrow$ monoclinic ($\textit{r}$-phase, $\sim$300-345 K), characterized in-plane and tilted polarization components. The LSMO layer not only serves as a bottom electrode but also modifies the strain state, while interfacial charge redistribution induces a built-in electric field, evidenced by self-polarization and asymmetric PFM hysteresis. These findings highlight the critical role of conductive buffer layers in controlling ferroelectric symmetry and enabling oxide heterostructures with tailored polarization textures for low-power spintronics, tunable microwave devices, and neuromorphic computing.

papers.title: Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature in complex space forms
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a connected Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian surface of constant Gaussian curvature $K$ in a two-dimensional complex space form $\Mtilde^2(4ε)$ of constant holomorphic sectional curvature $4ε$, and let $H$ denote its mean curvature vector field. We prove that either $K=ε$ or $K=0\neε$ and $|H|$ is constant. In particular, if $|H|$ is non-constant, then $K=ε$.

papers.title: On the Stability of Power Systems with AI Data Centers: A Multi-Equilibrium Switched DAE Framework
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI) data centers is introducing dynamic loads into power transmission systems as GPU clusters switch between computational phases with distinct power demands. These dynamics are naturally modeled by switched affine differential-algebraic equations (DAEs), where each mode induces a different equilibrium and consistency space. We study their stability using control and hybrid systems tools. Differential projectors derived from the quasi-Weierstrass form yield an equivalent hybrid representation, from which we characterize the $ω$-limit set and establish Lyapunov conditions for practical stability with an explicit $\mathcal{KL}$ bound accounting for switching-induced resets. For stochastic inference workloads, we use Foster--Lyapunov techniques to establish probabilistic uniform global recurrence under mode-dependent dwell times and transition probabilities. The framework is validated on the IEEE 39-bus transmission network with co-located AI data centers using high-fidelity electromagnetic transient simulations of deterministic training and stochastic inference workloads.

papers.title: Geospatial Vector Geometry as a Native Spatial Modality for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Geospatial reasoning links VLMs to real-world action and decision making. Reliable reasoning requires accurate spatial information and effective spatial representations. However, current VLMs obtain this information mainly from language and vision. At larger geographic scales, limited visual observations make it difficult to establish accurate spatial references and recover precise spatial relations. This leads to a bottleneck for VLM spatial perception and reasoning. This paper proposes that geospatial vector geometry can become a native spatial modality within a VLM and introduces GeoVec-VLM. First, we develop a structured geometry representation that preserves the spatial structure and arrangement of vector objects, building an explicit spatial basis. Second, we introduce a geometry interaction strategy that brings this basis into multimodal computation, where it interacts with visual content and language references according to the queried spatial relations. Together, these designs allow perception and reasoning to operate on shared geometric references. Across five spatial reasoning tasks, GeoVec-VLM improves mean accuracy by about 11\% relative to the strongest baseline, maintains its gains under geographic transfer, and shows greater geometric consistency. Our results show that geospatial vector geometry offers a promising internal spatial basis for VLM spatial reasoning. https://github.com/TXFR/GeoVector-VLM

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Referenced Belief-Guided Q-Learning for Jammer Identification and Beam-Power Control in a mmWave Model
papers.abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are expected to support high data rates and reliable connectivity while meeting requirements for energy efficiency, resource management, and communication security. Digital Twin (DT) technology represents expected network behavior and enables the actual network state to be assessed against it. Integrating DT technology with reinforcement learning (RL) supports adaptive resource allocation and security-aware decision-making. This paper presents a simulation-based DT reference and a belief-guided Q-learning (BGQL) method for joint jammer identification and beam-power control in a site-specific 28-GHz network model. Receiver-level residuals between attack-free and attacked configurations are combined with candidate spatial jamming footprints and accumulated into a normalized suspicion vector. BGQL incorporates this vector into its state, reward, and exploratory beam-selection rule. Compared with SARSA, Greedy, and Random across 30 paired Monte Carlo runs per configuration, with known jammer counts, BGQL achieves link-rate scores of 437.4-564.2 Mbit/s, rate-to-device-power scores of 60.37-76.79 Mbit/J, and localization recall of 100% for one jammer and 78%-81% for two jammers. BGQL requires 80-130 s per run versus 5-14 s for SARSA. These findings provide a matched-model simulation proof of concept for DT-referenced belief-guided learning for security-aware beam-power control in 6G networks.

papers.title: Matching Full-Hessian Oracle Complexity for Nonconvex--Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.abstract: We characterize the oracle complexity of finding first-order stationary points in smooth nonconvex--strongly-concave (NC--SC) minimax optimization when each query provides the full Hessian in addition to the function value and gradient. For $Φ(x)=\max_y f(x,y)$, assume that $f$ has an $L$-Lipschitz gradient, a $ρ$-Lipschitz Hessian, and is $μ$-strongly concave in $y$. Let $κ=L/μ$, let $Δ$ denote the initial value gap, and define $r=ρκ^{3/2}\varepsilon/L^2$. We establish matching deterministic upper bounds and randomized lower bounds, up to logarithmic factors and additive initialization costs. When the leading term dominates initialization, the resulting minimax complexity is \[ \widetildeΘ\!\left( \frac{ΔL}{\varepsilon^2}Ψ_κ(r) \right), \qquad Ψ_κ(r)= \begin{cases} r^{1/2}, & 0<r\le 1,\\ r^{2/7}, & 1<r<κ^{7/4},\\ \sqrtκ, & r\geκ^{7/4}. \end{cases} \] Despite the stronger oracle, the optimal complexity exhibits a nontrivial dependence on accuracy, conditioning, and Hessian smoothness. In particular, these regimes exhibit accuracy dependencies $\varepsilon^{-3/2}$, $\varepsilon^{-12/7}$, and $\varepsilon^{-2}$, respectively. The upper bounds combine second-order regularity estimates for a saddle Moreau envelope with certified accelerated reduced-dual solves and amortized warm starts. The lower bounds combine an all-derivative lift with a serial composition of private-handle constructions, using hard instances chosen independently of the algorithm's realized random seed. The resulting characterization quantifies improvements over the classical first-order benchmark under gradient smoothness alone and identifies the regime in which that benchmark is recovered.

papers.title: TESS flares and chromospheric variability in the Pleiades, the Hyades, and Praesepe
papers.abstract: Magnetic activity is a result of the interaction between rotation and dynamo processes in cool stars with outer convection zones. Since open cluster members share a common age, distance, and chemical composition, they provide an opportunity to study the magnetic activity of cool stars in a controlled astrophysical context. We used 120s cadence observations from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to study the flare activity of stars in three open clusters with different ages: the Pleiades (100 Myr), the Hyades (700 Myr) and Praesepe (700 Myr). We used the Ohio State Multi-Object Spectrograph (OSMOS) at MDM Observatory with the goal of identifying coronal mass ejections (CMEs) in the Pleiades and Praesepe. We investigated the flaring characteristics of the cluster members using the TESS light curves: we identified the flares, then divided the dataset into different categories based on the effective temperature and light curve amplitude. We calculated the flare energies and investigated the flare frequency distributions. We studied the dynamic spectra of the H$α$ line and its environment to search for indication of CMEs. The power-law indices of the flare frequency distributions obtained in our analysis span the 1.8-2.8 range. We found the highest flare rates in the Pleiades for all investigated spectral types. Our results show that the flare rate of M dwarfs is similar in the Pleiades and the Hyades while for K-type stars the flare rate in the Pleiades is an order of magnitude higher.
