Our main theorem states that a subgroupoid is the image of a complete orbifold embedding if and only if it is both orbit saturated and stabilizer split. We then prove that these notions are Morita invariant: if two orbifold groupoids are Morita equivalent, then their orbit saturated and stabilizer split subgroupoids correspond naturally to each other. This solves an open problem raised by Mestre and Weilandt and explains why the embedding definition of Cho--Hong--Shin fails to be Morita invariant. Along the way we provide detailed examples, including the diagonal embedding, the non-split example of Borzellino and Brunsden, and explicit Morita equivalences.

papers.title: Extragradient and Past Extragradient Methods for $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz Variational Inequalities
papers.abstract: Variational inequalities (VIs) capture a broad class of optimization problems central to modern machine learning, including min-max optimization and equilibrium computation in multiplayer games. Traditionally, algorithms for solving VIs, such as Extragradient (EG) and Past Extragradient (PEG), have been analyzed under the standard $L$-Lipschitz assumption. However, this condition is often overly restrictive, and recent works have instead turned to the more relaxed $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz setting. Existing guarantees for $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz VIs require a quasi-sharpness condition [Vankov et al., 2024], while monotone guarantees for EG cover only unconstrained root finding [Choudhury and Loizou, 2025]. In this work, we provide the first convergence guarantees for EG and PEG for monotone $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz VIs. We also improve upon prior convergence guarantees for strongly monotone VIs by supporting larger stepsizes in the constrained setting and eliminating exponential dependence on the initial distance from the solution for convergence rates in the unconstrained setting. Lastly, we propose line-search variants for when Lipschitz parameters are unknown. Numerical experiments complement our theoretical results and demonstrate the practical efficacy of our methods.

papers.title: Transparency as Answerability: Role-Dependent Information Flow Modeling
papers.abstract: Transparency in AI-supported decision systems is widely required but poorly defined. Existing approaches treat transparency as a property of systems or components, producing characteristic failures: assessments that do not transfer across organizational boundaries, stakeholder questions that cannot be formulated within the available frame of analysis, and component-level findings that say nothing about system-level behavior. We propose treating transparency as a relation: a system is transparent to a stakeholder to the degree that their legitimate questions are answerable from its structure. We formalize this using information flow networks, in which transparency questions are expressed in terms of network structure and answerability is the condition that the system settles them. The framework supports three dimensions of analysis: structural answerability from the network alone, compositional answerability across organizational boundaries for deployed systems, and role-dependent answerability given a stakeholder's accessible sub-network. We demonstrate the framework on a real pre-integration assessment of an AI recruitment tool in a public sector municipality. The assessment uses participatory design and interviews to model the decision system structure. We show how structural and role-dependent transparency questions can be formally stated and analyzed across the Provider and Deployer boundary where the AI system is composed together with the deployer's decision process.

papers.title: Out-of-time-order hydrodynamics and scrambling
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamics as an effective field theory (EFT) has been immensely successful for predicting the behaviour of time-ordered correlation functions in the long-time, large-distance regime. In this paper, we analyse the predictions of hydrodynamics for scrambling as probed by out-of-time order correlators (OTOCs). To do so, we consider an all-derivative order generalisation of the Schwinger-Keldysh EFT of hydrodynamics extended to a four-fold time contour required to capture OTOCs. A crucial ingredient of the construction is a local SL(2,R) symmetry, which has previously been suggested as a mechanism for scrambling. We also derive this exact EFT from the microscopic formulation of the maximally chaotic low-temperature limit of the SYK lattice, thereby determining all transport coefficients for this model. As a novel application, we compute the OTOC of energy currents, find that its exponential growth saturates the chaos bound, and match it to expectations based on a shockwave (or scramblon) effective description. Our work shows that the universality of hydrodynamics degrees of freedom extends beyond traditional time-ordered correlators to more complex observables such as OTOCs.

papers.title: Thermal aliases in quantum noise: sampling clocks and pulse widths
papers.abstract: Can collective quantum-noise measurements distinguish different mode temperatures from one common temperature when the coupling spectrum is unknown? For stationary Gaussian oscillator environments, we derive a sharp bandwidth threshold for an exact thermal alias on the integer-time sampling lattice. The threshold depends on temperature order through the quantum response. For frequencies within the first alias period, fixing sufficient integer-time correlations makes one additional fractional-time fluctuation observation enough to exclude every common-temperature fit. A calibrated second pulse width provides another route through the same collective port: both widths must probe one spectrum and retain their measured variance scales. For a specified two-mode example, continuous-frequency certificates cover all common temperatures and uncertainty in a shared pulse ramp. A binary-readout protocol combines randomly interleaved matched references with collective-variance and coherence checks to handle Gaussian oscillator loss and predictable readout drift. The selected fractional-clock and two-width designs require approximately $3.8\times10^7$ and $1.6\times10^8$ outcomes for at most 5\% type-I error and at least 95\% power on the stated alternative class. These theoretical and numerical acquisition guarantees assume independently validated preparation, spectral support and control specifications; validation costs are additional. The result identifies which new observation makes thermal-model testing informative when mode-resolved access is unavailable.

papers.title: FORGE: Procedural Weight Generation for Sparse MoE Inference
papers.abstract: We introduce FORGE (Fast On-chip Rotor Generation for Experts), a procedural weight generation system for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference. Rather than storing and loading every expert weight tensor from HBM, we show how a compact accelerator inside each Streaming Multiprocessor can regenerate them on-the-fly from $O(\log^2 d)$ rotor parameters per projection. Per replaced layer, gigabytes of stored expert weights are approximated with under a megabyte of seeds. This addresses the dual memory bottleneck of autoregressive Sparse MoE decode, where per-expert FFN operations are HBM-bandwidth-bound at small routed-token counts and the aggregate expert footprint forces multi-node Expert Parallelism (EP) with all-to-all traffic. We realize the approach as the Rotor Generation Unit (RGU), a fixed-function datapath that generates FFN weight tiles without competing with Tensor Core execution. With 30% of the MoE FFN layers replaced across five Sparse MoE models, we estimate 1.3-2.8x higher system throughput at matched GPU count and 1.10-1.15x lower per-user decode latency at short context. In exchange, downstream accuracy on three model families falls below that of the same model fine-tuned without rotor replacement, and the replacement ratio controls this tradeoff. FORGE also expands KV cache capacity by 1.2-2.6x. It is agnostic to the bit width at which weights are stored, so it can compose with quantization. The RGU is fully implemented/verified in SystemVerilog at ~0.9% SM area overhead (0.032 mm^2/SM, 7nm).

papers.title: AI-Assisted Tumor-Growth Law Discovery from Sparse Data: Refitting and LLM-Based Ranking
papers.abstract: Inferring tumor-growth laws from sparse, noisy observations requires more than accurate curve fitting. We study an AI-assisted workflow involving symbolic regression, mathematical admissibility checks, coefficient refitting, and large language model (LLM) ranking. Synthetic Gompertz data allow trajectory fit, forecasting, and recovery of the governing growth law to be assessed separately. A dense noiseless control recovers the generating family, but sparse noisy sampling frequently leads to alternative forms. Among retained candidates in the tested configurations, physics-informed neural network refitting often increases growth-law error, whereas classical nonlinear least squares usually reduces it. A separate exploratory analysis of archived LLM rankings shows no consistent improvement over selection by training error and identifies errors in mathematical reasoning. Plausible saturation, accurate trajectory fits, and convincing explanations can therefore coexist with incorrect growth laws. Mathematical validity and law recovery require evaluation alongside predictive performance.

papers.title: Development of a Particle Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook Method for Rarefied Monatomic Gas Mixtures
papers.abstract: The Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method has long served as a reliable numerical approach for simulating rarefied and non-equilibrium gas flows. Its computational cost, however, increases rapidly as the flow approaches the near-continuum regime. This limitation has motivated the development of kinetic model equations that replace binary collisions with simplified relaxation processes. This paper presents a particle multi-relaxation unified BGK (UBGK) model for monatomic gas mixtures. The model retains pairwise species relaxation and determines the target velocity, temperature, shear stress, and heat flux by matching the corresponding production terms to those of the Boltzmann equation. A stochastic particle algorithm is developed. The model is implemented in SPARTA, and two validation problems are considered: homogeneous relaxation and a Mach 3 flow over a cylinder. In both cases, the UBGK solution reproduces the DSMC reference behavior, including species-dependent relaxation and non-equilibrium shock structure.

papers.title: Barycentric Guidance: Turning Foundation Image Editors into Continuous Affective Controllers
papers.abstract: Emotions are expressed on a continuum and are naturally described in the valence-arousal (VA) space. Existing VA-based image editors are typically training-based and domain-specific, limiting them to VA regions seen during training and making them brittle across datasets and domains. Meanwhile, despite producing high-quality edits, state-of-the-art foundation image editors are not continuous affective controllers: non-linear emotion representations in text encoders makes prompt interpolation poorly calibrated, so accurate and continuous VA control remains unreliable. To fill this gap, we introduce Barycentric Guidance, a training-free framework that turns pretrained foundation image editors into continuous affective controllers over VA, requiring no finetuning, extra data, or model changes. Our method maps any target VA point to simplex-based guidance weights, enabling VA controllability in three aspects: (i) accurate targeting of VA states, (ii) broad coverage across the VA plane, and (iii) continuous control. Across three face datasets, we improve VA target accuracy by 25-29%, expand VA-plane coverage by 28-50%, and increase expression diversity by 29-49%, over the strongest baseline. Unlike prior domain-specific methods, our training-free approach exploits the foundation model's inherent versatility, enabling generalization beyond human faces to animals, artworks, and complex scenes within a single framework. Code is available at https://github.com/harveymannering/BarycentricGuidance.

papers.title: Approximation Algorithms for Graphic Multi-Depot TSP and Graphic Multi-Path TSP
papers.abstract: We give improved approximation algorithms for two graphic TSP variants. First, we consider Multi-Depot TSP on graphic instances. In this variant, we are given an undirected graph with a set of depot vertices, and we are tasked with finding an Eulerian multi-edge set that connects each non-depot vertex to at least one depot. For this problem, Deppert, Kaul and Mnich (ESA 2023) presented a 3/2-approximation algorithm with running time exponential in the number of depots. We improve this result to a fully polynomial 3/2-approximation. Our algorithm is a variant of the classic Christofides-Serdyukov algorithm with an improved and simple analysis. On subcubic instances, we improve the approximation guarantee to 4/3 using the technique of removable pairings introduced by Mömke and Svensson (J. ACM 2016). We use a removable pairing to construct a set of disjoint cycles that can be completed to a cheap feasible solution. Second, we consider the Graphic Multi-Path TSP, which was previously considered by Alimi, Dahlmeier, Mömke, Pabst and Vargas Koch (SOSA 2026) who give a 2-approximation for this problem. Additionally, the authors present a reduction that shows that any better-than-two approximation for Graphic Multi-Depot TSP immediately leads to an improvement for Graphic Multi-Path TSP. We give an improved algorithm and analysis that yield an approximation guarantee of 1.9304.

papers.title: Mutual linearity from classical response theory
papers.abstract: We unify known mutual-linearity relations for Markov jump processes and chemical reaction networks within a common framework based on classical finite-response theory. In a Markov jump process, an exact finite-response identity shows that all stationary probability changes share a common factor when the rates of one edge change. Eliminating this factor gives the relations between probabilities, observables, and currents, even far from equilibrium. We also explain how the same argument applies when one coefficient of a linear system changes and recovers the known relations in Laplace space and between stationary complex activities in chemical reaction networks.

papers.title: Observe, Share, or Predict? Disentangling Partner Information in Embodied Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.abstract: LLMs are used as high-level controllers for embodied agents, but it remains unclear whether they support collaborative reasoning, such as anticipating a collaborator's actions in real-time teamwork without dialogue. We ask if observing the partner's state, exchanging object knowledge, and predicting the partner's next action, shape task outcomes and coordination when agents can share percepts but never intentions, plans, or task-level messages, and whether the two agents occupy symmetric roles. Using the Habitat-based PARTNR benchmark, we introduce a Decoupled Partial Observability regime that enforces strictly individual perception, and we augment decentralized zero-shot ReAct planners with Other Agent's State (OAS) observation, object Knowledge Exchange (KE) between co-located agents, and Other Agent's Next Action (OANA) prediction, evaluated on the full 2 x 2 x 2 grid with four planners on 1,000 validation tasks. OAS observation improves task quality, reducing extraneous effort for every planner, whereas KE primarily improves execution efficiency, cutting simulation steps by up to 25% with little change in success. The two are largely redundant for strong planners but complementary for the weakest, for which KE without the OAS is the worst configuration. OANA prediction lowers the success rate in 15 of 16 model x context pairs while raising explicit partner mentions to 55-100%, and its accuracy gains lie mainly in the coarse action type, partly because agents recognize the action the partner is already performing. The robot retrieves objects sooner and completes its tasks earlier than the simulated human. Shared context reduces total task time by shortening the remaining duration that the human works alone. Also, coordination benefits arise from responding to shared context, especially the OAS, rather than explicit anticipation, yielding shallow, planner-dependent partner modeling.

papers.title: Quantitative asymptotic error analysis and Richardson extrapolation for exponential Euler approximations of stochastic wave equations
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative weak convergence for the joint terminal law of the solution to a stochastic wave equation and the normalized error of its exponential Euler approximation. For multiplicative trace-class noise and spatial regularity $α\in(1,2]$, the normalized error converges to its limiting distribution at rate $O(m^{-(α-1)})$, where $m$ is the number of time steps. This estimate identifies the leading weak bias and yields a first-order weak-error expansion with remainder $O(m^{-α})$. Moreover, by canceling the leading weak-error term, we construct a Richardson extrapolation scheme with weak convergence order $α$ for $α\in(1,2]$ and show that this rate is sharp. To overcome the lack of parabolic smoothing and control the remainders amplified by normalization, we combine dimension-uniform regularity estimates for the joint Kolmogorov equation with a conditional weak expansion and backward transport of coefficient directions.

papers.title: DeepGroundRepair: From API-Grounded Generation to Shape-Aware Repair for Deep Learning Programs
papers.abstract: Deep learning programs are fundamental to modern AI applications, and automatically generating them from natural language requirements can substantially reduce DL development effort. Large language models have demonstrated promising capabilities for this direction. However, generated DL programs often remain unreliable because they must satisfy domain specific API usage constraints and tensor shape dependencies, violations of which can cause API level syntactic issues and runtime failures. Existing retrieval augmented generation and feedback guided code repair methods do not adequately address these DL specific constraints. In this paper, we propose DeepGroundRepair, a three stage framework that establishes a generation localization repair workflow to improve the reliability of LLM-generated DL programs. Its key idea is to progressively narrow the generation and repair spaces using DL specific knowledge and runtime tensor information. Specifically, it grounds generation in task-relevant API knowledge, localizes the upstream causes of tensor shape mismatch failures, and uses runtime tensor shapes to guide parameter repair. We evaluate DeepGroundRepair on the 100 model-level DL programming tasks in DeepEval using six open-weight LLMs across TensorFlow, PyTorch, and PaddlePaddle. We compare it with four baselines: two generation-only methods and their counterparts incorporating traceback guided self debugging. The results show that, relative to these baselines, DeepGroundRepair reduces the combined number of API-level syntactic issues by an average of 5.4 per 10 program files and achieves an average relative improvement of 85.3% in code executability. Compared with the two self debugging baselines, it improves semantic consistency by an average of 18.1% and reduces token cost by an average of 28.4%.

papers.title: Exponential Local Search in Bounded-Occurrence MAX-CSP
papers.abstract: We study the number of improving steps that local search may require for $(2,2,r)$-MCA (Maximum Constraint Assignment), a bounded-occurrence version of MAX-CSP with valued constraints in which every constraint involves at most two variables, every variable occurs in at most two constraints, and every variable takes one of $r$ values. We consider the flip neighborhood, where two assignments are neighbors if they differ in the value of exactly one variable; moving to such a neighbor is called a flip. Local search repeatedly performs improving flips, that is, flips that strictly increase the objective value, until a local optimum is reached. Our main result is that $(2,2,5)$-MCA has the all-exp property: there is an infinite family of instances with initial assignments for which every sequence of improving flips ending in a local optimum has length exponential in the number of variables. Thus, on these instances, local search requires exponentially many steps regardless of which improving flip is chosen at each step. This is the first all-exp result for $(2,2,r)$-MCA for any value of $r$, and our result extends to every $r\ge 5$. In contrast, for $(2,2,2)$-MCA every sequence of improving flips has length at most quadratic in the number of variables~\cite{Kaz2020,KCJ2020}. We give a short, direct proof of this result.

papers.title: Double Detonations on a Moving Mesh with $\texttt{Cattails}$: Characterizing Early Reddening in SNe Ia
papers.abstract: Type Ia supernovae are useful as cosmological distance indicators and are significant sources of chemical enrichment in galaxies, but much about their origins remains uncertain. The double detonation explosion mechanism is one promising model for these transients. We present a suite of thermonuclear hydrodynamic double detonation models of sub-Chandrasekhar mass white dwarfs spanning thin to thick helium shells. Thin shell models produce light curves and spectra consistent with normal Type Ia supernovae, and thicker shell models have early time luminosity bumps from radioactive ashes in the shell and early reddening in color sometimes observed in peculiar Type I supernovae. The reddening is due to line blanketing from heavy elements produced in the shell detonation encompassing the central emission. We perform the computations using $\texttt{Cattails}$, a moving mesh nuclear hydrodynamics code introduced in this work. After carrying out subsequent radiative transfer calculations using the $\texttt{Sedona}$ code, we relate the time of early reddening to the mass of the initial helium shell. We also consider how the relation changes as a function of total mass as well as how the peak brightness depends on the total mass. Finally, we provide a series of fitting functions that can be used to estimate the mass of the shell consistent with an observation of reddening in the early color evolution of a type Ia supernova.

papers.title: Borderline double phase functionals with powers of the logarithm: regularity in the vectorial case
papers.abstract: We study vector-valued local minimizers of the borderline double phase functional whose integrand is $|D\mathbf{w}|^p+a(x)|D\mathbf{w}|^p\log^γ(e+|D\mathbf{w}|)$, where $p>1$, $γ>0$ and the coefficient $a(\cdot)$ is nonnegative and bounded. If the modulus of continuity $ω(\cdot)$ of $a(\cdot)$ satisfies $ω(r)\log^γ(1/r)\to0$ as $r\to0$, then minimizers are locally Hölder continuous for every exponent less than one. If $a(\cdot)$ is Hölder continuous, then the gradients of minimizers are locally Hölder continuous. In the vector-valued setting these results were previously available only for $γ=1$. The proof combines a comparison with frozen functionals, whose regularity theory applies uniformly in the frozen coefficient, with the higher integrability of minimizers.

papers.title: Solution Set Dimensions in Convex Optimization and Primal-Polar Facial Signatures
papers.abstract: We study the possible dimensions of solution sets in linearly perturbed convex optimization problems and their behavior under convex duality. The dimensions of solution sets and inverse solution sets capture two complementary forms of nonuniqueness: that of optimal solutions for a given perturbation, and that of perturbations for which a given point is optimal. Although these two families are linked by Fenchel conjugacy, we show that their collections of dimensions can be prescribed independently for finite supercoercive convex functions. As a geometric consequence, we prove that the facial dimension signatures of a convex body and its polar can be prescribed independently. The connection between these two realization results is obtained by homogenizing the epigraphs of a function and its conjugate. In contrast, under simultaneous facial exposedness, we establish a dimensional obstruction relating the smallest positive proper face dimensions of the body and its polar. These results resolve two open questions posed by Roshchina and Tunçel.

papers.title: Neural Bayesian Networks for Modular and Scalable Decision-Making Under Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Bayesian Networks (BNs) are established tools for letting agents reason under uncertainty in sequential decision-making. They split a joint distribution into local conditional mechanisms arranged on a directed acyclic graph, which makes them modular, interpretable, and ready to perform probabilistic inference. Their classical formulation, however, has limitations in both expressiveness and scale: each conditional is usually stored as a table or a linear-Gaussian form, and inference evaluates the graph one node and one query at a time. In this paper we introduce Neural Bayesian Networks (NBNs), in which each conditional is a differentiable, tensor-valued mechanism, while the graph and its factorization are unchanged. NBNs retain the modularity and local mechanisms of BNs, can represent any learnable conditional distribution, and run natively on GPUs. We also release NBN, a PyTorch-based library for learning and inference in NBNs, together with a public benchmark. Our evaluation shows gains in both expressiveness and scale: NBNs fit distributions that classical BN libraries struggle to represent, and on large networks and large batches of queries they run two orders of magnitude faster thanks to GPU parallelization. NBN is available at https://github.com/Giovannibriglia/NeuralBayesianNetworks.

papers.title: Initial Performance Tests of MASTA for Wide-Field Narrowband Imaging
papers.abstract: Wide-field narrowband imaging provides an efficient approach for mapping low-surface-brightness line emission over large angular scales. We present initial performance tests of Multi-Application Survey Telescope Array (MASTA) for narrowband imaging. Using commissioning data obtained with the QHY461 and COSMOS-8K cameras, we characterize the basic reduction procedure, photometric calibration, image quality, and point-source detection limits. The measured surface-brightness and point-source detection limits become deeper with increasing exposure time, roughly following the expected background-limited scaling. Under the current observing and reduction conditions, the COSMOS-8K camera generally reaches deeper surface-brightness limits, particularly in the red filters, while QHY461 has smaller pixel size and provides better sampling of the telescope point spread function (PSF). As demonstrations, we perform continuum subtraction for the nearby galaxy M106 and the supernova remnant Cygnus Loop using adjacent narrowband filters and reveal the Hα and [O III] structures in M106 and filamentary structures in the Cygnus Loop. We further compare the MASTA surface brightness Hα map of M106 with an independent SITELLE measurement. After accounting for [N II] contamination and the wavelength-dependent response of the 6544 Å filter in the f /1.7 converging beam, the corrected median ratio is 0.973. These tests indicate that MASTA is a promising facility for wide-field narrowband imaging. Further improvements in calibration frames, including flux calibration, field-dependent bandpass characterization, and spatially varying PSF modeling and matching will be required for quantitative studies of diffuse ionized gas.

papers.title: Exponential profiles for the intrinsic volumes of Orlicz balls
papers.abstract: An Orlicz ball is the set of points where the sum of a fixed even convex function of the coordinates does not exceed a given radius, here proportional to the dimension. For a broad class of such functions, including non-homogeneous ones, we find the exponential rate of the intrinsic volumes whose order is proportional to the dimension and express it by a two-parameter variational formula involving only one-dimensional integrals. As a function of the order-to-dimension ratio, this rate is concave and continuous on the closed unit interval, and the convergence is uniform in the order. This proves the exponential-profile conjecture of Kabluchko, Marynych, and Prochno for these bodies and recovers their result for $\ell_p$ balls with $p>1$. The proof relies on the theory of large deviations. An exact formula for the Laplace transform of the intrinsic volumes in the radius, extending theirs for $\ell_p$ balls, plays the role of a moment generating function, and a Laplace method gives its exponential rate. An exponential change of measure, analogous to that used in Cramér's theorem, then recovers the intrinsic volumes. The key step is a lower bound on the tilted density at its mean, obtained from log-concavity rather than a law of large numbers.

papers.title: Counterfactual Action-Conditioned Graph Prediction for Cascading-Failure Mitigation in Power Systems
papers.abstract: Cascading failures develop through coupled power flow redistribution, protection actions, and topology changes, making remedial control dependent on how alternative interventions modify the subsequent trajectory. This paper develops an action-conditioned graph predictor (ACGP) for multi-step cascade prediction and closed-loop mitigation. A same-state counterfactual branching procedure replays identical post-contingency grid states under multiple legal actions while preserving the exogenous trajectory, providing direct supervision for action-dependent electrical states, line connectivity, automatic protection trips, and terminal risk. ACGP is embedded in a receding-horizon controller that evaluates five-step candidate futures, executes the selected intervention, and replans from the observed next state. The final dataset contains 2,860 counter factual roots and 22,880 action-conditioned branches. On the held-out test set, ACGP achieves a five-step line-loading MAE of 0.0369 and a redispatch pairwise ranking accuracy of 0.806; action ablations reduce the ranking accuracy to approximately chance level. In closed-loop Grid2Op experiments, terminal-failure and cascade rates decrease from 53.3% and 51.1% under do-nothing operation to 12.2% and 7.8%, respectively, close to the simulator-reference values of 11.1% and 6.7%. The results show that same-state counterfactual prediction can support effective action comparison and feedback-based cascading-failure mitigation.

papers.title: Mining Cross-Modal Perception Gaps in Autonomous Driving: When Camera and LiDAR Disagree
papers.abstract: Multi-modal fusion for 3D object detection assumes that cameras and LiDAR are broadly complementary. In practice, how much each modality is trusted at a given location is decided by learned weights that are neither characterized nor auditable. We label every ground-truth object by which modalities detected it, then mine the resulting 0.4M-object database across nuScenes, KITTI, and Waymo. Because the patterns shift with distance from the ego vehicle, we read the mined model through Spatially Stratified Feature Attribution (SSFA), which conditions Shapley attribution on distance zones and exposes structure that global attribution averages away. Three assumptions built into the current fusion design do not hold. The modality-preference boundary tracks the object itself: a traffic cone is nearly six times as likely as a truck to be seen by the camera alone (16.8% vs. 2.9%), regardless of range. Camera-only detections peak at 10-30 m, inside the band usually ceded to LiDAR, and fall away on either side. The drivers of failure are not additive either: the distance - density interaction alone outweighs the entire main effect of viewing direction. We further find that modality dominance is directionally non-stationary, with objects behind the vehicle being markedly more LiDAR-dominant than those in front. We compile the mined structure into a Modality Reliability Map and inject it into four pretrained fusion detectors through a lightweight attention layer. This improves performance by up to 1.3 mean Average Precision (mAP) while fine-tuning under 4% of their parameters in 2-3 GPU-hours. Our work lifts reliability out of the weights and treats it as a quantity that can be examined before deployment. That is what a safety measure for multi-modal perception must rest on.

papers.title: Friends as Sensors: High-Sensitivity Monitoring of Misinformation and Platform Dynamics via the Friendship Paradox
papers.abstract: The friends of a randomly chosen social media user are, on average, better connected than the user, a network property known as the friendship paradox. We use it to monitor misinformation on Twitter/X around the 2024 US election, comparing roughly 27 million tweets from random users with 31 million from the accounts they retweet, which we call sensors. Sensors share news of about the same quality as random users, because news quality follows the political orientation of linked outlets and not the user's position in the network. News links rated by NewsGuard reach sensors a median of 70 minutes earlier, across the quality spectrum. Over the election window, right-leaning content rises about 2.5-fold in visibility, measured as impressions per tweet, among sensors but not among random users. Friendship-paradox sampling therefore cannot separate low-quality from high-quality news, but it detects news early and tracks what a platform makes visible.

papers.title: ConDenseDrive: Knowledge-Dense, Token-Sparse Visual Encoder for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: End-to-end driving requires rich spatiotemporal representations to support scene understanding and trajectory planning under strict latency constraints. However, most systems initialize their visual encoders from generic image pretraining and densely process all patch tokens for each camera view and input frame, limiting both representation quality and inference efficiency. To address these challenges, we present ConDenseDrive, a knowledge-dense and token-sparse visual encoder for end-to-end autonomous driving. Our three-stage framework first makes the encoder knowledge-dense by distilling complementary visual, semantic, and geometric knowledge from three vision foundation models. It then adapts the distilled encoder to multi-frame end-to-end driving and integrates spatiotemporal context into register tokens for planning. Finally, it makes the encoder token-sparse by applying register-guided token compression, reducing redundant patch computation and yielding a 2.0$\times$ speedup while improving planning performance. ConDenseDrive achieves 94.5 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.8 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, and reaches 37.4 HD-Score in zero-shot evaluation on HUGSIM. Extensive experiments and qualitative analyses demonstrate that visual encoder design provides an effective route to reliable and efficient end-to-end driving.

papers.title: Sequence spaces of Baire-one functions and their porosity
papers.abstract: We consider several families of sequences of Baire-one self-maps of $[0,1]$ investigated by A. Alikhani-Koopaei. They form a chain of inclusions where each space is closed and nowhere dense in the next one. We prove that each space is lower $2/3$-porous in the next one. If one modifies these families where sequences of Baire-one functions are real-valued uniformly bounded, then they are Banach spaces and each space of the respective chain is c-porous in the next one.

papers.title: QUARZ: a quasi-static particle-in-cell code with non-uniform radial grids for plasma wakefields
papers.abstract: We present a quasi-static particle-in-cell scheme for beam-driven plasma wakefields in cylindrical geometry that works on an arbitrary non-uniform radial grid. The field equations are discretized with hat-function finite elements and conservative finite volumes on any monotone set of radial nodes, and the transverse magnetic field is obtained explicitly, without iterations, following Baxevanis and Stupakov. An optional azimuthal mode $m=1$ describes beam offsets, tilts and hosing. The discretization keeps the discrete Gauss law exact, deposits a uniform plasma exactly on every node including the axis, and remains second-order accurate on smoothly stretched grids. Resolution can therefore be placed where the physics needs it. For a tightly focused witness beam that pulls the plasma ions onto the axis, a grid that is fine only near the axis gives the same near-axis fields as a uniform grid with the same axis resolution, with thirty times fewer cells and in thirty times less computing time. Such a grid also resolves the singular closure of a cold-plasma bubble, which a uniform grid hides by smoothing it over one cell; smoothing the plasma sources over a fixed length, chosen independently of the grid, regularizes the closure and makes the wake behind it converge. The scheme is implemented in the open-source C++/Kokkos code QUARZ (Quasistatic Arbitrary-resolution RZ), which runs on CPUs and GPUs and uses MPI with a pipelined decomposition along the co-moving coordinate. Simulations of the self-modulation of the AWAKE proton bunch agree with the three-dimensional code HiPACE++. QUARZ is, to our knowledge, the first production-grade simulation code in plasma physics that is \emph{zero-touch}: all of its source code, tests and documentation were written by an AI agent directed by a physicist who did not write a single line of the code.

papers.title: Audit tools of the trade: Automated Auditor Elicitation Can Be Sensitive to the Context the Auditor Is Given
papers.abstract: Does providing additional context to automated AI auditors improve their effectiveness? Using the Petri tool to audit LLM coding agents, we test the impact of providing two types of resources (an external codebase and benchmark transcripts) to LLM auditors, across four auditor-target LLM pairs and three behaviours (harmful compliance, reward hacking, sycophancy). (1) External codebase: We provide the auditor LLM with a fixed, external open source codebase, which prior work finds improves the realism of synthetic audits. Providing this resource suppresses reward hacking in both auditor-target pairs whose baseline rate is above the floor (4.8 to 1.3 and 3.9 to 1.8 on Petri's default 1-10 scale); the remaining two pairs sit at the floor throughout. The suppression recurs in three of four pairs under a different scenario and resource bundle. (2) External benchmark transcripts: We provide the auditor with transcripts of the target's performance on benchmarks measuring similar behaviours, intended to inform the auditor about the target's behavioural patterns. Providing this resource raises reward hacking scores in all four pairs (from 1.7 to 6.1 in one case). However, subsequent experiments show that supplying only the related benchmark's abstract, without transcripts, also increases reward hacking, and the effect is absent under a different framing of the same behaviour. Overall, we find no consistent effect of either resource outside reward hacking, but we find substantial variability in judge-scored behaviour across conditions. Our results underscore the importance of careful piloting with tools such as Petri, as the measured rate of target behaviour is highly sensitive to configuration decisions. We hope our results inspire more research into the reliability and robustness of automated alignment auditing.

papers.title: Rigid Bodies as Accidental Seismoscopes: Exact Time Stepper Inversion and an Estimate of Ground Acceleration in the 2026 La Guaira Earthquake
papers.abstract: An unknown ground excitation is recovered from the measured response of a rigid body sliding in two dimensions on an inclined surface under Coulomb friction, a system with no classical solution, whose sampled trajectories come from a time stepper. The Moreau stepper is shown to admit an exact inverse, explicit, non-iterative and vectorizable, giving the ground acceleration over each step in closed form, without regularization or an assumed source model. The inverse evaluates the friction direction at the end of the step, not its beginning. Inverting the continuous equation instead is not a secondary discretization choice: the two inverses differ by an exact identity proportional to the rotation of the sliding direction within the step, bounded by twice the frictional deceleration, which is of order one g for typical interfaces. The identity is inactive in one dimension, which explains why the sliding block literature has not confronted it. Verification against a manufactured reference solution recovers it to machine precision. On the field record, the discrepancy reaches 0.10g in root mean square, which exceeds the whole propagated uncertainty of the reported peak, and it suppresses 17% of the recovered travel, behaving as a bias, not noise, so root-mean-square agreement in acceleration understates it. The method is applied to surveillance video of a delineator post that slid in the 24 June 2026 La Guaira earthquake, yielding a peak ground acceleration of 0.912 +/- 0.047g, and a lower bound of 0.47g independent of the imagery. Displaced rigid bodies can therefore provide quantitative ground-motion information where instruments are absent.

papers.title: Simultaneous Matrix-Free HSS Compression and Factorization with Adaptive Ranks
papers.abstract: Many dense matrices in scientific computing have hierarchically low-rank off-diagonal structure but are accessible only through routines that apply the matrix and, in general, its transpose or adjoint to vectors, that is, through matrix--vector products (matvecs). We present a fully matrix-free algorithm that compresses such a matrix into Hierarchically Semi-Separable (HSS) form and factorizes it simultaneously with the off-diagonal ranks chosen adaptively from a prescribed tolerance. The method uses $\mathcal{O}(k)$ matvecs with each operator, where $k$ is the largest off-diagonal rank found. Building on fixed-rank block nullification, it samples the matrix in small random batches and enlarges each local basis until a randomized error estimate falls below the tolerance. Unitary nullspace updates give $\mathcal{O}(k^3)$ local dense work, the same asymptotic cost as when the ranks are known in advance. Because compression and elimination proceed together, no separate factorization step is required. Excluding the matvecs, the factorization uses $\mathcal{O}(N)$ arithmetic and storage when the off-diagonal ranks are bounded, and its inverse is applied in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time. Experiments on Poisson and Helmholtz Schur complements, Matérn covariance matrices, and a complex Lippmann--Schwinger equation demonstrate the factorization as both a direct solver and a preconditioner on problems with up to millions of unknowns.

papers.title: FOCUS: A Subspecialty Foundation Model for Intraoperative Central Nervous System Pathology
papers.abstract: Intraoperative frozen-section diagnosis of central nervous system (CNS) lesions guides surgical decisions but is challenged by artefacts, diagnostic complexity and time constraints. Most pathology foundation models have limited exposure to CNS frozen tissue. Here we present FOCUS, a subspecialty foundation model pretrained on 27,930 frozen-section whole-slide images enriched for CNS tissue. FOCUS ranked first across all 11 diagnostic and 12 biomarker-prediction tasks in the internal test cohort, achieving mean AUCs of 0.969 and 0.877, respectively. This advantage was retained in the temporal and external test cohorts. We further organized a WHO-aligned diagnostic hierarchy, where FOCUS also outperformed comparator models. In a reader study, FOCUS assistance enabled junior readers to approach or exceed unassisted senior readers in hierarchical diagnostic accuracy and granularity. More importantly, FOCUS assistance enabled readers to correctly identify a mean of 63.0% of initially missed lymphoma cases (73.2% among junior readers), potentially avoiding unnecessary extensive resection. These findings highlight the potential of FOCUS to provide clinically actionable support for intraoperative CNS pathology and inform surgical decisions.

papers.title: Mutual information across the commensurate--incommensurate crossover and near the Kosterlitz--Thouless point of the spin-$\tfrac12$ $J_1$--$J_2$ Heisenberg chain
papers.abstract: What quantum mutual information adds to conventional correlation functions is often unclear. We study the spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg chain, using DMRG on infinite chains and periodic rings and an SU(2) decomposition of the mutual information into correlation channels. For singlet ground states the two-site mutual information is an exact function of the spin correlator, so any additional content must come from blocks. In the dimerized phase, blocks resolve bond-energy correlations in the SU(2)-scalar channel without an independent asymptotic length: singlet and triplet correlation lengths agree to about 1%. The scalar channel dominates block mutual information at large distances in the commensurate regime up to $J_2/J_1=0.40$, but falls to a few percent beyond the disorder point, which coincides numerically with the Majumdar-Ghosh point $J_2/J_1=1/2$; the structure-factor peak splits only at the Lifshitz point $J_2/J_1=0.520622(2)$. On the gapless side we compare block mutual information on rings extrapolated to infinite size with the two-interval prediction of SU(2)$_1$ conformal field theory across the Kosterlitz-Thouless point $J_2/J_1=0.241167$. There, for block lengths $l\le6$, the correction decays as $l^{-p}$ with $p=1.96$-$2.07$, and any logarithmic term is at least 60 times smaller than in the Heisenberg chain. Expanding in the marginal coupling (from level spectroscopy) the first-order coefficient is consistent with $l^{-2}$ scaling and the second-order coefficient is positive for $x\le1/4$, suggesting that the mutual information relative to the field-theory value becomes stationary at the KT point for large blocks. The scalar-channel share approaches 1/4 at small cross ratio $x$, as expected from SO(4) symmetry; under two stated assumptions its first-order response to the coupling is $(3/8)\ln x-5/8$ at small $x$, matched by the $l=4$ data within 1-3% at $x\le1/9$.

papers.title: Transparent Information Flow Modeling for Role-Aware AI Act Assessment
papers.abstract: The European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act introduces a structured framework for governing high-risk AI systems, emphasizing transparency, risk management, and role-specific accountability. However, current assessment practices often rely on monolithic system views or disconnected checklists, limiting their ability to capture the socio-technical complexity of real-world deployments. We explore the use of the Information Flow Methodology (IFM), a modeling-based approach to AI Act compliance assessment. IFM represents decision systems -- whether algorithmic, human, or hybrid -- as networks of information sites and transformation channels, enabling structured analysis of how information, decisions, and responsibilities flow across organizational and technical boundaries. We apply IFM in a real-world case involving a recruitment support tool used by a public-sector organization, evaluating both the Provider's system and the Deployer's recruitment process. Our results demonstrate that IFM can serve as a scaffold to bridge both component-based and holistic perspectives, and how technical systems are situated within socio-technical contexts. In doing so, IFM supports transparency, identifies risk pathways, and enables alignment analysis between intended and actual use. We argue that such modeling provides a foundational tool for effective, context-sensitive AI governance and accountability -- offering capabilities beyond conventional checklist-based assessments.

papers.title: Second-order fluids and the choice of objective derivative
papers.abstract: We generalize the second-order fluid constitutive model to accommodate a range of possible frame indifferent time derivatives. Using the Gordon--Schowalter derivative, which contains the upper-convected, lower-convected, and corotational (Jaumann-Zaremba) derivatives as subsets, we show how the subjective choice of derivative may change model predictions and we identify features that remain universal independent of this choice. Writing these models in terms of generic coefficients is non-universal and may lead to misinterpretations of flow predictions. However, writing the models in terms of zero-shear material functions or terminal relaxation time reveals universal and robust representations.

papers.title: Physics-informed Neural Networks Based on the Fokker-Planck Model for Rarefied Gas Flows
papers.abstract: Rarefied nonequilibrium flows are described by the Boltzmann equation, which can be solved using stochastic particle or deterministic methods. With advances in computing, data-assisted physics-informed neural networks have been widely used for flow prediction by combining governing equations with measured or computed data. Data-free PINNs do not require such training data and have been widely studied for continuum flows, but their application to rarefied flows remains limited. This study develops a data-free Fokker-Planck physics-informed neural network (FP-PINN) to describe rarefied nonequilibrium flows. The physics loss is constructed from the ellipsoidal statistical Fokker-Planck (ES-FP) equation using a velocity distribution function (VDF) closure and moment projection. The FP-PINN is evaluated for a steady one-dimensional Mach 10 normal shock. The FP-PINN results agree with the numerical ES-FP results, with errors below $1\%$. Compared with the particle ES-FP results, the FP-PINN predicts a sharper shock structure with errors up to $17\%$. This difference is attributed to the VDF closure and moment projection.

papers.title: A Power-Trajectory Framework for Data Center Participation in Day-Ahead Markets
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) is driving substantial growth in data center electricity demand. Interval-based energy blocks in day-ahead markets do not explicitly retain predictable intra-interval demand evolution, potentially creating mismatches with ramp-feasible generation trajectories and affecting settlement. This paper proposes a power-trajectory framework in which data centers declare predictable aggregate demand evolution through continuous demand-side power trajectories before market clearing. The declared trajectories are treated as exogenous inputs for constructing generation trajectories and the corresponding price trajectory. For feasible market-clearing outcomes, physical temporal consistency is established through continuous-time power balance and satisfaction of the modeled generation operating constraints, while economic temporal consistency is established by preserving the dispatch-price correspondence in energy settlement on a common temporal basis. Under the adopted settlement definitions, a trajectory-based settlement analysis separately quantifies the monetary magnitude of representation-induced power imbalances and the supply-side compensation that may remain under temporally consistent clearing and settlement. An illustrative 5-bus case demonstrates the elimination of representation-induced power imbalance and identifies the timing and physical sources of supply-side compensation. A modified IEEE RTS-GMLC case further illustrates these compensation effects across multiple generating units under workload-driven data center demand variations.

papers.title: ML Engineering Agents - A Data Management Perspective
papers.abstract: Machine learning engineering (MLE) agents are emerging as a new paradigm for automating end-to-end ML pipeline development. Using large language models for code generation and predictive performance as a machine-gradable feedback signal, these agents iteratively synthesize, execute, and refine pipeline code. Yet current systems are largely evaluated on pre-built, single-table benchmarks that abstract away key data management challenges. This tutorial introduces the foundations of MLE agents and highlights research opportunities for the database community. We cover how agents combine program synthesis with iterative and evolutionary optimization, and discuss open challenges in efficient pipeline execution, data discovery and augmentation over heterogeneous sources, reliability and debugging, as well as fairness and compliance. We connect these challenges to existing data management techniques and conclude with a hands-on session using contemporary MLE agents.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of coupled electromagnetic and mass fields
papers.abstract: We formulate a unified thermodynamic framework for chemical, mechanical, and electromagnetic transport by extending the Gibbs--Duhem relation to include kinetic free-energy contributions associated with material and field motion. The resulting kinetic Gibbs--Duhem relation establishes a thermodynamic connection between free-energy variations, generalized chemical potentials, pressure, and transport momentum, while preserving the invariance of the system free energy under changes of reference frame. Within a Lagrangian formulation of free-energy evolution, the relation provides a common structure for diffusion, momentum transport, and electromagnetic dynamics. For nonuniform chemical systems, the framework recovers the coupling between Cahn--Hilliard dynamics and the Korteweg stress arising from composition gradients. Its extension to electromagnetic systems incorporates electric, magnetic, charge, and mechanical contributions into the same thermodynamic formulation, yielding a unified description of electromagnetic and momentum evolution. The framework further separates dissipative from nondissipative transport and establishes a common thermodynamic form for mechanical and electromagnetic propagation. In the isentropic limit, the characteristic propagation velocity is determined by the derivative of the thermodynamic pressure with respect to density, yielding the speed of sound for mechanical systems and the speed of light for electromagnetic systems. These results show that kinetic contributions can be incorporated consistently into the Gibbs--Duhem framework, providing a common thermodynamic basis for coupled chemical, mechanical, and electromagnetic transport without introducing separate thermodynamic principles for each mechanism.

papers.title: Multi-Objective Amortized CDRH3 Sequence Sampling Diversifies Promising Antibody Candidates
papers.abstract: Antibody therapeutics have transformed treatment across diverse therapeutic areas and have become central to modern medicine. While recent machine learning approaches aim to accelerate antibody discovery through structure-based design and target-affinity optimization, successful candidates must also satisfy broad developability constraints, including structural compatibility, low immunogenicity, and favorable biophysical properties, while remaining sufficiently diverse to provide sufficient coverage of design space to mitigate later-stage development failures. We introduce a preference-conditioned multi-objective generative flow network (GFN) fine-tuning pipeline for fixed-framework CDRH3 loop redesign that fine-tunes a biological sequence model against many inexpensive proxies covering backbone compatibility, sequence likelihood, immunogenicity risk, novelty, and developability liabilities. It combines up to fourteen predictive rewards in a single policy trained to sample CDRH3 loops across 623 SAbDab antibody structures, leveraging a reward reduction strategy to preserve Pareto dominance under this learned map. We also introduce a novel autoregressive span-in-filling variant of AMPLIFY-350M that serves both as a scaffold-conditioned CDRH3 generation prior and as a direct conditional likelihood scorer. We evaluated reward scores, diversity, and design quality on loops sampled on 45 held-out antibody complexes to assess structural consistency, confidence, aggregation propensity, stability, and antigen binding. Compared with the inverse-folding methods ProteinMPNN and ESM-IF, our approach produces roughly 10x more distinct acceptable candidates per design at 50% sequence identity, while holding 10% of the 14-objective Pareto front pooled across methods, trading per-sample quality for greater exploration of novel possible structures.

papers.title: Time Window Optimization for Motor Imagery Classification via Temporal Structure Embedded Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Online motor imagery-based brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) typically decode continuous EEG using fixed-length sliding windows that may be misaligned with neural events. Existing window optimization methods often evaluate windows independently, overlooking temporal dependencies and potentially producing fragmented or physiologically implausible selections. We propose Temporal Structure Embedded Reinforcement Learning (TSE-RL), a framework that incorporates prior knowledge of MI event structure into a constrained Markov decision process for adaptive window optimization. First, TSE-RL assigns each window an explicit semantic role through Discard, Onset, Sustain, or Offset actions, extending binary retain/discard decisions to event-level alignment. Second, a finite-state machine masks invalid actions to enforce the temporal order of MI phases and promote physiologically plausible window sequences. Third, a Transformer-based history encoder captures dependencies across windows, improving training stability and computational efficiency compared with recurrent architectures. TSE-RL is plug-and-play and can be integrated with diverse MI classifiers. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate consistent improvements in decoding performance in both cross-session and cross-subject settings. Visualization analyses further suggest that the learned window selection policy aligns with neurophysiological principles.

papers.title: Semiclassical Moser--Trudinger type inequalities for orthonormal families in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: For $H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$-orthonormal families $\{u_n\}_{n=1}^N$ with one-body density $ρ=\sum_{n=1}^N |u_n|^2$, we prove the whole-space endpoint Moser--Trudinger inequality $$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\frac{e^{4πρ(x)}-1-4πρ(x)}{ρ(x)}\,dx \le C\left(N-1+\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}ρ(x)\,dx\right), $$ where the integrand on the left-hand side is defined to be zero on $\{x: ρ(x)=0\}$. We develop a heat-semigroup refinement of Rumin's density method to treat both the endpoint coefficient $4π$ and the whole-space setting. Our inequality is sharp in two respects: the optimality of the coefficient $4π$ and the linear growth in the rank $N$. Moreover, through a semiclassical analysis of the density generated by normalized Dirichlet eigenfunctions, we establish the collective asymptotic behaviors of the quantities appearing in the inequality in various regimes. These semiclassical behaviors show that the rank-dependent term $N-1$ on the right-hand side is indispensable.

papers.title: Minimax Optimality of Shampoo for Nonstationary Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We develop a comprehensive theoretical analysis of Matrix Shampoo for tracking time-varying optima in nonstationary stochastic optimization. We derive finite-horizon high-probability bounds for average tracking error that disentangle initialization, optimizer drift, momentum-induced drift penalty, stochastic noise, and adaptive preconditioning, with explicit dependence on momentum parameter \(β_1\) and stabilization parameter \(\varepsilon\). These bounds reveal an explicit drift--noise and stability--geometry tradeoffs: noise-dominated regimes favor larger $β_1$, which provides stronger first-moment averaging and greater suppression of gradient noise, whereas drift-dominated regimes favor smaller $β_1$, allowing faster adaptation to moving optimizer. Larger $\varepsilon$ reduces the preconditioner-perturbation term while weakening Shampoo's ability to exploit matrix geometry, thereby reducing adaptivity. We establish a matching minimax lower bound under squared path-variation constraint, proving the information-theoretic optimality of Shampoo over the class of causal optimization procedures. Under a constant stepsize, we establish high-probability bounds for the average projected stationarity gap along general nonstationary nonconvex objectives. We validate our theoretical findings on both synthetic and multiple real-world problems.

papers.title: FidLIF: Parallel Training of High-Fidelity Spiking Neurons with Exact BPTT
papers.abstract: Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) show promise in energy-efficient computing through event-driven computation and stateful temporal processing, their recurrent membrane dynamics render their training inherently sequential and inefficient for long sequences. Existing methods achieve full-sequence parallelism in SNNs through two main strategies: redesigning or approximating spiking dynamics to avoid reset-coupled temporal dependencies, or relying on iterative relaxed fixed-point solvers that suffer from excessive memory costs and iteration-dependent backward overhead. To address these limitations, we present FidLIF, a novel framework that reconciles the incremental update and hard-reset behavior of standard spiking LIF neurons with parallel forward propagation and BPTT-equivalent backward propagation. FidLIF iteratively recovers the full-sequence membrane-potential trajectory in parallel. By exploiting the lower bidiagonal structure induced by the local recurrence of LIF neurons, FidLIF formulates each forward trajectory correction and backward adjoint propagation as associative scans with an $O(\log T)$ temporal depth. This formulation also supports input-dependent neuronal parameters and allows the same neuron to perform full-sequence parallel training and incremental step-by-step inference at deployment. In our numerical convergence evaluation, FidLIF achieves a mean absolute error below $10^{-7}$ relative to the matched serial relaxed LIF dynamics, while yielding gradients numerically equivalent to exact BPTT. Our Triton implementation delivers favorable long-sequence latency and memory scaling, while achieving competitive performance on four sequential classification benchmarks. By reconciling parallel training with step-by-step execution, FidLIF enables high-fidelity spiking dynamics to benefit from parallel hardware without compromising incremental inference at deployment.

papers.title: Comparing GenAI to Machine Learning and Manual Review for eDiscovery
papers.abstract: Keeling et al. [Keeling2026Generative] report on a case study recently conducted by Redgrave LLP in which they assert that Relativity's Generative AI Review tool (aiR) achieved 88% recall while Relativity Assisted Learning (RAL), its machine-learning tool, achieved 64% recall. These results are not comparable because the methods employed have different objectives, because of inter-assessor disagreement, and because they represent different recall-precision and cost-benefit trade-offs. Our analysis of the Redgrave data indicates that, when these differences are taken into account, aiR and manual review are comparable. Furthermore, established machine-learning models employing Continuous Active Learning (CAL) and Scalable Continuous Active Learning (S-CAL) show state-of-the-art effectiveness, and superior efficiency, when trained only on a sample of 2,000 first-pass-reviewer responsiveness determinations.

papers.title: Graph Distortion Distances, Gromov-Hausdorff and the Hardness of Gromov-Wasserstein
papers.abstract: We study the computational complexity of graph distortion distances, a family of graph metrics measuring how vertex distances differ between two graphs. Formally, these distances are defined in terms of standard matrix norms on the difference of distance matrices under an optimal vertex alignment. The resulting metrics have natural interpretations, corresponding to three ways of measuring the distortion of shortest-path distances: the maximum distortion among all vertex pairs (entrywise maximum norm), global aggregation (entrywise $p$-norms), and local aggregation (operator $p$-norms) of distortions. For maximum distortion, we show that approximation below a factor of two is NP-hard even for highly restricted trees. Due to the close connection to the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, we obtain a similar hardness result for the latter. In both cases, we show essentially optimal additive inapproximability. On the algorithmic side, we give a subcubic-time algorithm for optimal embeddings of connected graphs into paths, based on a structural decomposition along a diametral path. Additionally, we give a simple approximation algorithm when one input graph has a "relatively path-like" metric structure, i.e. has bounded pathlength. For local and global distortion, we derive various hardness results even for restricted inputs. Making use of a close connection between the global distortion distances and Gromov-Wasserstein distances, we give the first formal proof of NP-hardness of the latter, which has been claimed in the literature many times but has, to the best of our knowledge, never been correctly proven.

papers.title: WeFair: Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in Short-Video Search
papers.abstract: Short-video search needs compact query rewriters that recover users' personalized intent from ambiguous queries under strict latency constraints. Existing LLM-based methods have improved rewriting by using synthetic reasoning and subsequent consumption-behavioral feedback. However, overemphasizing subsequent consumption can favor engaging content over the user's immediate need, causing intent drift even when rewritten queries are grounded in behavioral history. We propose WeFair, Fidelity-Aware Alignment from Human Feedback for Personalized Query Rewriting in WeChat short-video search. WeFair uses human feedback according to how directly it reflects personalized intent, assigning feedback fidelity to a progression from demonstration to preference to verification. We first mine actual queries and user reformulations from search sessions, and then screen them for contextual support. In the demonstration stage, a supervised fine-tuning curriculum progresses from large-scale context-to-query learning to reasoning and direct prediction on human reformulation and preservation. In the preference stage, direct preference optimization learns relative preferences from subsequent consumption feedback. In the verification stage, group relative policy optimization rewards exact agreement with reformulation or preservation targets to constrain intent drift. Further analysis shows that broad supervision benefits the full curriculum supervised training, while strict verification achieves better performance than auxiliary rewards. In offline experiments, WeFair-2B outperforms strong rewriting baselines in overall accuracy and intent preservation. An online A/B test shows relative increases of 2.593% in effective video-view rate and a 2.350% relative reduction in query reformulation rate. WeFair-2B has been deployed in the WeChat short-video search system, which serves over 100 million queries per day.

papers.title: Security and robustness analysis of encrypted communications for local home automation: ESPHome Native API and MQTT over TLS 1.3
papers.abstract: The expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) in residential and local automation environments has highlighted the limitations of considering the internal network as an inherently trusted domain. Man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacks, such as ARP spoofing, can allow traffic interception or manipulation when communications lack appropriate confidentiality, integrity, and authentication mechanisms. This paper presents a systematized review of the security mechanisms used by two communication alternatives between ESP-family microcontrollers and the Home Assistant platform: MQTT protected through TLS 1.3 and the ESPHome Native API, whose encryption is based on the Noise Protocol Framework using the Noise_NNpsk0_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256 pattern. The analysis considers four dimensions: cryptographic robustness, attack surface, implementation complexity, and resource consumption. The review identifies significant differences resulting from the architecture and cryptographic model of each alternative. TLS 1.3 provides a standardized framework compatible with public-key infrastructure and formal identity management, though it introduces greater configuration complexity and computational overhead during session establishment. The ESPHome Native API employs a more specialized scheme with lower operational complexity, eliminates dynamic algorithm negotiation, and uses ChaCha20-Poly1305. The resource-consumption analysis relies on measurements published by the projects and manufacturers themselves, not on an experimental test bench, and this limitation is explicitly acknowledged. The results identify the conditions under which each mechanism is appropriate for local home-automation architectures and provide a basis for designing IoT systems that balance security, interoperability, and resource constraints.

papers.title: Decision-Making in Digital Twins: Optimization, Control, and Learning
papers.abstract: A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical system, continuously updated with data from the physical system, enabling dynamic information exchange and decision-making. This bidirectional interaction, which distinguishes digital twins from conventional simulation models, introduces new challenges to simulation-based optimization, control, and learning. This paper reviews recent developments in decision-making methodologies motivated by digital twins. We focus on three interconnected areas: simulation optimization, sequential decision making, and risk-aware decision making. For simulation optimization, we discuss data-driven simulation optimization under input uncertainty, streaming input data, decision-dependent observations, and limited computational and data-collection resources. For sequential decision making, we review the connections among digital twins, stochastic optimal control, and reinforcement learning, with emphasis on Bayesian approaches that update models and policies as new information becomes available. For risk-aware decision making, we discuss distributionally robust and Bayesian risk formulations as alternative approaches for addressing model uncertainty. Throughout the paper, we emphasize the common problem of making decisions while the underlying model is being updated. We conclude by identifying research challenges and opportunities.

papers.title: Microscopic Modeling of Interlayer Tunneling in Twisted Bilayer Cuprates
papers.abstract: The field of twistronics, recently extended to twisted bilayer cuprate systems, has generated considerable interest due to the prediction of $d+id'$ states close to a $45^\circ$ twist, as suggested by multiple experimental probes. Theoretical studies of these systems using a variety of models and many-body theoretical techniques have revealed multiple competing order parameters. The large variability in experimental results and theoretical predictions demands an accurate microscopic model for these systems, in particular a more realistic description of the interlayer tunneling. In this study, we fit the in-plane hopping and compute the interlayer tunneling amplitudes by calculating the orbital overlap between $d_{x^2-y^2}$ wave functions at each site of the twisted square-lattice model. We observe sign-changing tunneling amplitudes, a strong twist-angle dependence of the direct tunneling term, and long-range tunneling amplitudes that often dominate over direct tunneling. We investigate the band structure, Fermi surfaces, and spectral functions in comparison with those obtained from the phenomenological model and find a substantial redistribution of spectral weight that modifies the competition between different superconducting ground states. We determine the phase diagram as a function of twist angle, filling, and direct tunneling strength, which is controlled by the $c$-axis distance between the monolayers, and observe a reduction in the region of time-reversal-symmetry-breaking (TRSB) $d+id'$ states compared with the phenomenological model. Finally, we investigate the Josephson critical current across the phase diagram and find strongly suppressed critical currents close to a $45^\circ$ twist, consistent with experimental observations.

papers.title: Microlocal Arthur packets as a quasi-canonical basis of stable distributions
papers.abstract: We show that microlocal Arthur packets can be reconstructed from an otherwise underdetermined system of linear equations arising from Kashiwara's local index theorem. The key is a geometric rigidity property of Arthur orbits which, together with Fourier symmetry, uniquely determines the microlocal multiplicities defining these packets. This realizes the associated Arthur distribution as the unique normalized element in the intersection of two filtered spaces of standard stable distributions related by Fourier transform. Under standard enhanced local Langlands hypotheses and Aubert compatibility, this gives an alternative representation-theoretic definition of microlocal Arthur packets for general connected reductive $p$-adic groups that does not use twisted endoscopy and ensures stability through the stability of tempered packet distributions. In the unipotent setting, we use this characterization to prove agreement between endoscopic and microlocal Arthur packets for split $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ when the residue characteristic is at least $6n+4$. We further use this characterization to compute all unipotent Arthur packets with unramified real infinitesimal character for inner-to-split adjoint exceptional $p$-adic groups. In this exceptional setting, we prove the microlocal weak Arthur packet conjecture and give counterexamples to the microlocal analogues of the least- and greatest-parameter conjectures.

papers.title: The quarter-point theorem for Gromov hyperbolic graphs
papers.abstract: Gromov hyperbolicity measures the geometric complexity of metric spaces and metric graphs through geodesic triangles and four-point conditions. While calculating the exact continuous hyperbolicity constant $δ^*(G)$ of a graph $G$ typically requires evaluating quadruples of points over an infinite metric continuum, discretizing this domain is a fundamental challenge in metric graph theory. In this paper, we study the continuous Gromov hyperbolicity constant via the Gromov product. Our main result, the Quarter-Point Theorem, establishes that the search space for quadruples $(x,y,z,w)$ attaining the exact hyperbolicity constant $δ^*(G)$ can be reduced from the entire metric graph to a finite or discrete subset $J'(G)$, comprising solely the vertices, edge midpoints, and quarter-points of $G$. This result holds for every graph, finite or infinite. This theoretical result provides a considerably simplified combinatorial framework for calculating hyperbolicity in complex networks and metric graphs. Furthermore, we exploit this discretization to significantly improve classical results by establishing and structural bounds relating the global hyperbolicity constant $δ^*(G)$ with its restrictions to vertices ($δ_V^*(G)$) and midpoints ($δ_J^*(G)$).

papers.title: Estimating Uncertainty of Omnimodal Large Language Models via External Omnimodal Embeddings
papers.abstract: Recent work has investigated Omni-modal Large Language Models (OLLMs), models which can take multiple modalities and their combinations as input, as a way forward to have systems really capable of interacting with their environment. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) for OLLMs, however, remains an open problem: existing methods largely target at most two modalities at a time, require access to model internals, or re-invocation of the evaluated model. We propose a model-agnostic UQ framework that scores a Chain-of-Thought response entirely through external omni-modal embeddings, measuring the grounding of the reasoning in the multimodal input and its internal coherence. Our contribution is the family of signals and an empirical characterisation of when it is reliable, rather than any single estimator: we find the geometric scores to be largely redundant with one another (mean within-split rank correlation 0.91-0.94) but strongly complementary to answer-dispersion baselines, and their reliability to depend on the generator and the modality. The resulting confidence estimates require no access to logits, hidden states or gradients of the evaluated model and no additional inference from it; they do require segmenting the reasoning trace with an auxiliary model and, for the aggregated score, a labelled calibration set that we show can be as small as 25 examples (although we also show that such a set buys little over fixing one signal a priori). On UNO-Bench, with both a closed and an open model, our scores yield small gains over self-consistency (systematic with the closed generator, mixed with the open one) and are competitive with self-verbalisation and internal-state baselines, especially in open-ended, omni-modal questions where previous state-of-the-art baselines struggle.

papers.title: Inferring Hidden Structural Changes from Node-State Responses under Partial Network Observations
papers.abstract: Online platforms often expose activity signals even when records of the underlying connections are incomplete or delayed. These activity responses may retain indirect evidence of connections that formed during the observation period but are absent from the recorded topology. Recovering such hidden structural changes can help keep network records aligned with evolving interactions and support downstream network analysis. However, the effects of a change propagate through the network and may overlap, making state changes difficult to associate with specific connections. We propose the Hierarchical Structural Context Ranker (HSCR), which combines visible network structure with node-state changes to infer connections that have formed but remain unrecorded. By jointly modeling the topological context of state responses and associations among potential connections, HSCR converts distributed activity changes into evidence for distinguishing potential connections without prespecified dynamical equations or parameters. Experiments on five temporal-network benchmarks and a real temporal Reddit network validate its effectiveness. Across observation spans and structural-record delays, true added connections achieve a 36%-50% reduction in mean true rank relative to the corresponding best baselines. This work provides a principled way to prioritize unrecorded additions for structural verification and record maintenance in online communities, information networks, and other networked systems.

papers.title: Beyond the Boundary: Optimal Grid Dispersion by Spread, Reverse, and Collect
